Parts of England are at risk of drought after record-breaking heatwaves have left a number of rivers and reservoirs “exceptionally low”.

The country has seen three consecutive heatwaves and the driest spring on record for England and Wales, with southern and eastern England having no rain at all this month.

Environment experts say the prolonged hot and dry conditions have dried up land, rivers, and streams, while demand for water has soared during the hottest days, warning that eight areas are now at risk of a drought.

Eight areas are at risk of drought, the National Drought Group warned ( Getty )

Prolonged dry weather – the stage immediately before drought – has been declared in East Anglia, the West Midlands, Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly, Lincolnshire, Northamptonshire, Hertfordshire, London, Wessex, Thames, the Solent and the South Downs.

The National Drought Group, whose members include the Met Office, government, regulators, water companies and farmers, warned only 13 per cent of rivers are currently at normal levels for this time of year. The majority are lower than normal, including the Rivers Avon (Hampshire), Cam, Derwent (Yorkshire), Swale, Tone, Wye and Yare, which are exceptionally low.

This means these eight areas are one stage away from official drought status.

Six reservoirs are also classed as “notably low” – including Wimbleball, Grafham and Hanningfield and The Lower Thames group, while Blagdon is “exceptionally low”.

On Tuesday, Thames Water announced a hosepipe ban for 10.1 million customers. Britain’s biggest water company said the restriction, also known as a temporary use ban (TUB), will come into effect at 12.01am on Thursday.

The ban applies to all customers that it supplies with drinking water across London, the Thames Valley and the Home Counties – but not to waste-only customers.

It means hosepipes should not be used for watering gardens, cleaning cars or windows, or filling paddling pools, hot tubs or swimming pools.

The company is the latest in a string of utilities to announce a temporary use ban in recent weeks.

On Monday, South East Water announced that a hosepipe ban in Kent will be extended to parts of Surrey, Sussex, Hampshire and Berkshire from Saturday.

Bans are also in place for Southern Water customers across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight and South West Water customers in parts of Devon and Lyme Regis in Dorset.

Customers of Cambridge Water, Affinity Water and Anglian Water, which supply areas in the East of England, have also introduced restrictions.

It comes as the National Farmers Union (NFU) warned coming 10 days are set to determine whether supermarkets will be hit by food shortages later in the year. Speaking to The Independent, Paul Tompkins, NFU deputy president, said: “Parts of the country, particularly in the east and south, have seen exceptionally low rainfall, creating real challenges for farm businesses.

“For many arable farmers, this could be another difficult and expensive harvest after extreme weather in both 2024 and 2025 which saw both drought and flood.”

Delicious Orie’s boxing lifecycle has moved swiftly, at times abruptly, and in a sense he is already back at the start.

His retirement from boxing was certainly abrupt last year, when the English heavyweight called time on his professional career after just one bout. Before that, Orie had emulated domestic and international greats by boxing at the Olympics after claiming Commonwealth gold. And now, in a new role, he is back at the Commonwealth Games.

Ahead of the 2026 Glasgow edition, the 28-year-old (who predominantly works in the financial sector) is speaking to the Independent as a pundit for TNT Sports.

“I very much love the sport and I still want to be involved in the sport,” he says. “It’s just I knew personally stepping in the ring was a different beast, a different animal that I didn’t really want to fight anymore.” He adds with a laugh: “Metaphorically speaking.”

“I was very much at peace with life as soon as I sort of announced it,” he continues. “It almost felt like a weight was lifted off my shoulders, I’ll be honest with you.” Then, however, Orie grapples with his words. “But I’m not... you know... one of the things that I really want to express is: I didn’t leave boxing because it was... because I don’t like the sport, or...”

He finally settles. “I’m very much still connected to the boxing world, but just from a different angle.”

So here he is, speaking (thoughtfully, as ever) for TNT, while spending time with England’s Commonwealth boxing squad. Given he’s in such familiar surroundings, I ask for the first thought that comes to mind when he hears the words “Commonwealth Games”.

"The first... I’ll say... feeling. The feeling is warmth, and it’s joy, it’s happiness,” he says. “If you were to ask me the week before the Games, I would have said nervous. I can’t swear on here, so I won’t say anything else!

“But yeah, very, very nervous, very anxious. It was the pressure, it was my first multi-sport event. Joe Joyce has won it, the likes of Frazer Clarke has got the gold, so for me it was like: right, the benchmark is set, it’s a gold medal. At the time, it was difficult to handle, but now looking back, it was genuinely the best experience I had in my journey as a boxer.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

open image in gallery Orie after winning Commonwealth boxing gold in 2022 ( Getty )

“When you feel an extreme amount of pressure, you know who you truly are. Your self-doubts really come out, but also that self-belief. You really know who you are in the core, very quick. It was sort of a fast track into knowing who I am. I didn’t need to go to a meditation retreat or anything, I just needed to go into the Commonwealth Games!

“Also outside the ring, the sense of unity between countries, learning so much about different nations that I didn’t even know existed, learning about their cultures – what makes them laugh, things of that nature. Being invited to different people’s homes from around the world. ‘If you’re ever in Mauritius, come down to my grandma’s house, she’ll feed you!’” He laughs again. “It’s an experience that I know will stay with me forever.”

Orie also opens up on the difference between the Commonwealth and Olympic Games, saying: “[The Commonwealth Games] was my first multi-sport event, so... I know it’s a little bit smaller than the Olympics, but it felt like this really grand feeling, and you get seen, a lot of coverage.

“Team GB and the Olympics has a great sense of family feeling, but it’s just that little extra element in the Commonwealth Games. For me of course, it was the home Games, it was literally in my hometown [of Birmingham], so it felt a little bit closer. In my local area it felt like, ‘We’re pushing together to get you a gold medal.’ But at the same time, it was on a spectacular stage. So, it was uniquely special. The Olympics, of course, is this grand pinnacle, but the Commonwealth Games is something that really stays close to the heart.”

open image in gallery CLICK TO ENLARGE: The England boxing squad for the 2026 Commonwealth Games ( englandboxing.org )

And Orie will stay close during these Games, where he expects Chantelle Reid, Isaac Okoh and Damar Thomas to impress, as England bring 14 boxers to Glasgow.

“Chantelle has got the experience,” he says. “I’ve been on camp with her in the lead-up of the Paris Games, because she came in a little bit later in that cycle, so she developed very, very fast. She was very experienced anyway beforehand, but adapting to that international way of fighting and consistently being in camps is a big ask, and she did it so well. I believe she was hard done by in the Olympic Games, and she’s coming in with that fire.

“Of course, I’m going to mention the big boys: the likes of Isaac, who is in the 90 kilos, and then Damar, who’s 90-plus kilos. You’ve got the heavyweight and the super heavyweight, absolutely amazing fighters – technically sound and also very awkward. They both helped me massively towards my Olympic journey; they were both on the same camps as me, all the way in Sheffield through to Paris.

“I know they would’ve soaked up so much experience. That’s what Team GB are so good at: supporting that next gen coming up. I was the same when I was a sparring partner for Frazer in Tokyo. Dip your toe in the water, you don’t have to risk anything. But when it’s your time: ‘Oh, yeah, I’ve been here before. I know what it’s like.’”

Orie has been here before, but now it is time for a new generation.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

News.title: How to have the perfect holiday in France’s gastronomic capital
News.content:
Calling all bon vivants. This is your city. Within seconds of tucking into a traditional andouillette (tripe sausage) or modern vegetarian cuisine in a jam-packed bistro, admiring fine art in a Renaissance abbey, or getting delightfully lost in a traboule (secret passageway) used by 19th-century silk weavers, you’ll quickly realise that Lyon is a city that knows how to live well.

Enthralling, cinematic and richly storied, after living here for 10 years, I still find myself being surprised by a walled garden I never knew, a fresque (wall mural) suddenly popping up on a riverfront wall, a new museum or river boat route.

Street-smart Romans first spotted the city’s extraordinary topography, founding Lugdunum (Lyon’s predecessor) in 43BC on the sunny slopes of Fourvière. And to this day, this basilica-crowned hill above Lyon’s quaint Unesco-listed Old Town (Vieux Lyon) is the perfect perch for clocking the mighty Rhône and Saône rivers that wend their way so gracefully through the centre.

The city’s quays, landscaped with peaceful water gardens and floating bars, buzz night and day – while culture lovers can explore a bounty of museums. Then there’s the gastronomy: among France’s finest, thanks to the unfaltering creativity and sass of city chefs, both past and present.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan outraged by Morgan Rogers claim upon signing for Chelsea in British record £117million transfer
Sports.content:
PIERS MORGAN has emphatically hit back at Morgan Rogers’ claims that Chelsea are the biggest club in London after he completed his £117 million move.

After making the move from Aston Villa on Tuesday, Rogers said: “I’m so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I’ve always admired since I was a kid.”



Arsenal were thought to be the frontrunners for his signature this summer until Chelsea swiftly concluded a deal.

His comments come after Arsenal just lifted their first Premier League title in 22 years and they reached the Champions League final.



Chelsea finished 10th last season after working their way through three different managers.

Morgan, always keen to share his opinion, hit back at Rogers’ claims on X.

He tweeted: “They’re not even the biggest in West London… Brentford finished higher in the League last season.”

Morgan is not wrong – Brentford did finish ninth last season.

However, The Bees do not have multiple league and European titles, either.

Rogers’ comments are interesting, though. Arsenal are on top right now and have become a real force on the continent for the past couple of years, but what makes a club the biggest?



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Following West Ham‘s relegation, London boasts six clubs from the capital in the Premier League next season: Arsenal, Brentford, Chelsea, Crystal Palace, Fulham and Tottenham.

Due to league titles and domestic cup wins – certainly in the Premier League era – Arsenal and Chelsea immediately jump off the page as the London heavyweights.

So how do they compare?

In terms of major honours, Arsenal are slightly ahead of Chelsea domestically, but many fans would point to the fact that the Blues have two Champions League trophies in their cabinet – and two Club World Cup triumphs – to the Gunners’ zero.



Nobody has won the FA Cup more than Arsenal and they have eight more league titles than Chelsea for a total of 32 honours to Chelsea’s 28.

Chelsea have also spent far, far more money than Arsenal, especially since BlueCo came into power at Stamford Bridge.

They have a net spend of around £745m over the past five years and even Tottenham (£691m) have spent more than Arsenal’s £545m.

But, that doesn’t always equate to value. According to transfermarkt, Mikel Arteta‘s men are worth around £43m more.



Who has the biggest fanbase? It’s not all about having fans in London, of course (Man United probably have the most there!).

The Global Wealth Index estimates that Chelsea has around 202 million fans worldwide, some 24 million more than what Arsenal are purported to have.

Then you’ve got their stadiums. Arsenal moved out of Highbury back in 2007 and headed towards the Emirates Stadium, a state-of-the-art ground with over 60,000 capacity.

Stamford Bridge, although it has undergone several renovations over the years, holds just over 40,000. Arsenal may win that battle, but Chelsea continue to explore options of either improving Stamford Bridge or building a new stadium in the Earls Court area.



It’s understood Arsenal are also trying to expand their home.

It swings in roundabouts. At the turn of the millennium, Arsenal won a league and FA Cup double and then became the Invincibles two years later. No club can say they have done that in or outside London.

But, between that historic feat in 2004 and winning the title last year, Chelsea won the league FIVE times and the Champions League twice.

Sports.title: Sky Sports News host reveals horror of second, incorrect cancer diagnosis three years on from being given all-clear
Sports.content:
'WORLD CRUMBLED' Sky Sports News host reveals horror of second, incorrect cancer diagnosis three years on from being given all-clear

SKY SPORTS NEWS presenter Jo Wilson has revealed how she received an incorrect cancer diagnosis three years after being given the all-clear.

Wilson joined Sky as a trainee in 2011 before making her presenting debut in 2015.



In 2022, she was diagnosed with stage three cervical cancer and underwent radiotherapy and chemotherapy to save her life.

She returned to TV screens later that year before announcing she had beaten the cancer in 2023.



However, in a brave Instagram post, she has now opened up about her struggles after receiving a cancer diagnosis earlier in February, which thankfully turned out to be a false alarm.

The 41-year-old’s candid post read: “In February, after my three-year scan, I was told my cancer had returned in a lymph node. I couldn’t believe it – it felt like my whole world had crumbled all over again.



“But after being referred to the high-dose radiotherapy team, one consultant questioned whether the diagnosis was actually correct.

“What followed were five months of tests, scans, waiting and uncertainty before, last week, I finally got the news I’d been desperately hoping for: it wasn’t cancer after all.

“The lymph node is now thought to be a benign neuroma – a cluster of nerves that was likely inflamed at the time of my original scan.

“The relief was indescribable, but so too is the emotional toll from the last five months, believing – then not knowing if my cancer had returned. Living with that uncertainty was incredibly hard.



“On the outside, life carried on – I worked, was being a mum, played (lots of) padel, spent time with friends and family, and smiled for photos.

“But underneath it all, I was carrying something very heavy, and there were times I found myself in some very dark places.”

Wilson, who produced a documentary, “Football, Cancer and Me” that was released in November 2025, said she was sharing her story because she did not believe those who felt the sting of cancer were ever truly “free”.



She continued: ” The fear of recurrence can stay with you long after treatment ends, and I think it’s important we talk about that reality.

How to protect yourself against cervical cancer CERVICAL cancer is most commonly diagnosed in women in their early 30s, with around 3,200 new cases and 850 deaths each year in the UK. According to CRUK, the five-year survival rate is around 70 per cent – and the earlier it is caught, the better. Cervical screening programmes and HPV vaccines have reduced rates and save 4,000 lives each year. It is vital you attend your smear test and get jabbed when invited, and that you know the symptoms of cervical cancer to look out for. These aren’t always obvious, and they may not become noticeable until the cancer has reached an advanced stage. But you might notice: Unusual bleeding (often after sex, between periods, or after the menopause)

Pain and discomfort during sex

Vaginal discharge (often unpleasant smelling)

Pain in your lower back, between your hip bones or in your lower tummy Women are invited to have regular cervical screenings between the ages of 25 and 64. How often depends on your age. The HPV vaccine, which helps protect against the virus, is recommended for children aged 12 to 13 and people at higher risk from HPV. Source: NHS and Cancer Research UK

“If you’re someone living beyond a cancer diagnosis, please know you’re not alone.”

The Scottish presenter issued a plea for people to be kind to one another, adding that social media never showed the full picture of what someone was going through.

Her story and message received support from a number of Sky colleagues, including Emma Paton, Hayley McQueen, Izzy Christiansen and Emma Saunders, who is herself a cancer survivor.

Wilson lives in the Cotswolds with her long-term partner, Dan McGrath, and their daughter, whom she gave birth to in September 2020.

The couple married in 2022 after bringing forward their wedding plans when Wilson received her original cancer diagnosis.

Before moving into media, St Johnstone fan Wilson was a sprinter and jumper who represented Perth.

Sports.title: USA could host another World Cup as soon as 2038… despite England not hosting for over SIXTY YEARS
Sports.content:
THE USA could host the World Cup in 2038 despite the 2026 tournament only just wrapping up in the nation.

Spain took the glory in a dreary final hosted at New York’s MetLife Stadium last weekend.



But while the European nation celebrates, attention elsewhere has turned to the future of the competition.

The locations for the 2030 and 2034 editions have already been selected, but there are growing feelings that the US are emerging as favourites for the 2038 event.



No nation has ever held the event twice in a 12-year span.

But the locations of the intervening tournaments have left the US with an almost clear path to host the tournament.

READ MORE ON THE WORLD CUP NO STONE UNTURNED John Stones set for Premier League return as giants plot free transfer



A confederation can generally host a tournament provided it has not played host in the past two editions of the World Cup due to Fifa‘s rotation policy – though this is not a hard and fast rule.

Spain, Portugal and Morocco are all set to share co-hosting duties for the 2030 edition.

But that is further complicated by the fact that Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will all host one match each in 2030, in honour of the tournament’s centenary, 100 years on from its inaugural event in Uruguay.

That could leave Uefa (Europe), CAF (Africa) and CONMEBOL (South America) out of the running for the next two cycles.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

That tournament already left options for the 2034 event thin, with only the Asian and Oceanian federations in contention, before Australia‘s withdrawal handed the event to Saudi Arabia unopposed.

Only Concacaf – which includes the USA, Canada, Mexico and other Central American nations – and Asia’s AFC as potential suitors for the 2038 competitions.

And it is clear where the money would be for Fifa after its record-breaking revenues this year from ticketing and hospitality.

The US also seems keen to bring the tournament, even if Concacaf is apprehensive about allowing the nation to host on its own.



Donald Trump himself was clear about his hopes to see the game’s biggest competition return to American shores in the near future.

He told Fox ahead of the 2026 final: “Based on the numbers we will be requesting it immediately.

“We have to do this again, and we have to do this again while I am around, hear that Gianni [Infantino]?”

Trump and Infantino have gotten along swimmingly this tournament, and at times have appeared so close personally that it has caused several controversies, so it is not hard to imagine Fifa being friendly to the idea of a reunion.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

By comparison, England – consistently one of the top-ranked teams on the planet – have not hosted the tournament since their triumph in 1966, 60 years ago.

The nation has been encouraged to pursue the prospect of hosting in the near future, but if the US does seal the deal for 2038, it would have held it three times in the past 44 years.

Sports.title: Fan group launch stinging attack on Fifa over ‘World Cup that failed supporters’ with ‘serious concerns’ over next hosts
Sports.content:
A FOOTBALL fan group has slammed Fifa for the 2026 World Cup and are already worried about what’s to come in 2030.

Football Supporters Europe have taken aim at Fifa president Gianni Infantino, US president Donald Trump and Fifa as a whole in a statement.



It reads: “The 2026 World Cup should have been a celebration of the game and the supporters who give it life.

“Instead, it has too often become a case study in what is so deeply wrong with football today.”



Infantino has been widely criticised for allowing the tournament to become “Americanised” with the World Cup final half-time show on top of hydration breaks every quarter that turned into advertising opportunities.

Football’s chief has also come under fire for racking up an extraordinary number of air miles during the tournament that directly contradicts Fifa’s climate strategy.

The fan group released a statement chronicling all of the grave errors Fifa oversaw.

It read: “The controversy around this World Cup of FIFA’s making has ranged from its bogus ‘Peace Prize’ to appease Donald Trump to the bending of its own rules to breaking point.

“They changed the game’s identity beyond recognition with government interference in playing matters.

“The quartering of matches with advert breaks masquerading as hydration breaks and the abandonment of a 15-minute half-time for a pop concert, Iran being barred entry into the US on non-match days, and the Balogun scandal being clearly visible low points.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“FIFA walks away from this World Cup with its reputation with supporters totally shattered having opened a void for distrust.”

The next World Cup will take place across six nations and three continents for the first time ever.

Speaking from a European perspective, the FSE insists Spain and Portugal will present more problems for Fifa.

It said: “For FSE and its members, the focus now turns to all six co-hosts of the 2030 FIFA World Cup (Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay).



“From day one, the tournament must be planned with match-going supporters in mind. As a European organisation, we are acutely aware of the serious concerns for safety, security, and service standards at football matches in Spain and Portugal.

“Supporters regularly report disproportionate policing, police violence, invasive body searches, poor communication, and inadequate supporter services. Too often, supporters are treated as risks to manage rather than guests to welcome.

“If Spain and Portugal want to be successful World Cup co-hosts, these issues, as well as those from this summer’s World Cup, must be addressed.

“These two countries are far behind the current European standards on fan dialogue and must adopt modern policies to bridge the gap.

“Supporters from across the world will rightly expect safe, accessible, welcoming, and well-organised matchday experiences, and those standards are non-negotiable.”

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump, President of the United States have formed a close friendship. (Image: (Photo by Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images))

Donald Trump has reportedly given FIFA President Gianni Infantino his backing to become the next United Nations Secretary-General after growing close during their collaboration on delivering the 2026 World Cup. The pair have been thrust into the global spotlight, and the president of the United States is now championing Infantino for the role.

‌

Trump reportedly views Infantino as a unifying figure with worldwide credibility following years of engagement with football leagues, World Cup national associations, and major sponsors.

Trump reportedly believes Infantino would be perfectly suited to the role, according to the New York Post. This comes after a lip reader disclosed Infantino's appeal to Trump that he brushed aside at the World Cup final, and a body language expert identified the motive behind his 'purposeful' stunt.

Trump's backing for Infantino intensified after the 2026 World Cup concluded, following numerous appearances together during the tournament's closing stages. Infantino could yet pursue a fourth term as FIFA President when his present mandate expires in 2027.

"The World Cup turned out to be a spectacular SUCCESS!" Trump posted on Truth Social after Spain defeated Argentina in the final. He expressed gratitude to law enforcement and others who contributed, and offered particular commendation to Andrew Giuliani and Infantino.

"Few people will ever be able to accomplish what he has done in elevating the World Cup to a level that nobody thought was possible."

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino and U.S. President Donald Trump show off the World Cup winner's medals (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Trump was spotted alongside Infantino following England's semi-final defeat to Argentina and once more during Spain's trophy and medal ceremony.

However, the US President cannot simply hand Infantino the Secretary-General role. According to Article 97 of the UN Charter, the Secretary-General is chosen by the General Assembly following a recommendation from the Security Council.

A member state must first put forward a candidate, who then faces public scrutiny and Security Council straw polls before any formal recommendation can be made.

The primary obstacle is securing a minimum of nine Security Council votes while avoiding a veto from any of the five permanent members: the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, or China.

Trump can lobby and attempt to wield his influence should he pursue this avenue following the New York Post report.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola confirms Liverpool transfer priority - 'Not the ideal situation'
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola confirms Liverpool transfer priority - 'Not the ideal situation'

Liverpool have added Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz to their squad but Andoni Iraola has made it clear that the club still need to add another winger before the new season

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola wants a new winger (Image: Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu)

Andoni Iraola has stressed the need for Liverpool to sign a new winger ahead of the new Premier League season following the departure of Mohamed Salah.

‌



The Reds' talisman confirmed back in March that he would leave Anfield a year early and is seemingly poised to complete a move to the Turkish outfit, Besiktas.

‌



While Liverpool have added Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, a winger by trade, they are yet to commit to a deal for a senior replacement to Salah, who plundered 257 goals across his nine-year stay on Merseyside.

‌



Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain has been heavily linked with Liverpool in recent weeks, while the club made inroads into a deal for the impressive Yan Diomande earlier in the summer, only for PSG to emerge as the attacker's preferred destination.

Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits READ MORE :

Iraola has confirmed Liverpool's search for another winger is ongoing, pointing out that wide attack is one area that definitely needs strengthening.

"I think it is difficult to say a number [on how many incomings]. When the market is open, you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad," Iraola said from Liverpool's pre-season tour of the United States.

‌



"There are obvious situations where we need to sign players. Winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyze what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have.

"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust, but it is still not the ideal situation, so it will depend on a lot of things."

View 2 Images Liverpool have been linked heavily with PSG's Bradley Barcola (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



While Diomande's preference is a move to PSG, progress on a deal to take the Ivory Coast star to Paris has been slow.

If Diomande does swap RB Leipzig for PSG, the move could open the door for Barcola to leave. He is admired by both the Reds and Arsenal, who also want to level up their left attacking options.

The Premier League champions have been forced back into the market after failing to sign their priority transfer target, Morgan Rogers, who completed a £117million move to Chelsea on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Liverpool investment explained as Jeff Bezos talks revealed after FSG statement released
Sports.content:
Liverpool investment explained as Jeff Bezos talks revealed after FSG statement released

Billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is said to have been approached and entered talks to take over Premier League giants Liverpool

View 2 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has been approached to join the consortium in talks to buy a stake in Liverpool FC. The billionaire, with an estimated net worth of $259billion (£193bn), has held discussions about joining a syndicate of investors led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia.

‌



The Reds' current owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), have confirmed that a group has approached them to buy a stake in the club, managed by Bhatia. It is understood that the negotiations are viewed as similar to the agreement with Dynasty Equity in 2023, which made a strategic minority investment in Liverpool worth between £82m and £164m.

‌



Andoni Iraola faces an important summer with the two-time Premier League champions intent on righting the wrongs of their poor title defence last season.

‌



News of investment talks come during an uncertain period of time for the football club due to the upheaval at senior level with Michael Edwards, FSG's CEO of Football, leaving the club while Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes has been strongly linked with a move to Saudi Arabia.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos 'approached' as FSG enter talks over Liverpool investment READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical READ MORE :

Jeff Bezos approach

Bhatia, the son-in-law of billionaire steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal, is said to have held discussions with the Amazon founder, according to Sky News. However, a source reportedly cautioned that he was not certain that Bezos would proceed with an investment in the Premier League club.

Bezos is among the richest in the world with Forbes magazine estimating his $257bn wealth pits him as the fourth-richest man in the world. The 62-year-old has previously explored bids in sport, namely in the NFL with the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders but didn't proceed with either deal.

‌



There has been an influx of American involvement in the Premier League with half of the 20 teams owned predominantly by US-based investors. Talks between Bhatia's consortium and FSG are ongoing. FSG, which also owns Major League Baseball giants Boston Red Sox, have been the custodian of Liverpool since 2010 after saving the club from administration under American owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

FSG statement

Sky News have reported Bhatia's consortium could acquire as much as 30% of the football club. The British-Indian's decision to step away from QPR paves way for him to acquire a stake at Liverpool.

‌



The Reds' owners have been open to new investment, whether it be a minority shareholding or a full sale, since 2022, with Dynasty Equity's investment, a 4% stake, a year later. In a statement, FSG confirmed talks with an investment consortium led by the entrepreneur.

It said: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

View 2 Images Liverpool and FSG owner John W. Henry celebrates after their Premier League title win in 2025 (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images/Getty Images For The Premier League)

‌



A change in tact from FSG

Edwards' appointment as the ownership group's CEO of Football marked a move towards multi-club ownership, a model adopted by Manchester City and Chelsea. Both of Liverpool's Premier League rivals have utilised it, which has seen them use feeder clubs to sell, sign and develop players under a broader umbrella.

BBC Sport have reported that FSG have come away from the idea of investing in other football clubs. The Athletic previously reported that proposals were made over acquiring Bordeaux, Malaga, Getafe among others but UEFA's tightening of the restrictions made it complicated as well as concerns from higher-ups about the ability to grow new clubs' revenue streams, with Edwards later departing his role.

The Telegraph has reported that sources have stressed that no deal has been completed and any possible move is not a sign of FSG looking to step away from its interest in Liverpool.

Article continues below

The investment news illustrates the lucrative interest in England's top-flight and the level of finances required to continue competing at the top level across the country and Europe. It has been seven years since Liverpool won the Champions League. They lost the final in 2022 to Real Madrid, and face falling behind their rivals with Paris Saint-Germain threatening to dominate the competition with back-to-back titles.

Sports.title: Kai Rooney's younger brother, 8, lands first job as Coleen's pay soars above Wayne's
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney's younger brother, 8, lands first job as Coleen's pay soars above Wayne's

Coleen Rooney has gained a lucrative new deal that has overshadowed Wayne Rooney's with the BBC

View 2 Images Coleen poses alongside her son Cass, 8, for Primark's upcoming collections (Image: Charlotte Hadden for Primark)

The youngest son of Wayne and Coleen Rooney has begun a new career in modelling. Eight-year-old Cass, who is the younger brother of Manchester United star Kai, made his debut in front of the cameras alongside his mum to show off her clothing range for Primark.

‌



Coleen's shift into fashion has seen her become the family's biggest earner, according to reports. The 40-year-old is said to have pocketed more than the figure her husband received last year to join Match of the Day as a pundit, with the ex-footballer's BBC salarary for 2025/26 not meeting the £178,000 per year disclosure threshold when the broadcaster released its accounts earlier in July.

‌



In February, The Sun claimed that the former I'm a Celebrity star had signed a lucrative seven-figure deal with Primark last year. Coleen, who has four sons with ex-United star Wayne, said: “Having Cass as part of the kidswear photoshoot was special.”

‌



A source told The Sun at the time: “Coleen is so proud to be a working mum and she wanted to keep things affordable for her fans. She didn’t just sign for the cash, it was because she felt aligned with Primark’s values.

“Coleen is super proud with the clothes she’s worked on with Primark. It’s got a real athleisure feel. Primark thinks it will fly off the shelves.”

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



David Beckham's huge payment for World Cup appearance blows away Shakira and Justin Bieber READ MORE :

Man Utd may have to change plans for two players after Marcus Rashford return READ MORE :

Another insider told the newspaper: “Coleen is a perfectionist and throws herself into every project she gets involved in. With Primark, she worked so closely with them on the entire collection. It’s made for working mums just like her — the range is stylish yet practical.”

Coleen has had deals with George at Asda and Littlewoods, but it looks like she has out-earned Wayne with her latest contract. Meanwhile, young striker Kai recently celebrated reaching a new milestone.

View 2 Images Kai Rooney has signed a scholarship with Manchester United

‌



The 16-year-old signed a scholarship deal with United and subsequently took to social media, declaring: “Work starts now.” Kai has been part of United's youth ranks since the age of 11.

His deal marks a huge moment in his young career. A scholarship allows youngsters to continue studying while pursuing a career in football, and to sign a professional contract when they turn 17.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits

Andoni Iraola has been tasked with leading Liverpool back to the top, but two men in his squad who both know how to win a Premier League title have been tipped to leave Anfield

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola laid out his stance (Image: Jacek Boczarski/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has made it clear that he wants to keep both Alexis Mac Allister and Alisson Becker at the club. Both players have been linked with moves away, with Liverpool having already said goodbye to two senior players in Mo Salah and Andy Robertson, compounding a summer of change at Anfield.

‌



Iraola was appointed to replace Arne Slot and inherits a squad who this time last year had just lifted the Premier League title. But both Mac Allister and Alisson had indifferent seasons, with the latter suffering frequent injuries.

‌



Alisson, 33, was heavily linked with a move to Juventus earlier this summer but was tempted by their offer of a long-term contract. Meanwhile, Mac Allister only has two years left on his deal at Liverpool and has been linked with a sensational move to rivals Manchester United as well as Real Madrid.

‌



But at a press conference in Chicago, as Liverpool prepare to start their pre-season tour of the United States, Iraola laid out his stance. "I think Alexis has been one of the best players at the club for the last few years, and he has had a very good World Cup, so it is normal that other clubs want our best players," the Reds boss explained.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos 'approached' as FSG enter talks over Liverpool investment READ MORE :

FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation READ MORE :

"It always happens in other markets. But I want to keep my good players. I'm looking forward more to signing new players rather than losing the ones we have here."

‌



Regarding Alisson's future, Iraola said: "I'm very happy with the situation we have right now in the goalkeeping area. Alisson is someone also in a changing room that has lost some references in terms of experience.

"I think he's someone that definitely will help us in this process of adaptation of the new signings, of the new players, the young players. We need the references like Virgil [van Dijk], like Alisson, like Joe Gomez, players that have been here for a long time."

Should Liverpool sell Alexis Mac Allister and Alisson Becker? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Alisson Becker and Alexis Mac Allister's futures have been the subject of speculation (Image: Daniel Derajinski/Icon Sport)

As for who Liverpool are looking to bring in, the Spaniard admitted that his side are 'very thin' in defence. "With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now, so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes," Iraola added.

Liverpool begin their pre-season tour by facing Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday before taking on Wrexham and Leeds United in New York City and Chicago respectively next week. They'll also welcome Monaco and Como to Anfield next month.

Sports.title: Lingfield and Worcester host competitive Wednesday cards
Sports.content:
Worcester and Lingfield are the venues for today's racing, with National Hunt and Flat action on the agenda.

8.10 Lingfield - Hilltop, Kaori and Mojito contest trappy affair

Hilltop, Kaori and Mojito contest a trappy-looking Download The At The Races App Fillies' Handicap at Lingfield.

Top weight Hilltop is a consistent performer who ran another solid race when third over this course and distance in May and should give another bold bid off the same mark.

George Boughey's Kaori is a lightly raced type who is yet to win in five starts. She wasn't beaten far when third at Yarmouth and drops back to seven furlongs with the hope of more to offer under Billy Loughnane.

Mojito ran out an impressive winner on her penultimate run at Doncaster before disappointing when favourite at Salisbury and has a bit to prove here.

2.25 Worcester - Red-hot Regal Renaissance seeks a four-timer

Regal Renaissance seeks a fourth success on the bounce as she takes on eight rivals in this Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase at Worcester.

Jack Jones' in-form mare landed her final start for trainer Henry Daly in May and has two wins from two starts for her new connections. She stayed on strongly when outpointing Fringill Dike at Market Rasen and this looks a good opportunity to follow up despite a 2lb rise.

Harry Hope looks a danger for the Ben Pauling and Jones combination. He has an excellent strike-rate over fences and should strip fitter for his last outing at Stratford.

Axel Bleue scored over this track and trip 21 days ago and remains unexposed over fences.

4.00 Worcester - Last-time winners Media Mogul and Playful Fox clash

Last-time winners Media Mogul and Playful Fox clash in a competitive Dolphin Tec Handicap Hurdle at 4pm.

Media Mogul recorded a first hurdling success when challenging late over this course and distance last month and makes appeal as he heads into handicaps off a mark 105.

Playful Fox represents the powerful Skelton team and is another who arrives on the back of a victory at Stratford. That was his debut win over hurdles, and he looks well-suited to this two-mile distance.

Others to note include Jamie Snowden's Kernie d'Airy, who got off the mark at the third attempt over jumps here last month and is another who makes his handicap debut. Ez Tiger ran well in second over this course and distance last month and goes again today, with Bryan Carver retaining the ride.

Best of the rest

Back at Lingfield, Emma's Letter will be fancied to give Ed Dunlop and Billy Loughnane a positive start to proceedings in the attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (6.10pm). This three-year-old daughter of Saxon Warrior has only been nudged up 3lbs for success at Nottingham the last day and with only three rivals to beat, she could go in again.

An hour later, Dreamlover represents Richard Spencer and Phil Cunningham in the Follow @attheraces On X Nursery Handicap. Connections will be hoping a return to five furlongs will pay dividends for this gelding, who drops significantly down in class for this assignment. Romidijo found just one too good at Chepstow the last day and could also relish the drop in distance.

The 7.40pm Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Novice Stakes sees the 89-rated Asuka take on Coilltedudeisback and Yazoo. George Boughey's charge is likely to go off a very short price in the colours of the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid.

Sports.title: Kelly promises to let loose in 'spiteful' takedown of Agyarko
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly has promised that his IBF light-middleweight title defence against Caoimhin Agyarko will be "spiteful" ahead of their Saudi Arabia showdown on Saturday.

The fight forms part of the undercard of Anthony Joshua's return to the ring against Kristian Prenga at the Jeddah Superdome.

Sunderland's Kelly won the belt in January against Bakhram Murtazaliev, and told Sky Sports that being champion has given him added belief going into the bout against Agyarko of Belfast.

Image: Josh Kelly celebrates defeating Bakhram Murtazaliev to claim the IBF light-middleweight title

"The thing it has done for me inside is worth its weight in gold," Kelly said of his win over Murtazaliev.

"It's a weird one because, in training and everything, everyone is saying I just look different. These are the closest people to me, watching me go to work every day.

"It's a crazy experience. You don't know what something like this does for you, spiritually, energetically, motivation-wise, everything.

"It's actually taken a lot of expectation off. It's like I can now just let loose, let the reins go and just enjoy everything.

"It's knowing and believing. First, you have to believe, but when you complete the task, you know."

Initially, Agyarko was scheduled to face Brandon Adams in a final eliminator in April, but the American collapsed prior to the weigh-in and was unable to fight.

Rather than the IBF ordering another final eliminator between Agyarko and Murtazaliev, Kelly was given the option of a voluntary first defence, and a deal was struck to face Agyarko.

"We know each other, but he's just another opponent, basically," Kelly said of Agyarko.

"He's just another guy I've got to deal with, a stepping stone in this journey to creating more history. It's not about him, it's about me."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caoimhin Agyarko says Josh Kelly’s 'mentality and ego' will be his downfall in their IBF super-welterweight clash this Saturday.

Agyarko's last outing was a split-decision victory over Ishmael Davis in December, while Kelly has put eight wins together, including the title victory over Murtazaliev, since his sole career loss to David Avanesyan in 2021.

"There's no complacency," Kelly promised. "No other fight exists except this one.

"I've never overlooked anyone in my career. In fact, I end up overestimating every opponent - I build them up to be the fastest, hardest-hitting guys.

"I'm looking to do bigger and better things in the sport, and this is now a dangerous time to face me because I've got literally nothing to lose.

"I'm just going to go in there and enjoy it, put an absolute spectacle on.

"It's going to be fun. It's going to be spiteful."

Sports.title: Red Bull getting calls from 'good drivers' over future seat - Mekies
Sports.content:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies has suggested they are getting calls from "good drivers" about potential future seats at the team but believes they will make the further pace improvements required to ensure Max Verstappen stays.

As Formula 1 prepares for its final race before the summer break in Hungary this weekend, Verstappen's Red Bull future beyond this season remains uncertain.

His contract runs to the end of the 2028 season but contains performance clauses that would allow him to leave at the end of this year. He is thought to have until October to inform the team should he wish to activate a break in the deal.

It emerged last month that the Dutchman's representatives had spoken with McLaren, although the latter's Zak Brown has subsequently made clear that "I've got my two drivers" in Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Mercedes and Ferrari's drivers are also under contract, seemingly limiting Verstappen's short-term options beyond Red Bull, should he first choose to stay in F1, into 2027.

With it considered normal that Verstappen's representatives would be keeping abreast of potential options for their driver elsewhere, Mekies was asked by Sky Sports F1 at the Belgian Grand Prix whether his team, in turn, had also received enquiries from drivers elsewhere on the grid.

"It's working in both directions," replied Mekies. "It's completely natural and I think that's what you guys were reporting before.

"It's completely natural Max gets called from everyone because he's the best driver in the world and, equally, if you are a top team, you are going to get calls from many of these good drivers around as well. That's natural.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the Belgian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen gave blunt responses to questions about his future at Red Bull.

"Is it a distraction for us? Not really. The full focus is to get that car as fast as it can, then you will keep your best driver in the world and we also see there's a massive growth of Isack [Hadjar] alongside Max.

"That for us is the ideal pairing and we try to make sure we can keep that pairing."

Mekies is confident Red Bull will deliver on their ongoing quest to close its remaining gap to the front of the field after steps forward since the start of the season in F1's new era of regulations.

Since a big upgrade of the RB22 three races ago at the Austrian Grand Prix, Verstappen has finished on the podium in two of the last three races, although endured a difficult Silverstone where he spun out late on due to a rear-wing fault.

Isack Hadjar finished sixth from 21st on the grid last weekend in Belgium to extend his run of top-six finishes to six races.

"All we need to do is to continue to progress with the car," said Mekies.

"We started the season a bit more than one second off the pace and I don't think we should be surprised at that.

"I think it's a product of how late the title push was last year - a product of how late the title push was last year, a product of the incredible challenge of the new power unit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After finishing third in Belgium, Max Verstappen has disputed the FIA rating Red Bull's engine as the benchmark in Formula One.

"We started on the back foot but these guys did it again. We were more than a second away and we are now talking about the last two or three tenths for ultimate pace.

"When you are one second away, the drivers are going to be frustrated, Max is going to be frustrated. And we know it's not the position we want to stay.

"To your point, the best way to close the subject is to go and get these last two or three tenths and that's what everyone is focused on."

Red Bull have seen the departure of a number of key figures associated with their past title-winning successes over the last two years, while Verstappen's own race engineer and key ally, Gianpiero Lambiase, is heading to McLaren no later than 2028.

Asked how that sense of 'transition' at the team marries with attempts to keep Verstappen, Mekies said: "It's more simple than what it seems, because ultimately it's only about speed.

"Red Bull and Red Bull Racing only have one objective, it's to win, and it's the same objective that Max has.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix.

"So, it's not about, how can we prove to him that we can win. We are here to win anyhow.

"It's the same group of people that have done the incredible turnaround last year, that was a few months ago. It's the same group of people that, despite that late push, has managed to absorb nearly one second off our competitors, and they were not waiting for us in these first races.

"Now we are in the hardcore part of it, the last few tenths, the most difficult ones to get, but what we need to do is continue to work as a united group, and that's how we'll produce the best results."

Sports.title: 'Frustrated' Newcastle will demand £80m for Arsenal target Guimaraes
Sports.content:
Newcastle are frustrated with Arsenal's pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes and will only consider selling him for upwards of £80m, according to Sky Sports News' North East reporter Keith Downie.

The Brazil international has told his club he wants to join Arsenal this summer but Downie says that, contrary to recent reports, the Gunners still haven't made contact with Newcastle directly.

Arsenal have instead explored the conditions of a deal through intermediaries, an approach which has left Newcastle frustrated as they try to gauge whether their interest is genuine.

Downie expects the saga to continue but insists Newcastle are determined to keep their captain and value him at over £80m, only £20m less than his former team-mate Sandro Tonali, who they sold to Spurs for £100m earlier this month.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Bruno Guimaraes' best goals for Newcastle in the Premier League

"The stories regarding Bruno Guimaraes are not going to go away," Downie said on Sky Sports News.

"The main reason for that is that he has told Newcastle he would like to explore a move away from the club, and a move to Arsenal in particular.

"He is ambitious. He wants to win trophies. He doesn't want to end his career having only won the Carabao Cup and potentially another cup with Newcastle.

"Newcastle aren't going to win the Premier League. He wants to win titles. He wants to have the opportunity to do that. But Arsenal need to come to the table and show Newcastle the colour of their money.

"There are various reports out there saying Arsenal have made bids to Newcastle via intermediaries or middle-men. But as we sit here this morning, Arsenal have not contacted Newcastle.

"As I understand it, Newcastle have actually reached out to Arsenal and said, 'Look, are you serious about this? Are you trying to sign this player because we've had nothing from you?

"It's all playing out with agents and I think it's frustrating for Newcastle because without doubt it's unsettling the player, hence why he has said he would like to explore his options elsewhere."

Image: Newcastle value at £80m having sold Sandro Tonali for £100m

Newcastle are in the midst of a busy summer, having sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3m before Tonali's £100m sale to Spurs. The club have also spent a combined £83.5m on Bazoumana Toure, Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen.

Arsenal, meanwhile, are yet to complete any major signings. Morgan Rogers, one of their targets, sensationally joined Chelsea from Aston Villa, while their interest in Guimaraes is yet to be formalised, with Newcastle determined to secure a large profit on a player they signed for £40m in 2022.

"It feels like it's going to rumble on," added Downie.

"What would be the tipping point for Newcastle? I think it has to start with an eight. He is going to be 29 soon. They got £100m for Sandro Tonali but Bruno is three years older, so that means his value is a little bit less.

"Newcastle are desperate not to sell him. They've said he's not for sale. But once a player agitates to go, it's really difficult to hold on to him.

"But Arsenal need to come to the table and offer, and only then will Newcastle take their interest seriously, once they make a concrete offer, not via any middle-men."

Guimaraes, who featured for Brazil at the World Cup, has made 195 appearances in all competitions for Newcastle and scored 31 goals.

Leadership, experience, a history of robustness and a complete midfield profile make Guimaraes an attractive target for Arsenal, writes Sky Sports' Nick Wright, as the Premier League champions aim to turn last season's success into dominance.

Sports.title: Draper misses out on US Open main draw and will have to qualify
Sports.content:
Former British No 1 Jack Draper is set to have to qualify for the US Open this year as the 2024 semi-finalist missed out on a spot in the main draw.

Draper is poised to return to action at the DC Open in Washington from July 27 after missing Wimbledon due to a recurrence of bone bruising in his left arm.

The injury was the latest blow for the 24-year-old, who has managed only a handful of tournaments since first stepping away from the tour a year ago with the same issue.

Draper's ranking has taken a hit as a result, dropping down to 147th in the world, resulting in him having to likely qualify in order to play the fourth and final Grand Slam of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery says it was 'incredible' to reach the Wimbledon semi-finals and vows to keep the British No 1 spot.

Arthur Fery, the new British men's No 1, will feature at Flushing Meadows for the first time in his career after his remarkable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wild card has seen his ranking soar to 36th in the world.

Both he and Emma Raducanu, the 2021 US Open champion, are just outside of the top 32 seeds, however, with Raducanu ranked 37th.

Image: Emma Raducanu is ranked 37th in the world, just outside of one of the top 32 seeds

They're joined by fellow British hopefuls Cam Norrie, Jan Choinski and Katie Boulter in the main draw for when the tournament gets under way on August 30 - live on Sky Sports.

Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka and Wimbledon winner Jannik Sinner will lead the fields for the respective women's and men's singles in New York.

Sabalenka will look to become the first woman to win three straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, while Sinner will be trying to regain the title that Carlos Alcaraz took from the 2024 champion when they met in last year's final.

Image: Jannik Sinner retained his Wimbledon men's singles title earlier this month

The top-ranked Italian is coming off his fifth major championship, after beating French Open winner Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final.

Alcaraz, who has missed the last two majors because of a wrist injury but hopes to return during the North American hard-court swing, is ranked as the third seed and entered in the field.

Sports.title: Hearts suffer chastening CL defeat in nightmare first game for Vrancken
Sports.content:
New Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken endured a nightmare debut as his side's Champions League hopes all but vanished with a 4-0 defeat against Sturm Graz.

Hearts lost set-piece goals in the early stages of each half and conceded twice more during a torrid spell before the hour mark.

The visitors missed two excellent chances and played some good football in the first half but they are left with a mountain to climb ahead of next Tuesday's second qualifying round second leg at Tynecastle.

Image: Hearts look set to drop into the Europa League

Hearts look almost certain to drop into the Europa League, where they would face Benfica or Swiss side St Gallen, with the winners of this tie facing Fenerbahce or Gornik Zabrze.

Vrancken passed up the chance of guaranteed Europa League football with Sint-Truiden to replace Derek McInnes at Tynecastle with key players Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin following the manager to Rangers.

The Belgian named two debutants in his starting line-up, wide player Calvin Miller and centre-back Malachi Fagan-Walcott, while Jamie McCart was preferred to Stuart Findlay, one of Hearts' key players last season, in central defence.

Image: Calvin Miller made his competitive debut for Hearts in Austria

Hearts also changed set-piece coaches in the summer with Liam Ross coming in for Ross Grant following his move to Celtic.

Set-plays were one of the team's strengths in their unlikely title challenge but they looked vulnerable from dead balls throughout.

Despite a promising start which saw Harry Milne force a save, Hearts conceded inside four minutes from a long throw. Jon Gorenc Stankovic ran away from his marker and outjumped McCart to head home.

Graz attacker Seedy Jatta headed off the post following a corner and Alexander Schwolow, who was selected despite sealing an imminent move to Mainz, saved an effort with his feet.

Hearts improved. Claudio Braga forced a save with a decent effort before Landry Kabore shot straight at the goalkeeper from 10 yards after a good run from Oisin McEntee. Alexandros Kyziridis soon missed an even better chance when he flicked the ball wide after good work from Braga.

Image: Alexandros Kyziridis missed a brilliant chance to equalise for Hearts

The referee handed the Austrians a penalty for an extremely harsh handball decision against Milne before reversing the award following a look at his VAR monitor.

Graz dominated the opening stages of the second half and Jeyland Mitchell nodded home from close range after a 50th-minute corner. Schwolow seemed more concerned with pushing away an attacker than dealing with the inswinger, Kabore misjudged the flight and Mitchell shook off the attention of Braga.

Luca Weinhandl fired the third in off Milne three minutes later after the Hearts defence missed several chances to make a decisive challenge.

Schwolow stood motionless as Emran Soglo curled the ball off the inside of the far post and Jurgen Heil fired a shot through the goalkeeper at his near post after getting ample time and space to convert a return pass in the 59th minute.

Graz seemed to settle for four and Hearts could not get a lifeline.

McEntee made a mess of a free header, McCart failed to trouble the goalkeeper from a string of headed chances and Tom Renaud twice fired over from 22 yards.

Vrancken: Hearts 'killed by set-plays'

Image: It was a tough watch for the new Hearts head coach

After a hugely disappointing debut, Vrancken told Hearts TV: "For me we were killed by two set-plays and this is very difficult to accept, because we started okay.

"We got the first goal against, then we got control of the game and created some chances. We were not efficient and they were.

"I was pleased with a lot of things that I saw in the game. We could do better. We could have taken more responsibility to have the ball instead of just watching and reacting.

"But it was a pretty good first half, the only thing that was missing was goals.

"We kept believing at half-time but we missed a big chance and then again a set-piece.

"Efficiency is very important at this level. When you don't kill, you get killed."
