Sports.title: Wolves forced to CANCEL training as banned star refuses to leave the pitch - and extra security is enforced to keep player away from Compton Park
Sports.content:
Wolves forced to CANCEL training as banned star refuses to leave the pitch - and extra security is enforced to keep player away from Compton Park

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Wolves' preparations for life in the Championship descended into farce on Monday when training was cancelled because a player refused to leave the pitch.

Striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch when new manager Cesar Peixoto told him not to train with the first team.

And Wolves organised extra security at their training ground, Compton Park, to prevent the 25-year-old from entering.

Arokodare, who spent last season with Wolves as they were relegated from the Premier League, faced disciplinary action in April after getting into a physical altercation with team-mate Mateus Mane following their 4-0 thrashing by West Ham.

He will not be part of the squad travelling to Maidenhead for a pre-season friendly this evening. Arokodare did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

Manager Peixoto, who joined from Portuguese club Gil Vicente in June, has insisted he will be a firm hand with his players.

Wolves cancelled training after striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch - and called extra security on Tuesday to keep him away

New manager Cesar Peixoto initially left Arokodare out of their pre-season training camp

'Firstly, I'm a very demanding coach,' he said in his first interview.

'But, I believe in giving others maximum freedom and maximum responsibility. I want us to work as a team and as a unit and build a good environment. This is important to me, but I know very well what I want from the team. I want my team to be organised with and without the ball.

'Secondly, I want a team with intensity and to be aggressive and win duels.

'The third one is I want to show the quality of the players. To play an offensive game and to try and press high. To try and be the main character of the games. I want to win games, but I want to win while playing good football. With passion and energy.

'[The supporters can expect] a team with ambition. A strong character and identity and a strong idea of the game. A team that never gives up to win three points and to try and make the fans proud.'

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry. The Nigerian striker scored three Premier League goals last campaign.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted Wolves as well as Arokodare's representatives.

Demoting players from the first-team or forcing them to train in isolation is banned under new rules introduced by FIFA in June.

He faced disciplinary action after clashing with team-mate Mateus Mane in charge - but the duo shared supportive posts in an attempt to defuse the situation

Arokodare scored three Premier League goals campaign and could be moving to Serie A

FIFA reached an agreement with FIFPRO, the worldwide players' union, to better protect players from what is deemed an 'abusive practice'.

Chelsea's 'bomb squad' and treatment of players such as Raheem Sterling has come under scrutiny in recent seasons.

Clubs could face financial or sporting punishments under the new protections unless there is a genuine sporting reason for the player's exclusion.

Banishing them from first-team training cannot now be used as a tactic just to force them to find another club.

Daily Mail Sport has also contacted FIFA and FIFPRO.

Sports.title: Spain star who was attacked by Argentina players in shameful World Cup scenes insists they SHOULDN'T be banned amid FIFA's violent conduct investigation
Sports.content:
Spain star Gavi has surprisingly leapt to the defence of Leandro Paredes despite being involved in a nasty clash with the midfielder following the World Cup final.

Argentina were so close to retaining their title on Sunday after lifting the trophy in 2022, but were beaten 1-0 by Spain after a tense and scrappy affair.

Lionel Scaloni's side were aggressive throughout the match, as they had been during their semi-final victory over England, yet things escalated at the end of the game.

Having already had Enzo Fernandez sent off for a wild late challenge on Pau Cubarsi towards the end of normal time, Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground by putting his hand in the Spaniard's face.

Nahuel Molina also thumped Rodri in the torso as he was running by to celebrate Spain's triumph, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Paredes even appeared to throw punches during the altercations and Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala held Garcia around the throat before he struck Dani Olmo.

Gavi (No 9) leapt to the defence of Leandro Paredes despite their post-World Cup final clash

Paredes was involved in clashes with Spain's players but Gavi said he shouldn't face a ban

Then, as the Spanish squad lifted the trophy, Argentina's players faced away from their opponents in what was viewed by many as a poor show of sportsmanship.

FIFA have since launched an investigation into their behaviour, which could have serious consequences for the players involved.

However, during Spain's celebrations back home, Gavi was asked for his take on the chaos and left many surprised as he called for leniency towards Argentina's stars.

'No, to tell you the truth, I don't think he (Leandro Paredes) should be suspended,' he told Spanish radio station El Partidazo de COPE.

'I understand it's not a good image for children, but I think there's also that side to football, which is a bit more physical, more aggressive.

'The most logical thing would have been to send him off during the match, and that's it. In the end, I think it's all football, and it has to be that way.'

Paredes was fortunate not to be sent off during the game after committing a series of fouls while he was on a yellow card, and despite some miscommunication, he wasn't dismissed for his role in the post-match chaos.

Despite Gavi's words, Argentina's antics were widely condemned elsewhere, including from BBC Sport's pundits during their coverage of the game.

Micah Richards said: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time. Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest.

'Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Gavi did admit that the full-time scenes on Sunday were 'not a good image for children'

Fellow BBC pundit Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney also gave his views and said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina's players could also face further disciplinary action after FIFA opened an investigation following their semi-final win over England when several of them lifted a controversial banner touting their country’s claim to the Falkland Islands, which read: 'Las Malvinas Son Argentinas'.

Sports.title: Argentina star praised for defying his team-mates and watching Spain's World Cup trophy lift - amid heavy criticism of national team's disgraceful post-match conduct
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina star Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez has won plaudits for appearing to be the only player to acknowledge Spain's World Cup trophy lift after suffering a 1-0 defeat on Sunday.

The Albiceleste were unable to retain the trophy after their barnstorming victory in 2022 and instead reacted poorly, with many of the players refusing to acknowledge Spain's win.

The team was captured turning their backs on captain Rodri accepting the trophy in a gesture widely deemed bitter by international spectators.

But for Lopez, who plays for Brazilian side Palmeiras, the decision to watch the ceremony unfold and Spain lift the trophy after gaining their second star has seen him singled out as an example to his team-mates.

'To face your defeat head-on, that is what it truly means to be an honourable person,' one commenter said on social media.

Another added: 'Showed character. Congratulations!'

Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez was the only Argentina player to watch Spain lift the World Cup

The Palmeiras star was singled out as an example to his team-mates, many of whom turned their backs on Spain

A third suggested: 'Flaco Lopez all alone showing more class than the entire squad. The others had already vanished before the anthem even started playing.'

'The only one who respects football and his country by not letting them be made a laughingstock,' one social media user said.

Argentina were outplayed in New York after forcing extra time against Luis de la Fuente's side, with Ferran Torres finally grabbing the only goal of the game in the second-half of extra time.

When the final whistle blew, tensions bubbled over, with Leandro Paredes one of Argentina stars embroiled in physical violence, lashing out at Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

FIFA have since opened an investigation into Argentina's full-time confrontation, with the roles of other players and officials also set to be scrutinised.

Nahuel Molina hit Rodri in the torso as he was running by, resulting in the midfielder squaring up to his rival.

That saw players from both teams pile into the melee, before Paredes threw punches.

Elsewhere, 53-year-old assistant coach Roberto Ayala was also caught landing a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo at full time.

In the aftermath of the ugly brawl, DAZN Spain claimed Argentina defender Nicolas Otamendi complained to Rodri about La Roja's pre-match comments alluding to officiating concerns ahead of the final.

As well as turning their backs on their opponents some Argentineans descended into violence after the final whistle

The South Americans had benefitted from a series of questionable decisions heading into the showpiece event, with the Manchester City midfielder raising concerns before the final.

'You and (Spain team-mate Aymeric) Laporte. Both of you,' Otamendi said to Rodri.

'You spent the time crying and complaining about the referees, my friend. But you shouldn't have spoken before the match, you know that? Didn't you see what he said this week?'

Argentina's post-match conduct had earlier come under scrutiny in their semi-final against England, when unused substitute Valentin Barco celebrated Enzo Fernandez's equaliser by running towards the Three Lions' backline rather than joining his team-mates.

Barco is later thought to have said something in the direction of Jude Bellingham which prompted the Real Madrid star to smack him on the back of his head.

The Argentine national team later unfurled a banner repeating Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands, which has also seen FIFA open an investigation into their breach of the tournament's rules around political messaging.

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos 'holds talks about investing in Liverpool' as Amazon founder - and world's fourth richest man worth $257BILLION - considers joining bid for Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool.

British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia is leading a group of financiers which is in talks to make a 'strategic minority investment' in the Premier League giants.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport yesterday, Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, is pushing for a deal with owners Fenway Sports Group that could take the club's value above £4.5billion ($6bn).

Now, though, Sky News reports that Bezos has been approached to join the consortium and has held discussions about working with Bhatia and the rest of the group. FSG and Bezos have been approached for comment.

FSG took control of Liverpool in 2010 in a £300million deal and have since proven effective owners, giving the club the support they needed to win two Premier League titles and a sixth Champions League.

Liverpool are largely self-sufficient, meaning FSG have not had to invest much - figures published by the Athletic in 2024 indicated that they had only pumped in £136m.

It remains uncertain whether Bezos, 62, will help fund a stake in the Premier League team. Bezos is ranked by Forbes as the fourth richest man in the world. He has a net worth of $256.9bn (£194.9bn).

Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a small stake in the Premier League giants

Join the discussion Should mega-rich investors like Bezos be allowed to buy into iconic football clubs like Liverpool?

As reported by Sky News, the Amazon founder has previously considered bidding for the Seattle Seahawks - the reigning Super Bowl champions - and their NFL rivals, the Washington Commanders.

However, on neither occasion did Bezos proceed with a deal.

Bhatia, meanwhile, was co-owner at Championship side Queens Park Rangers. He has a stand named after him at the club's stadium, Loftus Road, but surprisingly stepped down from the QPR ownership setup yesterday.

A spokesman for Fenway Sports Group said in a statement: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

Nothing is official yet and, if it was to proceed, it would follow a similar structure to a deal made three years ago when FSG sold a small stake to sports investment firm Dynasty.

Bezos founded Amazon in 1994, originally operating it out of his garage. It now has a revenue of $716bn (£534.83bn) - the most of any company in the world - and employs almost 1.6million staff.

FSG has 33 partners including principal owner John W Henry, chairman Tom Werner, president Michael Gordon, as well as NBA legend LeBron James.

They have typically ceded a reasonable amount of influence to managers, being nowhere near as interfering in day-to-day affairs like the owners of Chelsea, Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

Fans have often been frustrated that the club have not taken off the handbrake in the transfer window. The usual policy is for the club to be financially sustainable.

Andoni Iraola manages the Premier League giants, who are currently on tour in the USA

The world's richest people *According to Forbes 1) Elon Musk $794.5B net worth (£593.59bn) 2) Larry Page - $284.5B net worth (£212.57bn) 3) Sergey Brin - $262.4B net worth (£196.05bn) 4) Jeff Bezos - $256.9B net worth (£191.94bn) 5) Michael Dell - $228.4B net worth (£170.65bn)

Last summer, they sanctioned the biggest transfer window spend by a Premier League club ever, £446m, though their club revenues had freed up space for that under Profit & Sustainability Rules.

Liverpool are currently in Chicago as they begin their pre-season tour of the USA.

Andoni Iraola's side play Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday, followed by Wrexham in New York and Leeds back in Chicago, before returning home at the start of August.

Reds fans are excited to see defender Jeremy Jacquet, who signed from Rennes for £60m in January, but more incomings are anticipated.

It has been a slow summer at Anfield - the only other arrival is £34.5m World Cup winner Victor Munoz from Osasuna.

Iraola has identified two areas of concern and has issued an indirect appeal to transfer chiefs to kick on with summer plans.

'It is difficult to say a number when the market is open,' said the Basque. 'You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

'There are obvious situations where we know we need to sign players. Winger, for example. We definitely need to sign a winger. In other situations, we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what the cost is, how we see the players we have.

'We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust that are not in the ideal situation. It depends on a lot of things.'

Iraola also said Liverpool are 'very thin' in terms of defensive depth, with Conor Bradley out for several months more yet after a long-term knee injury.

Asked about potential exits, Iraola insisted Alisson will remain No 1 after intense interest from Juventus earlier in the window and admitted he also wants to keep World Cup runner-up Alexis Mac Allister.

The Reds manager said: 'Alexis has been one of the best players of the club in the last years.

'He has had a very good World Cup so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. It always happens in the market. I want to keep my good players. I am looking more to sign new players than losing the ones we have.'

Sports.title: Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson reveals the 'emotional toll' of incorrect cancer diagnosis - three years on from receiving the all-clear after stage 3 cervical cancer battle
Sports.content:
Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson reveals the 'emotional toll' of incorrect cancer diagnosis - three years on from receiving the all-clear after stage 3 cervical cancer battle

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has opened up on receiving a second, incorrect, cancer diagnosis three years after she was given the all-clear following a year-long battle with stage 3 cervical cancer.

The broadcaster, 41, had been vocal about her journey with the disease, which saw her diagnosed after receiving a routine smear test in June 2022, and later undergo life-saving radiotherapy and chemotherapy treatment.

Wilson later produced a documentary on footballing figures who had similarly suffered with cancer, Football, Cancer and Me, which was released in November 2025.

But in a touching Instagram post, Wilson revealed that this year she had struggled after initially being told that cancer had returned.

'A little life update, please read until the end (red heart emoji),' she began.

Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has revealed that she was incorrectly diagnosed with cancer a second time

While the broadcaster revealed that her relief is 'indescribable', she spoke up about the 'emotional toll' of the misdiagnosis on Instagram

'In February, after my three-year scan, I was told my cancer had returned in a lymph node. I couldn’t believe it - it felt like my whole world had crumbled all over again.

'But after being referred to the high-dose radiotherapy team, one consultant questioned whether the diagnosis was actually correct. What followed were five months of tests, scans, waiting and uncertainty before, last week, I finally got the news I’d been desperately hoping for: it wasn’t cancer after all. The lymph node is now thought to be a benign neuroma - a cluster of nerves that was likely inflamed at the time of my original scan.

'The relief was indescribable, but so too is the emotional toll from the last five months, believing - then not knowing if my cancer had returned. Living with that uncertainty was incredibly hard. On the outside, life carried on - I worked, was being a mum, played (lots of) padel, spent time with friends and family, and smiled for photos. But underneath it all, I was carrying something very heavy, and there were times I found myself in some very dark places.

'So why am I sharing this?

'Firstly, because we often talk about being “cancer free”, but I’m not sure any of us ever truly feel free of it. The fear of recurrence can stay with you long after treatment ends, and I think it’s important we talk about that reality. If you’re someone living beyond a cancer diagnosis, please know you’re not alone.

'Secondly, because social media is never the full picture. The last few months on here have probably looked like lots of happy moments, lovely places and time with people I love - and those moments were all real. But they existed alongside this. Instagram is a highlight reel, not the whole story.

'And finally, because we never really know what someone else is carrying. A friend, a colleague, the person serving you coffee or standing next to you in the supermarket - they could be fighting a battle you know nothing about.

'So this is simply a reminder to be kind. Always (red heart emoji). Thank you to my incredible support network, you know who you are.'

In response to the post, Wilson received warm words of support from colleagues including Emma Paton, Hayley McQueen, Izzy Christiansen and Emma Saunders, who herself was diagnosed with thyroid cancer before suffering serious brain infection encephalitis last year.

Wilson revealed in her documentary that her life had changed 'in an instant' with her 2022 diagnosis, which came shortly after the birth of her daughter Mabel.

'It hit me like a truck,' she said. 'I did wonder if I'm going to die. I'd prepared myself for the worst, I think you have to.

'I actually didn't tell anyone. I didn't want to put it on anyone. If one person can see this and make a phone call to the doctor because something doesn't feel right, then it's worth talking about.'

Wilson shared pictures while undergoing the tests necessary to confirm she is cancer-free

A permanent fixture at Sky Sports News, Wilson also produced a documentary, Football, Cancer and Me

The intensity of the treatment which followed included five weeks of daily radiotherapy, weekly chemotherapy and three days of invasive internal brachytherapy.

She explained how the hardest moments came when treatment forced her to be separated from her daughter for the first time, describing those three days in hospital as the darkest period of her illness.

Wilson, who lives in the Cotswolds with her partner of nine years Dan, later celebrated being told there was 'no evidence of disease' in March 2023 with a bottle of champagne and a jubilant post on social media.

Wilson, who hails from Perth in Scotland, graduated from Glasgow Caledonian University with a Masters in journalism in 2011, beginning as a graduate trainee at Sky Sports News that same year.

She later became a sub-editor and then a co-producer before making her screen debut on the channel in 2015.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury lashes out at current world champions in blistering rant
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury lashes out at current world champions in blistering rant

The 'Gypsy King' will return to the ring on Friday night against Polish veteran Mariusz Wach, but ahead of the clash, Fury had some harsh words to say about the heavyweight division

View Image Tyson Fury speaks out ahead of his fight with Mariusz Wach (Image: @boxing/Youtube)

Tyson Fury brutally did not hold back in his assessment of the current landscape of the heavyweight division.

‌



The 'Gypsy King' will return to the ring on Friday night - three months after outpointing Arslanbek Makhmudov in front of over 60,000 fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Fury will take on Polish veteran Mariusz Wach behind closed doors over in Thailand.

‌



Since Fury's return, the heavyweight division has changed immensely. Following Oleksandr Usyk's controversial stoppage win against kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven over in Egypt back in May, the Ukrainian decided to drop his three body belts - the WBA 'super', WBC and IBF - in a move which has sent shockwaves across the sport.

‌



Murat Gassiev is the WBA champion, while Agit Kabayel is recognised as the WBC title holder. Daniel Dubois became a two-time world champion after knocking out Fabio Wardley back in May for the WBO strap, and the IBF belt remains vacant. Following the monumental shift, it now presents Fury with a perfect chance to become a three-time champion.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised READ MORE :

But when asked where he fits into the current picture in the blue ribbon division, Fury did not mince his words. "He does not. All those men have been gifted world titles. They never actually fought anyone to get one," he said on Wednesday. "Fabio Wardley - gifted a world title. Daniel Dubois - gifted a world title. Agit Kabayel - gifted a world title. Murat Gassiev - gifted a world title. How could you compare them men to me? Who's fought legends of the game and beat them for world titles.

"They're in their own little group, and I am f****** on top of the Empire State Building. They have got f*** all I want. They do not have any money. I have already had all the belts. They have got nothing that I want. And their names... they are not even high record names. Like, who knows who these people are? I know they are only just starting out their careers, most of them are a few years younger than me, but they are starting out with a no name and they have got to build their way up, and it's going to take years to get there.

Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

"This Gassiev guy who has just won a world title, who knows that guy outside of Russia? Nobody. Agit Kabayel. Frank Warren said 'you can't fight him!' Back in 2020. 'You can't fight Agit, he's a no name. You'd get booed out the stadium.' He was only 24-0, number one rated in the IBF at the time. All these guys, they are all doing their thing. They are all going to fight it out between themselves. Even after being retired for ten years, I can still come back and get a world title shot at any time, because I have paid the price. I have spent hours and years in this game to be able to do that. I will always be a big name."

Article continues below

He added: "I want to just keep busy and do me. I paid the price. I have fought four or five world title eliminators. I fought all the top contenders... champions... unifies and all of that s***. I have earned the right to do what the f*** I want now. Whoever I want to fight from any sport, I can make that fight happen. Because I am the 'GK' and I do what I want."

Whether Fury decides to fight for another world title remains to be seen. The 37-year-old insists he is content with doing whatever he wants. The Morecambe brawler is expected to come away from his fight with Wach unscathed and then take on long-time rival Anthony Joshua in a highly-anticipated all-British dust-up in November.

Sports.title: Adam Peaty issues defiant statement after wedding scuffle and family fallout
Sports.content:
Adam Peaty issues defiant statement after wedding scuffle and family fallout

Adam Peaty's relationship with Gordon Ramsay's daughter and his family feud have hogged the headlines

View 3 Images Adam Peaty is gearing up for the Commonwealth Games (Image: PA)

Adam Peaty has vowed to let his swimming do the talking following his high-profile wedding and family fallout. The three-time Olympic champion has become a fixture of the gossip columns since he married Holly Ramsay, daughter of celebrity chef Gordon, in December last year.

‌



That came amid a much-publicised rift with the majority of his family, which escalated after his mother, Caroline, was not invited to the bride's hen do. There was even controversy on the big day itself when paparazzi photographers clashed with bodyguards outside the venue.

‌



Before Gordon gave Holly away, a scuffle broke out, with the bride and the Hell's Kitchen star finding themselves caught up in the middle of the melee before eventually making their way into the abbey.

‌



Peaty, who has taken on the Ramsay name, has conceded he and Holly have not handled the "noise" surrounding their romance as well as they could have. But ahead of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, which starts on Thursday, he wants fans to focus on his exploits in the pool, declaring: "That's the Adam people should see – the racer. Everything else is my private life."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Peaty insists he welcomes the pressure that comes with being the biggest name in British swimming, telling The Independent: "Pressure can be given to anyone, but it’s probably best in my hands because the more pressure I'm under, the better I perform.

‌



Inside Adam Peaty and Holly Ramsay's wedding drama as the couple announces pregnancy READ MORE :

"At the same time, you need a strategy for managing the noise and we probably haven't done that as well as we could, but I'll make sure the swimming does the talking.

"We can't control every variable in life, but I can stand behind the blocks and not really care about what people's opinions are. Being at peace with a 100m or 50m breaststroke race is a beautiful place to be.

View 3 Images There were chaotic scenes outside the wedding venue (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Nothing else matters in that moment. That's the beauty of sport. If you can find that state of mind, it’s an incredible place to be."

Interest in Peaty’s private life – exacerbated by his recent announcement that he and his wife are expecting their first child – has ensured a tightly-controlled media build-up to the Commonwealth Games, where he is one of the few genuine stars due to compete.

View 3 Images The couple are expecting their first child together (Image: Karwai Tang, WireImagevia Getty Images)

Article continues below

His silver medal at the 2024 Olympics appeared to reaffirm his desire to continue on the big stage after a difficult 2023, in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns. He said: "I don't see success as medals anymore.

"That's not defeatist and it's not waving the white flag. It's probably the opposite. Success for me is coming away from Glasgow knowing I've done absolutely everything I possibly could to finish as high as I can."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury provides update on Anthony Joshua fight - 'Don't care'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury provides update on Anthony Joshua fight - 'Don't care'

Fury will return to the ring on Friday night against Polish scrapper Mariusz Wach, but has played down talks of a fight with Anthony Joshua later this year

View Image Tyson Fury ahead of his fight with Mariusz Wach (Image: @boxing/Youtube)

Tyson Fury is solely focused on Mariusz Wach and refuses to be drawn into talk about a fight with Anthony Joshua.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight champion will take on the Polish veteran behind closed doors in Thailand on Friday night - with all the proceeds going to charity. Fury ended a year-long hiatus back in April when he faced Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

‌



Fury would go on to cruise to a points victory, with Joshua watching ringside. The Morecambe brawler immediately called for a showdown with 'AJ' - who refused to step in the ring and face off with his long-time foe. But, just days later, the pair finally signed to fight and are expected to meet in November.

‌



But they must first get through their respective tune-up fights first. Joshua will trade leather with unknown heavyweight Kristian Prenga over in Saudi Arabia a day after Fury's fight in Thailand. But as anticipation grows over the all-British dust-up, the 'Gypsy King' refused to be bogged down by talks of a meeting with his adversary.

‌



Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury told exactly why mega-fight will not be jeopardised READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua retirement date emerges just days before Tyson Fury warm-up fight READ MORE :

Speaking at the pre-fight press conference on Wednesday, Fury admitted: "He (Wach) will give me some good rounds. I am not looking for a one round knock-over, I am looking for some good rounds, and that's what I intend to do. Whatever fights come up next, I just want to stay sharp. I said it at the beginning when I wanted to come back... I don't want to just have one fight and be waiting around for something that might not happen. If I am boxing, I am boxing. I do not want to be out of the ring for years on end, I have been out of the ring for seven of the last ten years.

"I want to stay active, and I want to box. Whoever, it might be, I do not care who it is. I have made a lot of money in my career and I have done very well, so it's not about money. I am boxing because I want to stay match fit. And if I am going to be a pro boxer, I may as well be one. Once I get past this fella here, whatever fight happens next, we will go into that and I won't be letting six or seven months pass by, I want to stay busy and active."

Anthony Joshua sent brutal warning ahead of boxing comeback READ MORE :

Out of the two main event fights this week, Fury is confident his opponent is the much tougher test and would knock Prenga out with ease. "Listen, this fight is a dangerous fight. Mariusz (Wach) is the same size as me. Same weight as me. He has had the same amount of fights as me, if not more," he explained.

Article continues below

"He has been in there with the most elite level champions out of two generations. Let me tell you, Mariusz Wach would put his fist through Anthony Joshua's opponent, whoever he is... Mr Pringles. This man will knock him spark out. He's a real fighting man. But, we are not interested in other people.

"This is my show and I am not interested in what's going on elsewhere with Joshua or Deontay Wilder or Oleksandr Usyk, or anybody. This is about me and Mariusz, it's not about anybody else. What happens beyond Friday is none of my concern. No interest. What will be will be and what won't, won't. And if it's to happen, and God willing it does, great, but if it doesn't - also good."

Sports.title: Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical
Sports.content:
Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical

Arsenal will have to pivot in the transfer market with Morgan Rogers becoming a Chelsea player but the Premier League champions are closing in on a new attacker

View 2 Images Christos Tzolis is set to undergo a medical with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Christos Tzolis is close to finalising his £34million transfer to Arsenal, with the Greek winger flying into London to undergo a medical before officially putting pen to paper.

‌



The Gunners are looking to refresh the left-hand side of their attack this summer and have moved quickly to sign Tzolis as a replacement for the popular Leandro Trossard, who joined Bestikas last week in a deal worth £15.3m. And while it's likely Arsenal will still sign a higher-profile player to compete for the left wing slot, Tzolis arrives at The Emirates off the back of an impressive campaign.

‌



He amassed a remarkable 22 goals and a further 29 assists across 52 appearances in all competitions for Club Brugge last season as the club won the Belgian title.

‌



Tzolis is no stranger to the Premier League, either, having spent time in the top-flight during a three-year stint at Norwich City.

While the 24-year-old is poised to become Arsenal's third signing of the summer, the club will have to pivot in their search for a new first-choice left attacker with Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea.

The England star was a priority target for Arsenal this summer after another stellar campaign for Aston Villa, who shook hands on a £117m deal to part ways with their attacking talisman.

‌



Rogers had been courted long-term by both London clubs with Arsenal widely considered as the red-hot favourites to sign him.

View 2 Images Arsenal target Morgan Rogers is now a Chelsea player (Image: CHELSEA FC)

However, Arsenal were unwilling to meet Aston Villa's valuation of the 23-year-old. And while Mirror Football understands they were prepared to pay a premium on top of the £80m figure they valued Rogers at, they were blown out of the water by Chelsea, who have chased the versatile attacking midfielder for over two years.

‌



With Rogers now a Chelsea player, it is yet unclear where Arsenal will turn next in their attempts to level up the left attack position.

They have been credited with an interest in the Paris Saint-Germain winger, Bradley Barcola, but the European champions value the Frenchman in excess of £100m, meaning a package to bring him to London could end up costing a similar amount to what Chelsea paid for Rogers.

Sports.title: Spain star speaks out on Argentina punishment after World Cup final ends in violent brawl
Sports.content:
Spain star speaks out on Argentina punishment after World Cup final ends in violent brawl

The World Cup final descended into chaos after the final whistle, with Spain star Gavi speaking out on the actions of Argentina's stars following the match

View 2 Images Spain star Gavi has broken his silence on being involved in the post-match brawl with Argentina stars (Image: (Photo by Howard Smith/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images))

Spain star Gavi has stated that Argentina's players should not be punished by FIFA for their actions after the World Cup final. The Barcelona star, who was an unused substitute in the 1-0 win, was among those heavily involved in the brawls as he was launched to the floor by Leandro Parades.

‌



Defender Nahuel Molina and coach Roberto Ayala also appeared to throw punches, but none were shown a red card for their actions. FIFA have since confirmed an investigation into their conduct, but Gavi believes they should not face any sanctions.

‌



Speaking back in his home town of Los Palacios y Villafranca, as per Marca, he said: "No, to be honest, I don't think they should be suspended. I understand it's not a good example for children, but there's also a more violent side to football.

‌



FIFA issue statement on Argentina bust-up and RESCIND World Cup final red card READ MORE :

Lionel Messi sparks conspiracy theories as footage from World Cup final speech leaked READ MORE :

"Perhaps the most logical thing for me would be to send them off during the match, but as I said, in the end I think it's all football and that's how it has to be."

Gavi was joined by fellow local Fabian Ruiz and to mark their achievement, where the two players were given their body weight in tomatoes. That saw Gavi receive 68.5kg and the Paris Saint-Germain star get 84.5kg.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



While Spain's players provided their public World Cup verdicts during celebrations and parades, several Argentina stars have instead chosen to post lengthy statements on social media.

Lionel Messi, Cristian Romero, Parades and most-recently Lisandro Martinez have all delivered emotional messages. The latter and Argentina's captain both congratulated Spain but the Manchester United star, who went off injured in the final, also appeared to aim a subtle dig.

Part of the caption on his Instagram post read: "I want to congratulate Spain on their well-deserved title. And to our people I want to tell you that the result does not define the journey.

‌



View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez went off injured in the World Cup final

"We went through adversity, we made what seemed impossible possible and we never find excuses, we only find reasons to keep going.

"We defend our colours far beyond the court and share unforgettable moments in the national team, together with our families and with the unconditional support of all Argentinians. It will always be a huge pride to represent them.

Article continues below

"Remember that 'the fall of the great is the happiness of the mediocre'. Thank you very much to all. Let's take care of our country. I love you Argentina!"

Sports.title: Wolves forced to CANCEL training as banned star refuses to leave pitch
Sports.content:
Wolves forced to CANCEL training as banned star refuses to leave pitch

New Wolves manager Cesar Peixoto has laid down the law during the club's pre-season campaign, with striker Tolu Arokodare being asked not to train with the first-team squad

View 2 Images Tolu Arokodare has been frozen out by Wolves (Image: Brett Patzke - WWFC/Wolves via Getty Images)

Championship side Wolves CANCELLED their training session on Monday after striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch. Extra security was also deployed the following day to ensure that the 25-year-old didn't return to the club's training ground.

‌



The extraordinary development comes just weeks into Cesar Peixoto's reign as manager. The Portuguese was brought in to replace Rob Edwards, who was sacked after Wolves were relegated from the Premier League by finishing rock bottom of the table.

‌



Arokodare, who scored just six goals in 38 games, was part of the squad responsible for Wolves' dismal season and had been linked with a move away. And his future at Molineux has been plunged into further uncertainty following Monday's debacle.

‌



The Wolves Poddy report that training was cancelled because of Arokodare's refusal to leave the pitch when asked not to train with the rest of the squad. On Tuesday, Wolves increased security at Compton Park in order to stop the ex-Genk star from entering.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arokodare won't be involved when Wolves face non-league outfit Maidenhead United in a pre-season friendly on Wednesday night. Clubs from Serie A including Genoa and Fiorentina are interested in signing Arokodare, with the latter having seen a bid rejected earlier this month.

‌



The decision to block Arokodare from training is viewed as a show of power by Peixoto, who's tasked with bringing Wolves back to the Premier League - and he made it clear in his first interview exactly what type of manager he'll be. "Firstly, I'm a very demanding coach," the former Gil Vicente boss said.

"But, I believe in giving others maximum freedom and maximum responsibility. I want us to work as a team and as a unit and build a good environment. This is important to me, but I know very well what I want from the team. I want my team to be organised with and without the ball.

Will Wolves come straight back up? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Cesar Peixoto was appointed in June (Image: Brett Patzke - WWFC/Wolves via Getty Images)

"Secondly, I want a team with intensity and to be aggressive and win duels. "The third one is I want to show the quality of the players. To play an offensive game and to try and press high. To try and be the main character of the games. I want to win games, but I want to win while playing good football. With passion and energy.

"[The supporters can expect] a team with ambition. A strong character and identity and a strong idea of the game. A team that never gives up to win three points and to try and make the fans proud."

Article continues below

Wolves have made three new signings alongside making defender Ladislav Krejci's loan move permanent for a total fee of £26million. Right-back Kieran Trippier and striker Raul Jimenez arrived on free transfers under Edwards before the club paid a reported £7.7m for left winger Rafiki Said.

Sports.title: David Beckham's huge payment for World Cup appearance blows away Shakira and Justin Bieber
Sports.content:
David Beckham's huge payment for World Cup appearance blows away Shakira and Justin Bieber

It was hard to miss David Beckham during the World Cup

View 3 Images David Beckham topped up his huge wealth at the World Cup (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

David Beckham has left Shakira and Justin Bieber trailing in his wake after his mammoth World Cup earnings were revealed. The England and Manchester United icon was one of the most visible celebrities at the tournament, attending numerous games and appearing in a succession of adverts for brands like McDonald's, Walkers and Stella Artois.

‌



Beckham, who boasts a combined net worth of £1.85billion with wife Victoria, made an estimated £19m from the tournament, according to market analysts. That tops World Cup regular Shakira (£15m), who performed at the opening ceremony and the final's half-time show and Bieber (£12m), who performed a solo at the latter.

‌



'Brand Beckham' carries huge clout in the United States, where David is a part-owner of Inter Miami, having spent five years with LA Galaxy as a player. One of his sons, Brooklyn, who has had a public falling out with his family, has even coined it in, making an estimated £1m, mostly from a lucrative commercial with DoorDash.

‌



Brand and culture expert Nick Ede said via The Sun: "While he's [Brooklyn] often criticised, global brands clearly believe his surname, social media reach and international recognition still have significant marketing value during events watched by billions. The advert, along with increased eyes on him, will have elevated his brand and value even more."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

On actors and pop stars' eagerness to be associated with the World Cup, Ede said: "Brands are willing to spend tens of millions securing celebrities who can instantly grab attention during the commercial breaks because they know they're reaching an audience of billions.

‌



Brooklyn Beckham watches World Cup final from home in dig at dad David READ MORE :

England World Cup player ratings: Bellingham shines but Arsenal duo suffer after gruelling season READ MORE :

"For many stars, appearing in this year's World Cup campaigns can be just as valuable as starring in a blockbuster film or releasing a hit album because the exposure is truly global."

But Beckham, 51, has become the celeb to beat when it comes to World Cup earnings. His £19m was £8m more than the England squad combined received for finishing third.

View 3 Images Shakira continued her long-running relationship with the World Cup (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



The FA received a £22m share from the tournament's huge prize fund, of which about half went to the squad and coaching staff. The players will earn between £350,000 and £420,000 each.

The FA sets aside a specific backroom bonus pool, with head coach Thomas Tuchel - under fire for his tactics in the semi-final defeat to Argentina - receiving a handsome standalone payment.

View 3 Images Justin Bieber performed at the half-time show during the final (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The players' money does not include their £2,000 match fees, which, thanks to a deal established by the England Footballers Foundation in 2007, are donated in full to charity. Still, no England player or staff member can get close to Beckham, who will walk away from the tournament even richer.

Sports.title: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos 'approached' as FSG enter talks over Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos 'approached' as FSG enter talks over Liverpool investment

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group have confirmed that a consortium, which is led by the businessman Amit Bhatia, have expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment

View 2 Images Jeff Bezos has reportedly been approached about an investment in Liverpool FC

A consortium in talks to buy a stake in Liverpool have reportedly approached Jeff Bezos. Amazon's founder and executive chairman is the fourth-richest man in the world, with a net worth of over £190billion.

‌



Liverpool's owners, Fenway Sports Group, confirmed on Tuesday that a consortium led by Amit Bhatia expressed interest in investing in the Premier League club. Bhatia was previously a co-owner and director of Queens Park Rangers.

‌



FSG said in a statement to our sister title the Liverpool ECHO: "An investment consortium led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

‌



FSG confirm Liverpool sale talks as billionaire family eyes deal after resignation READ MORE :

Sky News reports that Bezos has spoken about joining Bhatia's syndicate. However, they cite a source when claiming the billionaire is not certain to invest.

The consortium is understood to have already the backing of Lakshmi Mittal, Bhatia's father-in-law. He is worth over £20bn and led a £1bn-plus takeover of the Indian Premier League's Rajasthan Royals cricket team in May.

However, according to sources with knowledge of the situation, no investment deal is in place with Liverpool yet, with discussions over a "significant minority stake" only at a preliminary stage. FSG struck an £82m - £164m deal with Dynasty Equity in 2023.

‌



View 2 Images Amit Bhatia is leading a bid to buy a stake in Liverpool FC (Image: Andrew Fosker/REX/Shutterstock)

Bezos has previously been credited with an interest in buying an NFL franchise. He was said to be keen on the Washington Commanders three years ago and links to Super Bowl champions the Seattle Seahawks emerged earlier this year.

However, investing in a Premier League club would be considerably cheaper than the £4.5bn it cost to buy the Commanders. The Dynasty Equity deal valued Liverpool at around that amount, but Bhatia's group is said to be looking only to purchase a 30 per cent stake.

‌



Bezos's Amazon have shown an increasing interest in football over recent years. That began by broadcasting Premier League matches.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Prime Video now have the first pick for Champions League matches on Tuesday night's for until 2031. World Cup qualifiers now featuring national teams from the United Kingdom are also shown, albeit on pay-per-view.

Article continues below

They also have the 'All or Nothing' sports documentary series. Amazon have previously worked with Arsenal and Manchester City, with Manchester United next up this coming season.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
