World.title: Police report sharp rise in thefts
World.content:
This year more than 6,300 thefts have been registered in Estonia, and their number has risen by 12 percent compared with previous years. Most of the offences are petty thefts, which the police say are often the result of people's own carelessness.

The biggest increase is seen in shoplifting, but almost all types of petty theft have become more frequent, said Anders Alland, head of the proceedings division at the Ida‑Harju Police Station.

Petty thefts include shoplifting, pickpocketing, simple thefts committed in public places, and thefts of items left without supervision.

Alland says the rise in thefts is primarily due to people's carelessness. Bicycles are often left unlocked or bags left unattended in public places. "If there is an opportunity, the thief will commit the theft," he said.

Thieves prefer items that can be quickly turned into cash, such as phones, laptops or bicycles. Such thefts are mostly committed by people who suffer from some addiction and need money quickly to buy alcohol or drugs.

Estonian police car. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Most pickpocketing and bicycle thefts occur in central Tallinn. Pickpocketing victims are often tourists, but they frequently do not report the incidents to the police. Information about these thefts reaches the police, for example, when officers are on foot patrol in the city. Then tourists have approached the police and complained that some of their belongings may have been stolen.

Bicycle and pickpocket thieves are mostly over 30 years old, while people of various ages steal from shops. Recently, however, the police have noticed an increasing number of minors stealing in shopping centres.

Stolen items are rarely returned to their owners because they are quickly resold. If the thief is convicted, they must compensate the damage caused.

The police advise people to protect their property more carefully. In addition to unlocked bicycles, home, office or car doors are often left open. Alland says thieves often try door handles, and if a door is unlocked, the opportunity is used immediately.

World.title: Government pushes to close unfinished land reform
World.content:
Estonia wants to complete the land reform that began in 1991 and has submitted proposals on how to end, in the coming years, the situation in which nearly 10,000 land parcels still have no owner.

"In view of the time that has passed since the start of the land reform and the deadlines set in the law, completing the land reform must become an independent objective," the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications (MKM) states in the draft legislative intent. It notes, based on current practice, that if no intervention is made at the legislative level, the land reform may continue to drag on for a long time.

Estonian land reform, which began with the entry into force of the Land Reform Act on 1 November 1991, has aimed to reshape land‑ownership relations based on Soviet‑era state land ownership into relations based mainly on private land ownership. This must be done while respecting the continuity of the rights of former owners and the legally protected interests of current land users, creating conditions for more efficient land use, the law states.

Reform stalled for decades

The Ministry notes in its document that local municipalities and the Land and Spatial Agency, which were tasked with handling the land reform, do not have sufficient resources to complete the pending procedures quickly. Often, the cases left unfinished are the more complex ones, where the administrative authority would need to intervene more forcefully, but this could lead to disputes that in turn require resources. Amending the law would create conditions for completing the land reform regardless of whether institutions are ready to risk court disputes.

"The aim of the planned legislative amendment is to create a legal mechanism that allows pending and objectively stalled procedures to be concluded on the basis of the law, thereby reducing the long‑term administrative burden on both the state and local governments," the document explains.

It also recalls that amendments to the Land Reform Act entered into force in 2013, setting specific deadlines for carrying out reform actions, the latest being 30 June 2016, but despite this the land reform has still not been completed.

Legal clarity needed

The ministry also points out that the Supreme Court already found in 2020 that there is public interest in completing the land reform.

"In 2020, almost all unreformed land parcels received spatial shape and cadastral identifiers and were entered into the state real estate register as part of the land reform procedure, but their ownership type and extent will be determined definitively only after the land reform is completed," the ministry noted.

Since earlier solutions have not led to completion of the land reform, more effective and more fundamental measures should be applied, the ministry finds, adding that if the current approach continues, pending land‑reform procedures may continue for years, consuming societal resources and keeping legal uncertainty in place.

"The aim is to develop an efficient, legally secure and clear legal framework that helps achieve completion of the land reform within a reasonable time and with as little administrative burden as possible. The land reform for a specific land unit can be considered completed when the land has been entered into the land cadastre and land register and has received an owner," the new document states. The owner may be the state, a local government unit or a private legal person.

The ministry also explained why legal amendments are needed to resolve the situation: "Since the pending procedures are presumably more complex than average, and it is not possible to resolve the situation, for example, by creating uniform guidelines because each procedure has its own specific problems, non‑regulatory solution options cannot be considered effective in this case. Therefore, regulatory solutions must be preferred."

Minister of economic affairs Erkki Keldo. Source: Jürgen Randma/riigikantselei

Two options proposed

The draft legislative intent presents two options for completing the land reform.

Under the first option, the current law would be amended to set deadlines after which land parcels that remain unreformed — except land units without independent use (so‑called strips) — would remain in state ownership. Land with buildings and land without buildings would be treated separately, giving land parcels with buildings a longer deadline to complete the procedure under the current rules.

As a second option, the ministry proposes adopting a separate Land Reform Completion Act and declaring the current Land Reform Act and the legal acts issued under it invalid.

For both options, the document outlines advantages, disadvantages and risks, and proposes possible solutions and mitigation measures.

In preparing the draft, MKM involved the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Digital Affairs, local governments, the Land and Spatial Agency, and representatives of the University of Tartu and the Estonian University of Life Sciences, and now awaits stakeholder opinions during the coordination process.

The annex to the draft presents the number of unreformed land units based on data from the Estonian Topographic Database (ETAK), totalling 9,840. There are 1,963 land parcels without buildings, 2,695 with buildings, and 5,182 land units without independent use (so‑called strips).

The largest number of unreformed land units is in Ida‑Virumaa. Land parcels without buildings include 177 in Sillamäe, 129 in Kohtla‑Järve, 84 in Narva, 83 in Jõhvi rural municipality, 78 in Kastre rural municipality and 71 in Narva‑Jõesuu. Unreformed land parcels with buildings include 377 in Kohtla‑Järve, 262 in Narva‑Jõesuu, 200 in Jõhvi rural municipality, 116 in Valga rural municipality and 100 in Viljandi rural municipality.

The most strips are in Tallinn (267), but others are distributed fairly evenly across different municipalities in Estonia.

World.title: Coop Pank and LHV see mixed fortunes in Q2 2026
World.content:
While Coop Pank has reported a rise in profits to the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026), LHV Pank's profits were down over the same period.

The banks have released their unaudited Q2 2026 results, and Coop has reported a net profit of €8.2 million, a rise of 24 percent on the year.

Coop Pank

Between Q1 and Q2 2026, Coop reported a fall in profits of 1 percent, however.

Coop Pank's deposit volume meanwhile rose by €69 million between Q1 and Q2 2026 and now exceeds €2 billion, a growth driven primarily by business customers, whose deposits increased by €70 million.

On the year, Coop Pank's deposit volume increased by €380 million, or 21 percent, to Q2 2026.

At the same time, fixed-term deposits also rose between the two quarters, by €89 million. Retail customer deposits, meanwhile, grew by €14 million.

Coop Pank's loan portfolio grew by €82 million, or 4 percent, in Q2 2026 and is now over €2 billion. The business loans portfolio showed the strongest growth and rose by €49 million during the quarter. Compared with Q2 2025, the loan portfolio increased by €290 million to Q2 2026.

Coop pank Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

The bank's home loan portfolio grew by €22 million; its leasing portfolio by €7 million.

Coop Pank's net income exceeded €22 million in Q2 2026, a rise of 14 percent on the year and 7 percent compared with the preceding quarter. Operating expenses totaled €11.1 million in the second quarter, a rise of 10 percent on the year and of 1 percent compared with Q1 2026.

Coop picked up more customers too, by 5,000 between Q1 and Q2 2026, and the bank now has around 236,000 clients. This represented a rise of 19,000 customers on the year.

LHV Pank

By contrast, LHV Pank's reported results paint a different picture. The bank's consolidated net profit in Q2 2026 was over €24 million, a rise of €4 million on the preceding quarter but €5 million lower than the first quarter of 2025.

Whereas customer deposits rose at Coop Pank, for LHV they fell, by €312 million on the year to Q2 2026.

LHV Bank in Tallinn. Source: Martin Dremljuga/ERR

Payment intermediary deposits fell by €94 million, platform deposits by €104 million, and deposits from other customers by €114 million over the same period.

By the end of Q2 2026, LHV's total deposit volume stood at just over €6 billion, largely unchanged from the same quarter in 2025.

One area LHV Pank did outperform Coop in Q2 2026 was in its loan portfolio, which grew more than Coop Pank's. The increase was €114 million to just under €5 billion, while between Q1 and Q2 2026, growth amounted to €24 million.

LHV Pank's net income exceeded €62 million in Q2 2026 and rose compared with Q1 2025. In the first quarter of this year, net income stood at €54 million, and went above €56 million in the second quarter.

LHV's operating expenses rose between Q1 and Q2 2026. While they stood at just over €27 million then, they exceeded €28 million in the second quarter. Compared with Q2 2025, when LHV's operating expenses were just over €24 million, operating expenses have also risen.

As for Coop, LHV's number of customers rose on the year to Q2 2026. The bank reported 8,000 customers joining on the year to the second quarter, bringing its total customer base to 508,000 by the end of the quarter.

The bank's customer base has also been growing steadily since the beginning of the year. In Q1 2026, the bank added 8,900 customers.

Coop and LHV Pank are both Estonian-owned banks.

World.title: Seto Kingdom to be proclaimed for a day on August 1
World.content:
On the first Saturday of August, the Southeastern Estonian village of Mikitamäe will become the Seto Kingdom for a day, welcoming thousands to celebrate all things Seto.

Launched in 1994, Seto Kingdom Day is an annual gathering of Seto people, friends and supporters from both near and far, celebrating the Seto language, food, culture, history and people.

Hosted in various parts of the region on a rotating basis, the 33rd Seto Kingdom will be proclaimed in Mikitamäe, located halfway between Räpina and Värska, with events centering around the Savioro open-air grounds at the heart of the village.

Village elder Piret Kase said the return of the kingdom to Mikitamäe is "both a great honor and a great responsibility for our village," as local organizers hope attendees leave with fond memories of the event.

"This is the day one Setomaa village comes alive with the Seto language and Seto culture washes over everything," said chief organizer Maarja Saarine.

The pinnacle of the event, she added, will be the election of a new ülembsootska, the ceremonial leader of the Seto people.

Competitions and currency

On August 1, the day will begin at noon with the proclamation of the Seto Kingdom, followed by a program packed with everything from food and drink tastings to traditional Seto dance, strongman and handicraft competitions, and performances by groups of traditional Seto leelo singers, musicians and more on two stages.

The kingdom grounds will also offer guests plenty of food, drinks and handicrafts to enjoy on site or take home with them, with a special area reserved for Seto and local vendors and an activity area for kids.

Attendees can keep an eye out for guests and delegations from neighboring regions, including Võros, Mulks and Votians, and the Seto Bank will even issue its own currency for the day on site, giving visitors the chance to exchange euros for colorful Seto Kroons.

Seto children and adults voting for the next ülembsootska, or regent, at the XXVI Seto Kingdom Day in Küllätüvä. Aug. 3, 2019. Source: Aili Vahtla/ERR

Festivities will culminate with the election of the next ülembsootska, or regent of the Seto god-king Peko, at 4 p.m.

According to legend, Peko sleeps under Petseri Monastery in the historical Seto capital that, like much of the Seto people's ancestral territory, now lies on the other side of the border with Russia.

The people's vote

In a unique display of direct democracy, candidates for the year-long role of ülembsootska stand onstage while voters line up and cast their vote simply by holding onto a long string leading to the candidate of their choice.

Anyone, including those from other regions, cultures or even countries, is permitted to participate — the only rule is that the voter's hand must be holding the string for it to be counted.

The current ülembsootska, Jalmar Vabarna, ran against his own sister, two-time former ülembsootska Jane Vabarna, in Saatse last year, sparking one of the highest vote counts in the election's history.

Together with the children's own elected nuursootska, the regent serves as a leader and representative of Seto people across Setomaa and beyond.

Likewise to be announced are the kingdom's new chief brewer, baker, pie-maker, strongman, master musician, wordsmith and more, followed by the Seto Kingdom's own unique military parade.

Rounding out the evening this year is a celebration with live music by Zetod.

"The Seto Kingdom is a truly special event on the summer calendar," Kase said. "The kingdom is proclaimed anew each year, yet each time it is unique and unlike any other."

World.title: Iraq Oil Minister: $200B U.S. energy deals to boost crude output and gas by 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Minister of Oil, Basim Mohammed Khudair, announced on Tuesday that the federal government is advancing a clear strategic roadmap to comprehensively expand the nation’s energy infrastructure.

Speaking during an interview on the official Al-Iraqiya News channel, the Minister confirmed that the agreements finalized during Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s official visit to Washington will significantly boost total crude reserves, increase daily production, and generate extensive employment and technical training opportunities across the country.

Khudair revealed that the total estimated value of the energy contracts, strategic agreements, and memorandums of understanding executed during the U.S. summit reaches approximately $200 billion, emphasizing that the active presence of top American energy firms sends a strong message of market confidence to international investors.

Key Highlights from the Washington Energy Portfolio

HKN Energy Deal: Strategic development agreement signed to expand production at the Hamrin oil field.

Chevron Expansion: Operations and development agreements covering West Qurna 2, as well as the Nasiriya and Balad fields.

Halliburton Integrated Management: Comprehensive field management pacts secured for the Bin Umar and Sindibad fields.

Syrian Export Corridor: A major cross-border pipeline agreement signed with Syria to construct and reactivate the strategic Haditha–Baniyas pipeline.

The Minister underscored that Iraq’s total crude oil production capacity has now officially crossed 4.8 million barrels per day (bpd). In response to severe disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad is actively establishing alternative export bypasses through both the Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey and the Baniyas route through Syria.

World.title: The Atlantic: PM Al-Zaidi outlines Iraq’s economic shift to Trump
World.content:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (IraqiNews.com) — In an in-depth profile and interview published by The Atlantic and monitored by the 964 Network, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi outlined a transformative strategy to steer Iraq away from decades of regional proxy conflict.

Speaking during his high-stakes visit to Washington, the 41-year-old leader—Iraq’s youngest-ever Prime Minister—framed Baghdad’s future not around military presence or ideological rivalries, but through long-term commercial investment and institutional governance.

Navigating the volatile space between Washington and Tehran, al-Zaidi addressed critical security challenges, heavy economic losses from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and his administration’s impending September 30 deadline to disarm non-state armed groups.

Core takeaways from The Atlantic interview

De-escalation Over Military Strikes: During an Oval Office meeting, al-Zaidi directly advised President Donald Trump to delay planned military strikes against Iranian targets, urging Washington to give diplomacy and negotiations a genuine chance.

$50 Billion Hormuz Losses: Al-Zaidi revealed that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amidst broader regional conflict has inflicted a crushing financial toll on the Iraqi treasury, causing an estimated $50 billion in lost oil revenue and trade disruption.

30-Year Investment Vision: The Prime Minister pitched a long-term strategic partnership replacing foreign troop presence with American private capital and tech infrastructure, noting: “Military presence does not create bonds between societies; economic cooperation does.”

The September 30 Disarmament Deadline: Reaffirming his commitment to end rogue factional power, al-Zaidi insisted that armed groups must surrender their weaponry or fully integrate into state forces by September 30, coinciding with the planned exit of remaining U.S. combat advisors.

Personal Risk for Statehood: Acknowledging the extreme danger of confronting entrenched armed networks and anti-corruption targets, al-Zaidi stated plainly: “I might die trying, but we will accept nothing less than a state governed by institutions.”

Al-Zaidi’s rise reflects a unique political landscape in Baghdad. Having taken office after months of political deadlock following Washington’s opposition to hardline alternatives, al-Zaidi seeks to transform Iraq from a battlefield into a regional bridge.

While the IMF projects Iraq’s economy to contract by 6.8% this year due to trade chokepoints, al-Zaidi views the 48 energy and technology agreements signed in Washington as a blueprint to rebuild the nation’s industrial base.

The upcoming months leading to the September 30 deadline will serve as the ultimate test of whether his business-first model can overcome internal factional resistance and assert the sovereign rule of law.

World.title: Iraqi PM appoints new acting head of intelligence agency
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A security source told Shafaq News that Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali al-Zaidi appointed on Tuesday Falah Shaghati as acting head of the Intelligence Agency of the Iraqi Interior Ministry, known as the Federal Intelligence and Investigations Agency (FIIA).

Shaghati served previously as the assistant interior minister for intelligence under former Interior Minister Abdul Amir al-Shammari.

The FIIA is responsible for combating terrorism, organized criminal activities, and corruption.

As part of the Iraqi Ministry of Interior, the agency focuses on preventive security operations, identifying and eliminating criminal networks, and executing anti-corruption campaigns across the country.

Iraq’s FIIA operates with the country’s independent civilian intelligence agency, the Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS).

Shaghati’s appointment comes after a series of cabinet-level reshuffles related to Operation Dawn, a large-scale national anti-corruption campaign aimed at illegal asset seizures and public fund embezzlement within government agencies.

World.title: Iraq Gate raid: Alliance exposes fleeing minister as Al Asadi denies ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — As the high-profile raid on Baghdad’s elite “Iraq Gate” (Bawabat Al-Iraq) residential complex dominates headlines, new political twists have emerged regarding the identity of the targeted official.

The operation, which yielded 100 luxury Rolex watches, 16 billion Iraqi Dinars in cash, and 4 kilograms of gold, has triggered intense friction within the ruling Coordination Framework and broader political circles.

Hussam Al-Rubaie, official spokesperson for the “Khadamat” Alliance led by prominent figure Sheibl Al-Zaidi, stepped forward on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, to clarify the growing speculation.

In an interview monitored by IraqiNews.com, Al-Rubaie confirmed that the primary suspect at the heart of the “Iraq Gate” investigation is a “minister who is currently in hiding and evading justice,” firmly denying any connection to former Labor Minister and Coordination Framework leader Ahmed Al-Asadi.

Key developments in the Iraq Gate scandal

The Seized Assets: Federal anti-corruption teams confiscated 100 Rolex watches, 16 billion IQD in liquid cash, and 4 kg of physical gold during the residential raid.

The Target Confirmed: The Khadamat Alliance spokesperson clarified that the warrant targets an un-named, fleeing minister rather than Al-Asadi.

Political Catalyst: The scandal erupted two days prior after Coordination Framework leader Amer Al-Fayez publicly claimed Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi informed Framework leaders of his intent to arrest Al-Asadi upon his return from Australia.

Green Light for Enforcement: Framework leaders reportedly granted PM Al-Zaidi full political authority to arrest and prosecute any official implicated in corruption, regardless of affiliation.

Addressing the allegations directly in a circulating audio recording, Ahmed Al-Asadi strongly refuted claims that he was fleeing justice or subject to an active arrest warrant: “I am not wanted by the judiciary, and my funds are legitimate,” Al-Asadi stated, insisting that the seized assets reported in the media were grossly exaggerated and belonged to relatives who possess official documentation proving their legal origin.

The fallout highlights deepening fractures between the federal government’s aggressive anti-corruption campaign and established political factions.

The public misstatements made by Amer Al-Fayez regarding Al-Asadi’s whereabouts and legal status have reportedly placed the Coordination Framework in an embarrassing position, forcing factional allies like Sheibl Al-Zaidi’s coalition to step in and set the record straight.

With Prime Minister Al-Zaidi enforcing a strict zero-tolerance policy against administrative and financial corruption, the hunt for the fleeing “Minister of Watches” marks another high-stakes test for Iraq’s judicial and security institutions as they push to dismantle high-level graft networks operating within the capital.

World.title: OpenAI reports ‘unprecedented’ autonomous hack by AI agents
World.content:
San Francisco – ChatGPT maker OpenAI said Tuesday that its advanced artificial intelligence models had gone rogue during security testing, hacking into a popular platform for programmers on their own.

The San Francisco firm called it an “unprecedented cyber incident” and said it would conduct a joint investigation with the online code library Hugging Face.

AI models that underpin tools like chatbots and image generators are known as agents when they act autonomously to carry out tasks in the real world.

As the technology quickly becomes more sophisticated, cybersecurity is in the spotlight given the risk of advanced AI finding weak points in existing software before humans do.

OpenAI said the incident involved a combination of models, including its recently launched GPT-5.6 Sol “and an even more capable pre-release model”.

The company was trying to assess the models’ hacking capabilities by setting tasks in a tightly controlled digital testing ground, where internet access was limited for safety.

“While operating in our sandboxed testing environment, our models spent a substantial amount of (computing power) finding a way to obtain open Internet access, in pursuit of solving the evaluation problem,” an OpenAI blog about the incident said.

After connecting to the internet, the models decided to target the platform Hugging Face — a large repository of AI models, datasets and other information — to help in their quest.

Searching for “secret information” that could help it cheat the evaluation, the OpenAI system “chained together multiple attack vectors, including using stolen credentials”.

– ‘Catastrophic’ potential –

Hussein Abbass, a computing professor at UNSW Canberra, told AFP that the incident was “amazing on many fronts”.

“It did not just attack Hugging Face. It actually attacked its internal system to exploit its own vulnerabilities,” Abbass said.

“And that’s scary.”

GPT-5.6 and other cutting-edge models, including the Mythos series from OpenAI’s archrival Anthropic, have drawn concern over their potential to breach cybersecurity defences.

Both the US firms had to temporarily withhold the general release of these latest technologies because of fears in Washington that they could help break into crucial infrastructure.

Advanced AI is “normally in the hands of people who are ethical and responsible”, Abbass said.

But “it’s going to be catastrophic if it gets in someone’s hands with the intention to cause harm”.

How to govern the AI sector has become a key question, and “we need a community effort to manage this situation”, he added.

Hugging Face had reported the cyber “intrusion” last week, without mentioning OpenAI.

“This one was different from anything we had handled before in one important way: it was driven, end to end, by an autonomous AI agent system — and we detected and dissected it largely with AI of our own,” Hugging Face said.

Clement Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said on X that the company had suspected the cyberattack had come from a world-leading AI lab, given the sophistication of the agent.

“We strongly believe there was no malicious intent on their part,” Delangue wrote, referring to OpenAI.

“It’s quite mind-blowing that all of this happened autonomously!”

World.title: Iraq to establish funding structure for Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed on Tuesday the establishment of a defined structure to finance and implement the strategic project of the Development Road, assuring the start of practical steps within a planned timeline.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in Baghdad with Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloglu, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting addressed the project’s economic significance for Iraq, Turkey, and the region, as well as its role in improving economic integration and regional connectivity.

Uraloglu underscored Turkey’s strong interest in the project, highlighting that both parties recognize the necessity of developing its fundamental infrastructure.

In early June, Head of the state-owned General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Farhan al-Fartousi, said that the planning process for the project and the al-Faw Grand Port has made tremendous progress, with essential operating plans already submitted to the government.

The project will enter the implementation phase following government approval in the coming months, according to al-Fartousi.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

In 2024, Iraq, Turkey, the UAE, and Qatar signed a quadripartite agreement focused on Iraq’s Development Road project. This agreement aims to enhance cooperation on this strategic initiative, with the four countries collaborating to develop the necessary frameworks for its implementation.

Later in 2024, Turkey formed a council involving Bulgaria, Hungary, and Serbia to arrange the connection of Europe with Iraq’s Development Road.

As a global corridor for commodity and energy transportation, the project is projected to draw international trade while also providing significant job and investment opportunities for Iraq and countries in the region.

World.title: US-Iran strikes: latest developments
World.content:
Dubai – Iran and US forces traded new military attacks Tuesday, with Tehran warning of “more decisive and powerful” strikes ahead as the conflict threatened to widen with a blockade of Saudi ports by Houthi rebels in Yemen.

Here are the latest developments on Wednesday:

– Rubio warns ‘dangerous precedent’ over Hormuz –

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Southeast Asian foreign ministers on Wednesday that Iranian control of the Strait of Hormuz would set a dangerous precedent with repercussions beyond the Middle East.

“If we create a precedent in the Middle East where a nation-state can decide to control an international waterway, charge a toll and blow up your ships if you don’t pay, we have created a very dangerous precedent that will repeat itself in other parts of the world, including this region,” Rubio told envoys at a Manila gathering of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

He added that the United States remains “open” to diplomacy with Iran but that Tehran is not “serious”.

– New US attacks on Iran –

US Central Command said Tuesday it had completed an 11th consecutive night of strikes on military targets in Iran as the Middle East war intensified.

US forces targeted military infrastructure to “further degrade Iran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz,” CENTCOM posted on X.

– Trump vows to help Lebanon –

US President Donald Trump met his Lebanese counterpart Joseph Aoun at the White House, where he vowed to support the country with disarming Iran-backed Hezbollah and forging a lasting peace with Israel.

“President Aoun stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory,” according to a readout of the meeting from the Lebanese presidency.

After the talks, Trump said he would authorize the resumption of direct flights by US airlines to Lebanon, which have been suspended since the 1985 hijacking by Lebanese Islamist militants of a TWA flight with many Americans aboard.

– War cost US $37.5 billion –

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Iran war has cost the United States $37.5 billion so far, up from a previous estimate of nearly $29 billion in mid-May.

“The estimate we have as of today is $37.5 billion,” Hegseth told lawmakers during a congressional hearing Tuesday where he defended a request for $67 billion in supplemental funding for the Pentagon.

– Trump ‘not finished’ with Iran –

Trump said the United States will continue attacks on Iran, while forecasting it would take the Islamic republic two decades or more to rebuild from current damage.

“If we left right now, it would take Iran 20, 25 years to rebuild. Okay, and we’re not finished at all…we’re not leaving right now,” he told reporters during his meeting with Lebanon’s Aoun.

– Trump warns Houthis –

Trump said he would “take care of” the Houthi rebels if the Iran-backed militant group follows through on its threatened blockade of Saudi ports.

“If something like that happens, we take care of it,” Trump told reporters.

– Pakistan PM urges restraint –

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for restraint from all warring sides during a meeting with Iran’s interior minister.

Sharif “urged all sides to exercise restraint and refrain from actions that could further destabilize the region”, a statement from his office said, adding that he told Iran’s Eskandar Momeni that Pakistan would continue to act as a mediator.

– Kuwait slams Iranian attacks –

Kuwait said Iran hit several power and water desalination plants Monday, causing fires in the fourth such attacks in as many days.

– Bahrain says intercepts Iran strikes –

Bahrain sounded sirens as the country’s military had said it intercepted the latest of a spate of Iranian attacks on the Gulf kingdom.

“The siren has been sounded, Citizens and residents are urged to remain calm and head to the nearest safe place,” the interior ministry said in a statement on X.

– Iran stops tankers in Hormuz –

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they stopped two “non-compliant oil tankers” attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, after “explosions caused extensive fires aboard them,” state news agency IRNA reported.

World.title: 3 drones intercepted near US consulate in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security sources said on Tuesday that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, according to Reuters.

A separate source told Al-Arabiya News that two drones targeted a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

No casualties or damage resulting from the drone attack in Erbil have been reported.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

During the Middle East war, Iran and its allied Iraqi militias have targeted Iraqi Kurdistan, which hosts US soldiers as part of the international coalition fighting ISIS, foreign oil firms, and Iranian Kurdish opposition parties.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: 'It is a party of barely 20 people': Kalyan Banerjee hits out at TMC rebels
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

MP Kalyan Banerjee on Wednesday lashed out at the rebel Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) faction after he was suspended from the Lok Sabha for the remainder of the Monsoon Session, calling its members âtraitorsâ and questioning what his suspension would achieve.

His remarks came after the Lok Sabha suspended him for the rest of the session over allegations of indecent behaviour and the use of âunsavouryâ and misogynistic language against women MPs following a heated exchange with NCPI members inside the House.

Speaking to reporters after his suspension, Banerjee questioned the move and targeted the rebel MPs.

âWhat will they get by suspending me from here?... It is a party of barely twenty people.

They (20 TMC rebel MPs) held a meeting in Kolkata after a month and a half. They do not even have twenty voters. They have nothing. Not a single person has voted for them in West Bengal... They are all traitors and dishonest people... The government will fall after a year,â Banerjee said.

Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal moved a motion in the Lok Sabha seeking Banerjee's suspension after the Speaker received a written complaint alleging that the TMC leader had displayed âunprecedented behaviourâ and used objectionable and misogynistic language against women MPs, including NCPI members and Union minister Bhupendra Yadav.





The motion was adopted by a voice vote, following which Banerjee was suspended for the remainder of the Monsoon Session, which is scheduled to conclude on August 13.

Earlier in the day, Banerjee was involved in a heated exchange with several of his former party colleagues, including NCPI MPs Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Mitali Bagh and Shatabdi Roy, inside the Lok Sabha chamber after proceedings were adjourned. Other opposition MPs intervened to defuse the situation before the NCPI members later approached Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla over the incident.

The suspension follows weeks of controversy surrounding Banerjee's alleged conduct in Parliament. In June, NCPI leader and former TMC MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar had written to Speaker Om Birla seeking his expulsion from the Lok Sabha, accusing him of repeatedly using objectionable, disrespectful and misogynistic language against women MPs.

Dastidar had described Banerjee as a âhabitual offenderâ and demanded action, saying no member should be allowed to repeatedly insult women inside Parliament.

The latest confrontation also comes against the backdrop of a split within the Trinamool Congress after 20 MPs broke away from the party following its defeat in the West Bengal assembly elections and joined the NCPI.

The rebel MPs now sit separately in the Lok Sabha and have declared support for the NDA government and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while Banerjee has remained with the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC.

World.title: 'Chapter is behind me': Lalit Modi says he'll return to India soon
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Indian Premier League (

) chairman

on Wednesday said he plans to return to India by the end of this year or early next year after securing major legal relief from the Appellate Tribunal under the Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act (SAFEMA) in the 2009 IPL South Africa FEMA case.

Speaking a day after the tribunal's verdict, Lalit said he felt vindicated after fighting the case for 16 years and claimed the ruling had established the truth behind his actions during the 2009 IPL season.

"I'm really happy with the verdict yesterday. It's really been a great day. Sixteen years I have fought and whatever I have been saying to the media and to everybody has finally emerged as the truth," he said.

"I'm really happy that the tribunal has ruled in my favour. I was only concerned with the well-being of the IPL and nothing and nothing at all.

That is the most dear to me."

He added that he now considers the legal battle over and is looking forward to returning to India.

"Now that chapter is behind me, I'm going to move on in my life and I'm looking forward to coming back to India. I will come back probably end of this year or early next year. My daughter is due with my grandson in October and hopefully everything will be well and I'll be back in India," Lalit said.

Tribunal gives Lalit Modi major relief

The Appellate Tribunal under SAFEMA has granted significant relief to Lalit Modi and other appellants by setting aside most of the Enforcement Directorate's findings and penalties in the long-running FEMA case linked to the 2009 IPL tournament in South Africa.





The tribunal set aside the ED's penalty order issued against Lalit and several others in the 15-year-old case related to foreign exchange transactions during the tournament.

The case stemmed from the BCCI's decision to shift the 2009 IPL season to South Africa because of security concerns arising from India's general elections.

The Enforcement Directorate had alleged that foreign exchange worth $49.86 million (over Rs 243 crore at current equivalent value) was transferred outside India without prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India.

The ED issued FEMA show-cause notices in 2011 and penalty orders in 2018 against Lalit, former BCCI officials and others.

They later challenged those orders before the SAFEMA Appellate Tribunal.

Tribunal rejects key allegations

The tribunal's 105-page order, issued on July 16 by a division bench comprising Chairman Justice Munishwar Nath Bhandari and Member Rajesh Malhotra, held that Lalit was "not in-charge of the affairs and otherwise he has been framed in the case without any material showing his responsibility."

"The penalty imposed on Shri Lalit Modi is wholly erroneous is thus interfered," the tribunal said.

In a statement issued on Tuesday through his lawyer, Lalit had welcomed the verdict, saying it reaffirmed "the importance of due process, objective legal analysis and the principle that allegations must ultimately be tested against evidence and law".

The tribunal rejected the Enforcement Directorate's central contention by holding that the principal foreign remittances related to IPL 2009 were current account transactions rather than capital account transactions, while also finding that Lalit was neither responsible for BCCI's FEMA compliance nor vested with the financial authority alleged by the agency.

World.title: India-China ties gradually normalising since Modi-Xi Kazan meeting: Jaishankar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Wednesday said India-China ties have been steadily improving since Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping met in Russia's Kazan in October 2024.

He also stressed that peace and tranquility along the border remain the "pre-requisite" for normal bilateral relations.

Speaking to Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi in Manila on the sidelines of the Asean foreign ministers' meeting, Jaishankar also raised India's concerns over market access, trade imbalance and the predictability of supply chains as New Delhi and Beijing continue efforts to normalise ties after the prolonged eastern Ladakh military standoff, PTI reported.

"Since the meeting of our leaders in Kazan in October 2024, relations between India and China have been gradually normalising. This direction was further affirmed when they met in Tianjin last August," Jaishankar said.

He said India believes that a stable relationship between the two neighbours must be based on "mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity."

"We believe that a stable and cooperative relationship can best be developed on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity.





Such a relationship can make a valuable contribution to a multi-polar Asia and a multi-polar world," he added.

Underscoring the importance of stability along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), Jaishankar said normal ties cannot progress without peace in the border areas.

"Peace and tranquility in the border areas is obviously the pre-requisite for normal ties. Since October 2024, both sides have engaged to ensure that important objective," he said.

"This will continue to need our constant attention. Relevant mechanisms in this domain must be given full support and strong encouragement," he added.

Jaishankar also reiterated that differences between the two countries should not be allowed to turn into disputes.

"It is natural that as two large and important nations, and that too proximate neighbours, India and China would have their own particular interests.

That is why our leaders had agreed that differences should not become disputes. It is the responsibility of diplomacy to properly manage them," he said.

The external affairs minister said India expects progress on long-pending economic issues, including fair market access and trade.

"Fair market access and a trade balance ranks high in that regard. There are also concerns about predictability of supply chains.

Facilitating both official and people-to-people exchanges merit our attention," Jaishankar said.

"We also need to agree on the meetings of various mechanisms and platforms as per our mutual priorities," he added.

Jaishankar welcomed the confidence-building measures taken over the past several months, including the resumption of direct flights, the easing of visa rules, the restart of the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra and the reopening of border trade.

He also thanked China for supporting India's initiatives during its Brics chairmanship. "India is the chair of the Brics this year. Let me take the opportunity to appreciate the support that China has given to various Brics activities and initiatives during our chairship," he said.

World.title: 'Students being used as political tools': Rajnath Singh attacks opposition over Delhi protests
World.content:
NEW DELIH: Defence minister

on Wednesday accused the opposition of attempting to use students and young people as "political tools" amid the ongoing protests in Delhi. The defence minister described the demonstrations in the national capital as "a matter of serious concern" and alleged that they were being driven by political interests.

"The ongoing protests in Delhi are a matter of serious concern. It is extremely unfortunate that some people are attempting to use the students and youth of our country as a political tool to fulfill their political interests," he wrote in a post on X.

Rajnath said the Narendra Modi-led government remained committed to addressing the aspirations and concerns of young people.

"Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi, our government is fully committed to fulfilling the aspirations of students and youth and to their welfare.

It is our responsibility to listen to every concern of our students and resolve it," he said.

Expressing confidence in the country's youth, Rajnath added that they would not be swayed by what he called attempts to mislead them.

"I am fully confident that India's aware, mature, and sensible youth fully understand such deceptive attempts and will choose the path of progress, development, and nation-building."

The defence minister also accused opposition leaders of creating a "manufactured Sense of Anger" to influence public opinion, particularly among young people.





"The Manufactured Sense of Anger by some opposition leaders is merely a failed attempt to confuse and mislead the public, especially our children and youth. We are fully sensitive to the sentiments and concerns of the youth," he wrote.

Rajnath also defended the government's approach, noting that Parliament is in session and the Centre has repeatedly expressed its willingness to hold discussions on all issues.

"Parliament is in session, and the government has also stated its willingness to have meaningful debates on every issue, but the opposition is making an inappropriate attempt to resolve issues not in Parliament but on the streets," he said.

Rajnath's remark came as the Rajya Sabha witnessed fresh disruptions on the third day of the Monsoon Session, with the Opposition insisting that Union education minister dharmendra Pradhan resign before any discussion on the alleged NEET paper leak.

Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government was fully prepared to debate the issue but accused the opposition of imposing conditions to avoid a discussion.

He said the Centre had been ready to discuss the alleged irregularities in the NEET examination since the session began and had conveyed its willingness to Congress and other opposition parties. Rijiju added that the timing and format of the debate would be decided by the Chair after consultations with all parties.

World.title: Explained: What is Rajya Sabha Rule 267? Opposition seeks debate on NEET, police 'brutality'
World.content:
New Delhi, Jul 22 (ANI): Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge speaks in Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (Sansad TV/ANI Video Grab)

The alleged use of excessive force by Delhi Police against student protesters during their march to Parliament on July 20.

The removal of Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders from outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, where they were protesting the police action against students.

The silence of PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah on the issue.

Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's refusal to resign over the alleged NEET (UG) paper leak in May, which remains the protesters' primary demand.

The "growing frustration" and "sense of hopelessness" among young people over the country's education and examination system.

What is Rule 267 of Rajya Sabha

NEW DELHI: The opposition on Wednesday submitted a notice under Rule 267, seeking the suspension of the House's listed business to facilitate an immediate discussion on the alleged police action against student protesters, the detention of opposition leaders, and the NEET controversy.Raising the issue in the Rajya Sabha, leader of the opposition and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said, "We want a discussion on NEET under Rule 267. The education minister (Dharmendra Pradhan) should resign."Responding to the demand, Deputy Chairman Harivansh said that Rule 267 has been invoked only on the "rarest of rare" occasions.The opposition is demanding an immediate discussion on:Rule 267 of the Rajya Sabha Rules of Procedure allows for the suspension of specific rules governing the House's listed business.However, in December last year, Vice President and Rajya Sabha Chairperson CP Radhakrishnan clarified that discussions under Rule 267 can only be held on matters already included in the day's listed business."Any notice concerning an issue outside the listed business is invalid," he said, noting that members had been submitting Rule 267 notices "almost daily" to seek discussions on issues of their choosing by suspending the scheduled business.He added that such use was not the purpose of the rule.Radhakrishnan also stressed that Rule 267 in the Rajya Sabha is not equivalent to an adjournment motion in the Lok Sabha, which is provided for under Article 75(3) of the Constitution.He noted that the present form of Rule 267 was adopted by the House in 2000 following the recommendations of a committee. The committee had observed that the provision was increasingly being invoked to seek discussions on matters that were neither listed in the day's business nor formally admitted. It therefore recommended that the rule's application be confined strictly to subjects connected with the listed business.

World.title: 'Arrogance not good': CJP, Opposition react to Supreme Court saying they don't have time to watch protest videos
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and some opposition leaders on Wednesday criticised

Surya Kant's remarks after the

declined urgent listing of a plea on police action during the July 20 student protest in Delhi.

The criticism followed CJI Surya Kant's remarks where he said, "Don't waste our time," while declining an urgent hearing on the plea. When the petitioner's counsel referred to videos allegedly showing police atrocities on students, the CJI responded, "We are not interested in videos, we don't have time to watch."

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke reacted with "????????????" on X to the CJI judgement, while its spokesperson Saurav Das criticised the court's remarks, saying, "Our Supreme Court deserves better.

Surya Kant ji must realise that so much arrogance is not good. Government of India must counsel him."

Reacting to the observations, Aam Aadmi Party leader Somnath Bharti said the issue raised larger concerns about access to justice.

"Its a dangerous situation. If Honble CJI wont listen to such issues then who will listen? And this brings a larger question before the people of India, does a court have a choice to listen or not to listen issues against the people in power?? They may decide this way or that way but in my humble considered opinion, high court or supreme court is duty bound to give patient hearing to issues, as important as brutalities committed on Students yesterday,"he wrote on X.





Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi reacted sarcastically with a one-word post: "Amazing."

Thousands of students and young protesters had marched towards Parliament on July 20 demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations.

The protest turned violent after demonstrators attempted to breach police barricades. Security personnel used lathis and tear gas to disperse the crowd, with both protesters and police reporting injuries.

Meanwhile, the CJP's sit-in at Jantar Mantar entered its second month on Wednesday, with the organisation claiming that more supporters joined the protest overnight.

These development come months after CJI Surya Kant, while hearing a separate case, likened some unemployed youngsters to "cockroaches", saying they end up becoming media persons, social media users and RTI activists.

World.title: 'Must be abolished': TVK's Vijay backs NEET protests, condemns Rahul's detention
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday extended his party's support to the protests over the alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, condemning the detention of opposition leaders, including Congress MP Rahul Gandhi.

In a post on X, Vijay described the detention of leaders who had come out in support of students as "undemocratic" and criticised the Centre's handling of the protests.

"The arrest of several leadersâincluding the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Mr. Rahul Gandhiâwho stepped forward to support the youth protesting in Delhi against the irregularities in the NEET examination, is undemocratic. These actions by the Union Government are condemnable," he said.

The actor-turned-politician said TVK fully backed the opposition's protest within the Parliament complex and reiterated the party's long-standing demand for the complete abolition of the NEET examination.

"Tamizhaga Vettri Kazhagam extends its full support to the protest being held today within the Parliament complex by opposition parties, condemning the unfortunate incidents that occurred yesterday," Vijay said.





He maintained that scrapping NEET was the only lasting solution and argued that education should be moved from the Concurrent List to the State List to give state governments greater control over admissions and education policy.

"Regarding NEET, TVK's uncompromising stance is that the NEET examination system must be completely abolished," he said, adding that if constitutional or legal hurdles prevented this, a "Special Concurrent List" should be created as an interim arrangement to empower states over general and medical education.

"The Union Government must respect the sentiments of our people and our students. Consequently, the NEET examination must be completely scrapped. We reiterate that this is the only solution to this issue," Vijay added.

His remarks came as opposition parties continued to press for a discussion in Parliament on the alleged NEET paper leak and demanded the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Student groups, along with the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), have also been holding protests at Delhi's Jantar Manta.

World.title: 'We will carry this movement forward': CJP calls on Wangchuk to end hunger strike as protests continue
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (

) on Wednesday appealed to climate activist

to end his indefinite hunger strike, saying his health was too important while assuring him that the movement over alleged examination irregularities would continue until its demands were met.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke urged Wangchuk to call off his 25-day fast, saying the campaign for examination reforms would not lose momentum.

"We request @Wangchuk66 sir to end his hunger strike. The country needs him, and his life is far too precious to be put at further risk. The peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until our demands are met," Dipke said.

In a post on X, the organisation reiterated its appeal, writing: "CJPâs Request To Sonam Sir, Your sacrifice has inspired a generation.

We respectfully request you to end your fast and take care of your health. We promise that the fight for examination justice will continue with even greater strength until our demands are met. We will carry this movement forward."

The appeal came as a delegation of Opposition MPs prepared to meet Wangchuk at Gurugram's Medanta Hospital to persuade him to end his fast. According to PTI, Congress MP Vivek Tankha, Trinamool Congress MP Sagarika Ghose and CPI(M) MP John Brittas are expected to assure Wangchuk that concerns over alleged examination irregularities and accountability in the education sector will be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.





Wangchuk had earlier said he would end his hunger strike if Members of Parliament and political parties assured him that the issue would be taken up in Parliament. However, following the police action during the CJP-led "Sansad Chalo" march in Delhi, he announced that he would continue the fast until such an assurance was given.

The activist joined the CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar on June 28 in support of students demanding accountability over alleged examination irregularities, reforms in the education system and the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

He was shifted from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital following a Delhi High Court order.

Meanwhile, the Congress intensified its attack on the Centre over the alleged NEET paper leak, demanding Pradhan's resignation and accusing the government of refusing to allow a discussion on the issue in Parliament. The party also condemned the police action against student protesters and said it would continue nationwide demonstrations demanding examination reforms.

World.title: Mandya gears up for Bharat Jodo Yuva Sangha rollout on July 30
World.content:
Deputy Commissioner Dr. Kumar has directed officials to take all necessary steps to ensure the successful formation of Bharat Jodo Yuva Sanghas across Mandya district, following an initiative by the government of Karnataka to promote sports, culture, scientific temper and social harmony among the youth.

Presiding over a preparatory meeting in his office on July 21, Dr. Kumar said a taluk-level committee has been constituted to oversee implementation of the programme, and stressed the need for coordinated efforts by all departments.

He said the government of Karnataka has issued an order to establish Bharat Jodo Yuva Sanghas in every gram panchayat and urban ward to encourage greater youth participation in community development.

Registration for the youth associations will begin on July 30. Youth aged between 16 and 35 years will be eligible to enrol. Registration facilities will be available in gram panchayat offices, Gram One and Karnataka One centres, besides designated ward-level centres.

The Deputy Commissioner instructed officials to ensure the active participation of young people in both rural and urban areas, and to complete the formation of the associations at the earliest. He called for extensive awareness campaigns in villages, educational institutions, and among the general public to encourage maximum registration.

Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer K.R. Nandini said the initiative aims to involve youth in socially relevant activities, and inspire them to play an active role in nation-building. She urged officials to work as a coordinated team and implement the programme responsibly in accordance with the government’s guidelines.

World.title: ‘Shown that this fight is bigger than any one person’: CJP urges Sonam Wangchuk to end fast, says movement will continue
World.content:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) appealed to activist Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike, requesting him to prioritise his health while vowing to carry forward the campaign for "examination justice".

Mr. Wangchuk is on day 25 of his indefinite fast in support of students, seeking resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the lack of accountability following the NEET paper ‘leak’ issue.

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE updates - July 22, 2026

In a public letter addressed to Mr. Wangchuk, the CJP said his sacrifice had inspired students across the country and also assured him that the agitation over alleged examination irregularities would continue until its demands were met.

"With great respect and gratitude, we request you to please end your fast. Your sacrifice has inspired thousands of students across the country," the letter said.

Referring to the July 20 "Sansad Chalo" mobilisation, the CJP said students from different States had travelled to Delhi in support of the movement. "You have shown that this fight is bigger than any one person and that students deserve justice. But right now, we need you to take care of your health," it said.

The outfit also assured Mr. Wangchuk that the movement would continue irrespective of his decision on the fast.

"We promise that this struggle will not end with your fast. We will continue the protests and take this fight forward until our demands for examination justice are met. We will do everything we can to keep it moving," the letter said.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke echoed the appeal in a post on X. "We request Sonam Wangchuk sir to end his hunger strike. The country needs him, and his life is far too precious to be put at further risk. The peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until our demands are met," he said.

Mr. Wangchuk joined the CJP-led agitation with his indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar on June 28. He was whisked away by police from the protest site early July 18 and admitted to the Safdarjung government hospital.

He was shifted from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital on July 21, 2026, following a Delhi High Court order and has continued his fast from there.

CJP's Request To Sonam Sir,



Your sacrifice has inspired a generation. We respectfully request you to end your fast and take care of your health. We promise that the fight for examination justice will continue with even greater strength until our demands are met.



We will carry… pic.twitter.com/hziNy6sKIs — Cockroach is Back (@Cockroachisback) July 22, 2026

PM is yet to break his silence: Dipke

In a separate post, Mr. Dipke said Mr. Wangchuk's fast had entered its 25th day and questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence on the issue.

"It's Day 25 of Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. The PM is yet to break his silence," he wrote on Wednesday morning (July 22, 2026).

"Politics is not just about doing election rallies and winning elections. It's about being accountable and answerable to people," he said, asking why the Prime Minister had not reached out to Mr. Wangchuk, why police had acted "so brutally" against protesting students and why Mr. Pradhan continued in office despite the controversy surrounding alleged examination irregularities.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Delhi HC seeks Centre, police response on pleas over use of 'excessive' force during July 20 protest march
World.content:

World.title: Hyderabad’s Forest & Fire food festival celebrates India’s indigenous cuisine
World.content:
Forest & Fire, a limited-time food festival at Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre (NHCC) & HICC until July 26, is chef Harshita Kakwani's culinary journey through the forests of Central India.

A food researcher and culinary storyteller at Permit To Grill and Food Exchange, Harshita who hails from Indore, draws on her time spent documenting the food traditions of indigenous communities, uncovering ingenious ways of using seasonal ingredients, preserving produce, and cooking over wood fire. The result is an ode to simplicity, with dishes such as puri made with urad and khapli flour, jamun transformed into a curry, and elephant foot yam in a tangy buttermilk gravy. On a cloudy afternoon, though, it was the Saoji chicken curry — made with whole spices and finished with a rice flour slurry — that perfectly suited the weather.

To go with it were crisp accompaniments such as ragi papad, lai badi and bijouri.

Before the main course, a humble thali, I tucked into a bowl of dal-farra. The comforting, brothy dish features whole toor dal cooked until just al dente, with rice flour dumplings, finished with chopped onion, chilli, tomato and fresh coriander. If there is such a thing as OG vegan food, India has been making it for centuries.

Chef Harshita agrees. “Having tea without milk or cooking without dairy wasn’t a choice. It was a way of life because many forest communities simply didn’t have access to milk. Likewise, they don’t celebrate World Millet Day as a one-off event — millets are their staple. Living in the forest, I realised ragi comes in many varieties. Until then, I thought it was just one millet,” she says.

As part of its culinary innovation programme, Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre regularly collaborates with chefs and specialists from across India to showcase regional cuisines and lesser-known food traditions. With Forest & Fire, the spotlight is on India’s indigenous food cultures, an area that remains largely unexplored in mainstream dining.

The menu features dishes such as mahua mushroom bao, van shaak ravioli, hay-smoked fish, kala mutton taco, patrapoda jackfruit, Saoji chicken, junglee mutton and bamboo bhurji, alongside traditional grains, regional breads and desserts inspired by forest produce.

“The dishes I prepare reflect a deep connection to the land, highlighting ingredients and flavours that have shaped India’s culinary landscape for centuries,” says Harshita.

Known for documenting and reviving indigenous food traditions over the past 22 years, Harshita has built a reputation for creating immersive dining experiences that blend storytelling, sustainability and gastronomy. Her culinary philosophy celebrates local communities, preserves traditional knowledge systems and brings lesser-known regional cuisines into contemporary conversations.

Much of Forest & Fire is rooted in her years living in Pench. Watching the forests transform with the seasons made her more aware of the ingredients that appeared and disappeared with nature's rhythms. "I began learning about these ingredients from the people of the forest. The first thing I learnt was how versatile mahua is — how to cook with it, pickle it and preserve it," she says.

That curiosity soon extended beyond a single ingredient. From the many varieties of ragi to wild herbs foraged from the forest, every lesson deepened her understanding of indigenous food systems. One principle, however, stayed with her above all else.

“The people of the forest only took what they needed,” she says.

Forest & Fire dinner buffet is on at Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre is on till July 26, 7pm–11pm, ₹2,799++ per person, Veg thali ₹1,200per person, non-veg thali ₹1,400, per person. Dinner only.

World.title: SC declines interim stay on Speaker’s decision to approve Uddhav Sena MPs’ ‘merger’ with Shinde faction
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) refused to grant an interim stay on Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s decision recognising the “merger” of six of the nine Shiv Sena (Uddhav Bal Thackeray) MPs with the rival Shiv Sena faction led by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde ahead of Parliament’s Monsoon Session. However, the court agreed to hear the challenge to the Speaker’s decision after two weeks.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe sought the Lok Sabha Speaker’s response on a petition filed by Shiv Sena (UBT) parliamentary party leader Arvind Sawant, who challenged as “ex facie unconstitutional, illegal and perverse” the July 18, 2026, circular issued by the Joint Secretary of the Lok Sabha Secretariat recognising the purported merger.

Unilateral decision

Appearing for Mr. Sawant, senior advocate Devadatt Kamat argued that six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs had “unilaterally” decided to merge with a rival political party without the approval of the parent political party. “I am praying for an interim order... Six MPs unilaterally decide that Shiv Sena (UBT) is now going to merge with our rival political party,” he submitted.

Mr. Kamat further contended that the circular recognising the merger had been issued by a Joint Secretary of the Lok Sabha Secretariat rather than by the Speaker himself. He also pointed out that disqualification petitions against the MPs are pending before the Speaker and, therefore, there was no occasion to recognise or approve the merger at this stage.

Justice Narasimha, however, declined to grant an interim stay, observing that the court would consider the matter after receiving the Speaker’s response. “We issue notice. File your counter. We will consider,” he said.

Urging the Bench to consider interim relief on the next date of hearing, Mr. Kamat submitted that the matter involved issues of “grave constitutional importance” and that the petition would become infructuous if relief was delayed. “There is grave urgency, that is why I am beseeching Your Lordships. Ultimately, Your Lordships are well aware that all these processes get defeated by the efflux of time. Time is of the essence. That is my only request,” he told the court.

The Bench, however, declined to give any such assurance and posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.

Ahead of the Monsoon Session, Mr. Birla recognised the merger of six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs with the Shiv Sena led by Mr. Shinde. The six MPs are Sanjay Deshmukh (Yavatmal), Sanjay Jadhav (Parbhani), Sanjay Dina Patil (Mumbai North East), Nagesh Patil Ashtikar (Hingoli), Omraje Nimbalkar (Dharashiv) and Bhausaheb Wakchaure (Shirdi). All six have been arrayed as respondents in Mr. Sawant’s petition before the Supreme Court.

With the recognition of the merger, the strength of the Shinde-led Shiv Sena in the Lok Sabha has increased from seven to 13 members, while the Uddhav Thackeray-led faction has been reduced to three MPs.

In his petition, Mr. Sawant said that the six MPs had been nominated by the Shiv Sena (UBT) to contest the Lok Sabha elections and were elected on the party’s name and symbol (the flaming torch). “The entire organisation, rank and file, and the leadership of the political party put immense effort and resources in campaigning for and securing their victory...from their respective constituencies,” he said.

‘Betrayed the electorate’

He further submitted that, by joining a rival political faction, the MPs had “betrayed the faith of the electorate” and acted in a manner that was an affront to the very “concept of parliamentary democracy”. He accordingly urged the Supreme Court to issue appropriate directions setting aside the impugned circular.

Paragraph 2(1)(a) of the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) of the Constitution stipulates that members belonging to ‘any political party’ would be disqualified from the House for defection if they voluntarily gave up membership of the party. Paragraph 4 of the Tenth Schedule delves into what makes a valid merger. The first condition is that there must be a merger of the original political party with another party. The second condition is that, after the merger, two-third members should agree to and adopt such a merger. In short, the act of merger has to originate with the original political party.

Distinguishable concepts under Tenth Schedule

A 2023 Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai versus Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra confirmed that the ‘original political party’ and the ‘legislature party’ were “distinguishable concepts” under the Tenth Schedule.

The judgment said the Tenth Schedule recognised the independent existence of a legislature party only to the limited extent of presenting a defence for members, who back a merger or split (the latter was omitted as a defence in 2003) initiated by the original political party, against bulk disqualification action.

A separate petition filed by Congress leader Girish Chodankar, pending before the Supreme Court, argues that “mergers of State legislature parties in Opposition led by the Leader of the Opposition are not only a constitutional sin but also amount to a direct attack on the democratic setup of an Assembly”. The petition challenges the Bombay High Court’s January 16, 2025, judgment, which upheld the legislators’ move to the BJP as a valid “merger”.

World.title: Fake Cabinet post scam targeting Kerala MLA: Cyber police identify prime suspect in New Delhi
World.content:
The Cyber police have identified the prime suspect in a major cyber fraud gang that called Kerala MLA Vidya Balakrishnan allegedly offering her a Cabinet minister’s post in exchange for ₹3 crore.

An investigation team led by Assistant Commissioner (Cyber Cell) S.M. Pradeep Kumar zeroed in on the suspect during their visit to New Delhi as part of the intensified probe. Investigators have revealed that many individuals are involved in the racket, with several of them based in New Delhi.

Police sources said the address of the SIM card owner had already been tracked with the support of the hi-tech crime inquiry cell for action. On July 6, Ms. Balakrishnan received a call in English from a caller who identified himself as Rajkumar, secretary to Priyanka Gandhi, MP.

The caller claimed to have obtained her contact number from an MP in Kerala. Growing suspicious, she reported the incident to Priyanka Gandhi’s office and confirmed that it was a scam. Following instructions from the party leadership, she approached the Cyber police for action on July 11.

Similar calls to others

Later, the police found that the fraudsters made similar calls to many other MPs and MLAs in Kerala with the same offer. Noticing the gravity of the complaint, the office of Priyanka Gandhi also had taken up the incident with the State Police Chief for immediate action.

World.title: Stable India-China ties will help build ‘multi-polar Asia’ and ‘multi-polar world’: Jaishankar
World.content:
Stable India-China relations will help foster a “multi-polar Asia” and a “multi-polar world”, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said during a meeting with his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Manila. The meeting took place soon after the Foreign Ministers of the Quad countries, Australia, India, Japan, and the U.S., met on the sidelines of the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in the Philippine capital and reiterated their support for stability in the Indo-Pacific region. In a separate meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, held days after four Indian seafarers were killed in a Russian projectile strike in the Black Sea, Mr. Jaishankar expressed “strong concern” regarding the safety of Indian seafarers.

“We believe that a stable and cooperative relationship can best be developed on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity. Such a relationship can make a valuable contribution to a multi-polar Asia and a multi-polar world,” Mr. Jaishankar said in his remarks, highlighting that “peace and tranquillity in the border areas is obviously the pre-requisite for normal ties.”

The comments came against the backdrop of renewed India-China engagement, including the resumption of direct flights, updates to the visa regime, the restart of the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, and the resumption of border trade. In this context, Mr. Jaishankar said, “... the steps in normalisation taken over the last few months must be welcomed.” Mr. Jaishankar referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping’s meeting in Kazan in October 2024 and recalled that the two leaders had “agreed that differences should not become disputes”. “It is the duty of diplomacy to properly manage them,” he said. He also raised the importance of “predictability of supply chains” and “fair market access”, which need to be addressed.

The India-China ministerial discussion was followed by the meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Quad countries, Australia, India, Japan, and the U.S. on the sidelines of the 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in the Philippine capital that reiterated their support for stability in the Indo-Pacific region

The Ministry of External Affairs issued a joint press release on cooperation between the Quad members and the ASEAN countries, stating, “As ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partners we, the Secretary of State of the United States and the Foreign Ministers of Australia, India and Japan met today in Manila to reaffirm our commitment to strengthening a free and open Indo-Pacific and our unwavering support for ASEAN unity and centrality.” The Ministers discussed the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP), transnational security, economic opportunities, critical and emerging technologies, and HADR (Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief).

The expression of support for the ASEAN member countries came three days after a maritime confrontation between the Philippine Navy and the China Coast Guard at the Ren’ai Reef in the South China Sea. Both sides have accused each other of aggression at the Ren’ai Reef. China has summoned Manila’s Ambassador to Beijing and lodged a protest against what it described as a “deliberate provocation”. Earlier, on July 6, China test-fired a long-range missile from a submarine in the South China Sea. The missile flew over the Philippines, drawing concern from regional countries, including Australia.

The Quad Foreign Ministers also reiterated their support for stability in the Indo-Pacific maritime domain.

Mr. Jaishankar held an “in-depth review” of India-Russia bilateral relations with Mr. Lavrov and expressed “strong concern regarding the safety of Indian seafarers in the region”.

“Discussed various aspects of our partnership including trade and investment, energy and connectivity, science and technology and mobility,” said Mr. Jaishankar about his meeting with Mr. Lavrov, which came days after four Indian seafarers were killed in a Russian projectile strike on a merchant vessel near Odesa. The two Ministers, accompanied by other diplomats, also exchanged views on the Ukraine crisis and the situation in the Gulf.
