World.title: Philippines raises Ayungin incident, racist ‘monkey’ video in meeting with China’s Wang Yi
World.content:
MEETING. Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Theresa Lazaro looks on at Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi during the Opening Statement of the ASEAN Post-Ministerial Conference with China, at the Philippine International Convention Centre in Pasay City, Metro Manila, Philippines, on July 22, 2026.

For its first bilateral ministerial meeting in two years, the Philippines brings up a long list of grievances, even as it highlights the 'importance of maintaining open channels of communication'

MANILA, Philippines – Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro on Wednesday, July 22, raised a long list of Manila’s grievances and concerns against China during the first foreign minister-level meeting between Manila and Beijing in two years.

In a release to the media, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said Lazaro raised the following in her meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi:

the Philippines’ strong protest over the violent actions committed by China Coast Guard personnel against Filipino navy personnel at Ayungin Shoal on July 20

concerns over actions that have infringed on maritime rights and entitlements, including incidents affecting the safety of Filipino personnel and fishermen

the removal of remaining structures in Bajo de Masinloc

Lazaro, according to the DFA, also said during the meeting that “disagreements over legal and political issues do not justify resorting to disturbing imagery.” The DFA had earlier protested the depiction of the Philippines and Filipinos as monkeys in a July 10 “deeply offensive, distressing, and unacceptable” AI-generated video by Chinese state-run China Daily.

Two things serve as backdrop to the Lazaro-Wang meeting: Manila’s desire to “reset” ties with its northern neighbor and successive incidents, at sea and in the political and information sphere, that have caused tensions between the Philippines and China to rise.

The bilateral meeting is the first foreign minister-level meeting between Beijing and Manila. It happened on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Foreign Ministers Meetings and the Post-Ministerial Conferences, where ASEAN officials met with their counterparts from the bloc’s dialogue partners, including China.

The DFA, in its release, described the meeting as a “candid, comprehensive, and constructive” discussion covering “political and security matters, maritime and law enforcement issues, regional and international developments, and mutually beneficial cooperation in trade and investment, agriculture, tourism, connectivity, and people-to-people exchanges.”

The two countries, said Manila, “underscored the importance of maintaining open channels of communication, enhancing mutual understanding, and strengthening confidence-building measures.”

Philippine-China ties

The two countries’ bilateral ties have turned tense since 2023, when Philippine policy under President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. evolved to become more assertive in its entitlements and claims in the South China Sea, which Beijing claims in almost its entirety.

At sea, confrontations between the two countries are almost always dangerous and have, in several instances, turned physical or mortal. In June 2024, the China Coast Guard harassed Philippine soldiers already moored alongside the BRP Sierra Madre in Ayungin Shoal. Over two years later, on July 20, 2026, CCG personnel sailed close to the makeshift outpost, leading to a confrontation that left a Filipino soldier with a head wound.

BILATERAL. Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro talks to China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi during their bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Pasay, Metro Manila on July 22, 2026. Photo by Ted Aljibe/Pool via Reuters

For China, maritime confrontations have harmed their own, too. A CCG and Chinese navy warship collided with each other in August 2025 as both were trying to chase down a Philippine Coast Guard vessel. It’s been reported that at least two CCG personnel may have died from the collision, but Beijing had not even acknowledged the clash.

At the beginning of 2026, or upon Manila’s assumption of the ASEAN chairmanship, the Philippines also worked to revive bilateral ties. On the sidelines of the Code of Conduct negotiations in Cebu City last January, senior diplomats from both sides met. This meeting was followed by a series of consultations in China at the end of March.

ASEAN hopes to finish its talks on a Code of Conduct (COC) on the South China Sea with China before the Philippines’ chairmanship ends. Experts have not been optimistic about the ASEAN-set 2026 deadline, although both Lazaro and Wang “highlighted the progress of the negotiations” in their meeting, said the DFA.

“Both sides underscored the importance of maintaining open channels of communication, enhancing mutual understanding, and strengthening confidence-building measures. They highlighted the progress of the negotiations on the ASEAN-China Code of Conduct and the continued willingness to work together to conclude the negotiations of the COC this year,” said the DFA.

“The two sides underscored the importance of maintaining peace, security, and stability in the region, reducing the risk of miscalculation, and sustaining dialogue on matters of mutual concern.” – Rappler.com

World.title: [Be The Good] Rappler is covering the impeachment trial. What can we do better?
World.content:
We at Rappler invite you to ask us any question about how we are covering and reporting on the Sara Duterte impeachment trial

Hello!

Last Friday, July 17, four-time Senate president and impeachment trial veteran Franklin Drilon, was a guest at our second Rappler+ quarterly town hall of the year.

His answer to Rappler political reporter Dwight de Leon’s last question lingered with me over the weekend. Dwight, who was our moderator for the open forum with the former senator, asked: What can civil society and the media do to help the impeachment trial fulfill its constitutionally-mandated role of ensuring accountability?

“Make noise,” said Drilon.

Unlike criminal court proceedings, the impeachment trial is political in nature. Public perception of accountability being upheld is critical to the senator-judges. And that is where the power of this unique process lies.

“I tell you, the senators are concerned about the views expressed by civil society. I have been there. I know that they are very concerned about how people will judge them, more than the congressmen,” Drilon told Rappler+ members and various Rappler staff present in the newsroom.

“There should be a better coordinated effort to make our senator-judges realize that their obligation is to ferret out the truth,” he added.

With that in mind, we at Rappler invite you and all our other readers to ask us any question about how we are covering and reporting on the Sara Duterte impeachment trial.

We will collate all your questions, share them with our staff, and devote an article to answering them. We’d also like to get your ideas on how we can cover this high-stakes trial better. What are we missing? What should we focus on?

Here’s a quick look at our coverage:

You can answer by just replying to this newsletter. If you’re reading this on Rappler’s app or website, you can send your answers to community@rappler.com.

You can also suggest speakers or topics you’d like us to feature in our next Rappler+ town hall. We’re doing these town halls every quarter. To attend, become a Rappler+ member through this page. We have a virtual component to allow members outside Metro Manila to participate.

These town halls are a chance for us to meet Rappler+ members, give them a unique experience of our journalism, and report to them on the impact we’ve made together during the past quarter.

I will leave you with these final words from Drilon, after he was asked what advice he can give to people who are disillusioned by everything that is happening in the Philippines.

“I must admit that there are times when I myself get disillusioned. But you wake up to the fact that this is your only country,” said the statesman.

“We can’t rely on anybody else. But at the end of the day, this is our country, and we suffer the consequences of erroneous decisions that we make as a people.”

Until the next newsletter!

World.title: FACT CHECK: No Trump plan to secure Duterte’s release from ICC
World.content:
The US president has not made any statement supporting Duterte’s release; similar posts have been debunked since Duterte's arrest in March 2025

Claim: US President Donald Trump plans to secure the release of former president Rodrigo Duterte from the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC).

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-check this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim was uploaded on July 17 and has garnered 383,000 views, 18,500 reactions, 2,500 comments, 5,500 shares, and 664 saves, as of writing.

The video’s narrator says, “Magandang balita ‘to. Good news. Nandyan si Donald Trump na gusto niyang kunin sa ICC si Duterte. Kaya sa mga nanonood sa aking video ngayon, maniwala na kayo, hindi ito fake news. Abangan na lang natin ang mga kabanata nito kapag makuha na si Duterte ni Trump.”

(This is good news. Good news. Donald Trump wants to free Duterte from the ICC. So, to everyone watching my video right now, believe it — this is not fake news. Let’s just wait for the next developments once Trump has freed Duterte.)



The video also uses an edited photo of Duterte side by side with Trump, who is shown wearing a Captain America suit.

The facts: There are no official statements from Trump or the White House indicating that the US president is seeking or intends to seek Duterte’s release from the ICC.

While Trump and Duterte maintained a cordial relationship during their terms as presidents, the former has not made any public remarks about Duterte’s ICC case.

It is also highly unlikely that the US leader is planning to secure Duterte’s release from ICC custody. The United States is not a state party to the Rome Statute, the treaty establishing the ICC, and has no authority to interfere in the court’s affairs.

The US is also at odds with the ICC. On July 13, 2026, the US government asserted that the ICC has no jurisdiction over Americans and announced a sweeping campaign targeting the court over its investigations involving American servicemen and intelligence officers.

Duterte trial: Duterte remains at the ICC detention center in The Hague, Netherlands, where he has been detained since his March 2025 arrest.

The ICC has scheduled the start of his trial on November 30, 2026. The former president faces charges of crimes against humanity due to his alleged involvement in the killings under his war on drugs and the Davao Death Squad.

The court is set to hold its next status conference on the case on September 16, 2026.

Debunked: Similar fact-check articles have been published by Rappler on claims related to Trump and Duterte’s ICC case:

– Jennifer Pading/Rappler.com

Jennifer Jezreel Kaye Pading is an economics student at Visayas State University in Baybay City in Leyte. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, she is also the Executive Editor of Amaranth and community officer of AYEJ-Leyte Panaad Ha Sinirangan.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: Nominations for 2026 Quezon City Green Awards open until August 14, 2026
World.content:
PRESS RELEASE: As the city continues to champion innovation and community-driven solutions, the Quezon City Government is now accepting entries for the 2026 Quezon City Green Awards.

(The following is a press release from the Quezon City Government.)

Launched in 2023, the Quezon City Green Awards (QCGA) is the country’s first LGU-led award-giving program that recognizes the most innovative initiatives that address today’s environmental and disaster resilience challenges.

This year’s competition marks a significant shift from last year’s sector-based evaluation process. While the QCGA continues to recognize initiatives under its two categories—Green and Resilient—entries will now be assessed based on the challenges they address and the tangible impact they create.

The Resilient Category covers initiatives on disaster prevention and mitigation, disaster preparedness, disaster response, and recovery and rehabilitation.

On the other hand, the Green Category recognizes initiatives on food security, green building, plastic waste management, and textile circularity.

“Innovation knows no boundaries, so this year’s Green Awards will adopt thematic categories to really put the spotlight on innovative solutions rather than the sector they belong to,” Mayor Joy Belmonte said.

“At the end of the day, our goal is to encourage collaboration across sectors and to welcome diverse ideas that can be adapted and replicated within communities, groups, and organizations, further strengthening our commitment to an inclusive, green, resilient, and sustainable future for all,” she added.

Groups, including government, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector, can submit their applications online by filling out the entry form (bit.ly/4wACD2S) until August 14, 2026.

Winning organizations will receive grants of up to ₱300,000 to support their innovation proposals, along with special citations, media recognition, and the opportunity to have their initiatives integrated into the city’s resilient and green programs.

Beyond recognizing outstanding initiatives, the QC Green Awards will help organizations refine and expand their projects. Semi-finalists will receive expert coaching from disaster risk reduction and climate action practitioners, participate in a full-day ideation workshop, receive technical feedback from the review panel, and continue to receive guidance from the QCGA secretariat throughout the competition.

Finalists will build on these opportunities through dedicated pitch coaching, formal recognition through the city’s public communication platforms, and endless opportunities for future partnerships with the Quezon City Government.

A detailed competition briefer is available at bit.ly/QCGA2026Briefer.

For inquiries, organizations may email entry.greenawards@quezoncity.gov.ph or contact the Quezon City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office at 8988-4242 local 8038 or the Climate Change and Environmental Sustainability Department at 8988-4242 local 8360. – Rappler.com

World.title: Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial: Article IV highlights
World.content:
Inquirer image

MANILA, Philippines — The House prosecution panel on Wednesday concluded its presentation of Article IV, which accuses Vice President Sara Duterte of making grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.

The prosecution’s presentation was completed in 9 days, despite being given a total of 11 days to present their evidence. Though it should be noted that, technically, it only took six days for the court to tackle Article IV as three days were spent on other matters.

READ: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of VP Sara Duterte | July 21, 2026

Article continues after this 

Below are the highlights from these nine days:

Day 1

The trial officially began on July 6, marking the very first time the Senate convened as an impeachment court to try a sitting Vice President.

However, the first day of the trial focused on administrative and procedural matters, with Senator-judge Francis “Chiz” Escudero being elected as the court’s presiding officer, a post traditionally held by the Senate president.

Escudero then made his first ruling the same day of her election, maintaining that at least 16 votes from senator-judges are needed for a conviction, even if three senators are currently unable to participate in the trial.

Article continues after this 

Duterte, maintaining her consistent absence from previous House hearings, chose to snub the first day of the proceedings—relying only on her team of private lawyers to represent her as the defense panel.

Day 2

Article continues after this 

Meanwhile, arguably the main highlight of the second day occurred right before the trial itself started when Duterte herself suddenly showed up at the Senate.

However, the vice president appeared at the upper chamber not to join the trial but only to meet with her lawyers, choosing to hold their meeting at the Senate instead of a different location.

Despite being adamant about not joining the trial, the vice president delivered a statement to reporters: “In this bloodbath and bludgeoning, I will be bloodied but unbowed.”

It was during the second day when the prosecution panel formally introduced Article IV of the Articles of Impeachment against Duterte before the court.

House prosecutor Rep. Lorenz Defensor opened the prosecution’s case by calling the threats “especially sinister” because they came from the vice president herself and not an ordinary citizen.

Their accusation was rooted in a statement uttered by Duterte herself during a November 2024 online press conference where she herself revealed the kill plot. This clip was screened before the senator-judges despite defense objections.

The prosecution then called up their first witness, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Senior Cyber Investigation Agent John Mark Calilung, who testified on the forensic authentication of the livestreamed videos containing the statements.

The defense attempted to block Calilung’s presentation as a witness, but was overruled by the court.

Private prosecutor Amando Ligutan then argued that Duterte’s statements established that she had a “plan” to have the three officials killed, which was in response to Sen.-judge Risa Hontiveros’s question on how the statements are impeachable given that they do not constitute proof an assassin was actually contracted.

Escudero then gave the defense a chance to also respond to Hontiveros’ question as it “pertains to the final issue of this entire impeachment proceeding.”

Day 3

It was on the third day when NBI senior agent John Mark Calilung concluded his testimony, informing senator-judges that the NBI investigated Duterte’s alleged threats based on its mandate to probe threats against the president and other top officials, even without a formal complaint from the offended parties.

Duterte’s defense team then presented snippets of Duterte’s chief of staff Zuleika Lopez crying over her detention by the House in the same press conference where the vice president revealed her kill plot against Marcos, his wife and Romualdez.

Senator-Judge Risa Hontiveros then pressed the defense on the clip’s relevance, asking if the defense was arguing that Duterte’s alleged threats were warranted because her chief of staff had been oppressed.

The defense, through Atty. Carlo Joaquin Narvasa Jr. then confirmed that the defense’s position is that there had been systematic oppression by the House of Representatives when Duterte made her pronouncements.

Meanwhile, after being given a chance to respond to Hontiveros’ earlier question the day before, the defense, through Atty. Mark Vinluan, maintained that Duterte’s alleged hiring of an individual to assassinate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Lisa Marcos, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez was merely an “unconventional” but “justified” response to genuine threats against her and her family.

It was also on the third day when the impeachment court granted the House prosecution’s request to subpoena Lopez.

Day 4

On the fourth day of the impeachment trial, the prosecution presented its second witness, NBI Regional Director Jeremy Lotoc, who testified that Duterte’s alleged kill plot was “serious” and not protected by freedom of speech.

Lotoc, who previously headed the NBI Cybercrime Division that investigated the case, told the impeachment court that the bureau found sufficient basis to investigate Duterte’s statements, saying she herself admitted having spoken to a supposed assassin before her Nov. 23, 2024 online press conference.

He also testified that the NBI is mandated by law to investigate threats against the country’s high officials, effectively corroborating Calilung—the first witness’s—testimony before the court.

Another highlight was Senator-Judge Bam Aquino questioning the defense on its position that Duterte never hired a hitman, asking whether that meant her statements during the November 2024 briefing were untrue. Defense counsel Mark Vinluan, in response, then simply maintained that the vice president did not contract an assassin.

Meanwhile, the prosecution, in its position, also drew a parallel to the 2020 case of public school teacher Ronnel Mas, who was swiftly arrested for placing a bounty on former President Rodrigo Duterte, to argue that the VP’s threats should be treated similarly.

The defense, on the other hand, announced the same day its intent to present witnesses to prove the existence of the so-called “Operation Romanov,” an alleged plot targeting Duterte and her family.

Day 5

Lotoc’s testimony was then continued on the fifth day of the trial, with the NBI official this time telling the impeachment court that former President Rodrigo Duterte’s case before the International Criminal Court (ICC) was among the factors considered in assessing Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged capability to carry out her alleged kill plot.

According to Lotoc, investigators factored in the vice president’s relationship to the former president and his pending ICC case when evaluating whether she had the capability to execute the threats she allegedly made during a November 2024 online press briefing.

However, during the defense’s cross-examination led by Vinluan, Lotoc admitted that he had no personal knowledge that Duterte had contracted someone to kill the president or the other targets, but maintained that the evidence the NBI gathered linked her to such a plot.

The defense also continued to point out various typographical errors in the NBI documents presented as evidence, but Lotoc asserted that such errors did not alter the NBI’s findings that Duterte committed grave threats and inciting to sedition.

The term “Oplan Romanov,” was also once again touched upon during the trial’s fifth day, with Lotoc and even Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo—in a manifestation—saying that it was first actually first publicly used by Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte during a rally referring not to him and his families, but actually against the Marcos family.

Meanwhile, it was this day when the prosecution revealed its decision to withdraw its presentation of two witnesses, particularly, Zuleika Lopez and House Legislative Security Bureau official Capt. Belinda Bello.

Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan explained that they withdrew the two witnesses as their testimonies on Duterte’s alleged grave threats would be “unnecessary,” “redundant,” and a “surplusage” after the testimonies of Calilung and Lotoc.

Day 8

With the sixth and seventh day of the trial largely focused on matters unrelated to Article IV—as both days were focused on the oral arguments concerning the prosecution’s request to subpoena Duterte’s financial and tax records—the prosecution’s presentation on the subject article continued on the eighth day.

On the eighth day, NBI Director Melvin Matibag was called to the witness stand by the prosecution panel. But before his testimony began, Escudero admonished and warned Matibag from making statements pertaining to individual senator-judges to avoid affecting the court’s integrity.

In his testimony, Matibag told the court that the NBI aimed to establish a “pattern of violence” against Duterte.

Matibag also testified that the similarity between threats made by Duterte and those later made by her brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte, suggests possible collusion against the president’s life.

When Senator-judge Bam Aquino asked about the probability that Duterte had spoken to a hitman, Matibag replied that based on the vice president’s own statements, he was “100 percent” certain she had spoken to someone.

READ: Highlights: Day 8 of Sara Duterte impeachment trial | July 21, 2026

Another highlight was when the prosecution presented a video of Duterte, when she was Davao City mayor, punching a sheriff as supporting evidence of that pattern.

Furthermore, the prosecution also showed an “affidavit” of former self-proclaimed member of the Davao Death Squad and ex-police officer Arturo Lascañas that Vice President Sara Duterte was among the architects of the “Oplan Tokhang” in his father’s bloody campaign against drugs.

This, however, was objected to by both the defense and Senator-judge Pia Cayetano as the affidavit was not notarized.

Meanwhile, the court granted the defense’s motion for a continuance, giving the defense team more time to examine documents the prosecution presented during Matibag’s testimony.

As a result, the cross-examination of Matibag continued to a ninth day.

Final Day

On the ninth and final day of the trial days so far, Vinluan continued the defense’s cross examination of Matibag.

One highlight was Vinluan asking Matibag whether the NBI is conducting its ongoing investigation to substantiate the impeachment case against the vice president, and the latter responding that there would be no need to as “it has already been established.”

Vinluan also asked if it was possible the NBI misunderstood Duterte, particularly in one of her press conferences where she said she “imagined cutting the President’s head” as she may have only said this in jest—thereby taking her out of context.

But Matibag responded that it is hard for the law enforcement to ignore such pronouncements, likening it to “bomb jokes” made in public vehicles, particularly airplanes.

Matibag said this statement of Duterte is part of their investigation where they established a “pattern of violence.”

The prosecution then forwent their redirect examination, stating that they no longer find it necessary.

Since Matibag was the last witness for Article IV, presiding officer Escudero informed the court and both parties that the prosecution only consumed six days for their presentation.

“So we are still ahead by 2 days based on the timetable given in the pre-trial order. I hope we can be able to continue along these lines,” said Escudero.

After Article IV, the court is then expected to proceed tackling Article I, which involves the alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds from the Office of the Vice President, or P500 million, and the Department of Education, or DepEd, amounting to P112.5 million.

With the court now taking nine days, it has 83 days left to decide whether to convict Duterte.

World.title: Magnitude 5.0 quake strikes off Sarangani, Davao Occidental
World.content:
A magnitude 5.0 earthquake was recorded off Sarangani Island in Davao Occidental on July 22, 2026. (Image by Phivolcs/Facebook)

MANILA, Philippines – A magnitude 5.0 earthquake was recorded off Sarangani, Davao Occidental on Wednesday afternoon, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) said.

Phivolcs said that this is an aftershock of the magnitude 7.8 earthquake that struck Sarangani last June 8 and the magnitude 6.5 earthquake that struck off Davao Occidental last June 26.

READ: Angara leads inspection of disaster-hit Davao Occidental schools for rehab

Article continues after this 

In its earthquake bulletin, Phivolcs said that the epicenter of the earthquake was located some 11 kilometers (km) west off Sarangani Island in Sarangani town.

It was tectonic in origin and had a depth of 10 km.

Phivolcs noted that the following instrumental intensities were recorded:

Instrumental Intensity IV: Sarangani, Davao Occidental

Instrumental Intensity II: Malapatan, Sarangani; General Santos City

Instrumental Intensity I: Malungon, Maasim, Sarangani

It added that no aftershocks or damage to property are expected./gsg

World.title: Lacson confirms OVP request; Poa says Senate isn’t paying
World.content:
INQUIRER/SCREENGRAB PHOTOS

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson confirmed that the Office of the Vice President (OVP) sought Senate funding for catering during Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, but a defense lawyer said the request does not appear to have been granted.

“Well, I can confirm that no such arrangement is being allowed, as far as I know,” defense counsel and spokesperson Michael Poa said during a press briefing when asked about the request for the Senate to shoulder the costs.

Poa said he could not discuss the July 7 letter in detail because the defense team had no role in preparing it.

Article continues after this 

Asked about the meals being served to the defense panel, Poa said: “It’s okay, but I don’t know. I don’t think it’s being supplied by the Senate.”

Impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol, meanwhile, said he was not privy to the matter and that it was “outside my pay grade.”

Lacson confirmed the authenticity of the July 7 letter in a text message to reporters but said a subsequent communication appeared to have modified its contents.

“Although, I should say that apparently there is a follow-up letter modifying it, but not expressly requesting to disregard the letter that you showed me,” Lacson said.

Addressed to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, the letter asked the Senate to shoulder the “reasonable costs” of food, beverages and catering services for the defense team, support staff and witnesses.

Article continues after this 

“As these arrangements are required solely in connection with these proceedings, the OVP respectfully requests that the Senate shoulder the reasonable costs of food and beverage and catering services for the defense team, support staff, and witnesses,” the letter read.

The OVP also requested that all food and beverages for the defense team, support staff and witnesses be served only in their designated holding room and be sourced, prepared and served exclusively by the OVP’s accredited caterer, citing security concerns.

Article continues after this 

According to the letter, the arrangements were necessary to safeguard the safety and well-being of the defense team, support staff and witnesses and to ensure their full participation in the proceedings.

It remained unclear as of posting whether the Senate had formally acted on the requests.

READ: Sara Duterte camp wants to bring own equipment, caterer at Senate room

On July 10, Senate Secretary Renato Bantug said Duterte’s camp, through chief of staff Zuleika Lopez, had inquired about bringing its own equipment and hiring a caterer for its holding area during the impeachment trial. Bantug said the request was not unusual because the prosecution panel had also brought its own equipment and catering arrangements.

The OVP also told the Inquirer on July 10 that the requested equipment and catering services were intended for everyone and for coverage purposes.

World.title: PNP probes cops over ‘harassment’ of 2 photojournalists covering rally
World.content:
Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. — Photo from Office of the Chief PNP/Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) has started investigating an incident in which two photojournalists were reportedly harassed by police officers while they were covering a rally in Pasay City on Wednesday.

“We assure the public that the investigation will be guided by evidence, due process, and fairness,” PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said in a statement.

“Should it be established that any personnel acted contrary to existing laws, PNP policies, or prescribed operational procedures, appropriate administrative and other legal actions will be taken,” he added.

Article continues after this 

READ: PCP condemns ‘harassment’ of 2 photojournalists covering rally

The photojournalists, Bullit Marquez and Rene Dilan, were allegedly confronted by police officers and prevented from photographing the arrest of protesters at a rally outside the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City, according to the Photojournalists’ Center of the Philippines.

This came during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

“The PNP recognizes the important role of journalists and media practitioners in documenting events of public interest and respects their freedom to carry out their work,” Nartatez said.

“At the same time, our personnel remain duty-bound to ensure public safety, maintain peace and order, and implement the law,” he added. /jpv

World.title: NBI bared enough to prove threat case vs VP Duterte – prosecution
World.content:
National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag takes the witness stand during the continuation of the cross-examination on Day 9 at the Senate Impeachment Court in Pasay City, July 22, 2026. —Photo by Niño Jesus Orbeta | INQUIRER

MANILA, Philippines — Director Melvin Matibag of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and two of his agents have given enough evidence to prove the grave threat allegation against Vice President Sara Duterte, Rep. Rodge Gutierrez said in a media briefing on Wednesday.

“We do believe that the evidence has already established all the points that the prosecution needed to establish,” Gutierrez said, referring to the fourth impeachment article, which accuses Duterte of betraying public trust by threatening to have someone kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

The accusation stemmed from Duterte’s Nov. 23, 2024, online media conference, in which she said she had arranged for someone to kill the country’s top officials if she herself were killed.

Article continues after this 

READ: NBI chief: VP’s kill threat a nat’l security concern

Gutierrez explained that it was Matibag, the last witness for the fourth article, who “was able to piece together the evidence” earlier provided by Senior Agent John Mark Calilung and Regional Director Jeremy Lotoc.

Calilung authenticated the recording of Duterte’s “kill” remarks, and Lotoc testified that the NBI found probable cause to recommend the filing of criminal complaints for grave threats and inciting to sedition against the vice president.

“With the testimony of Director Matibag, we now have the institutional picture of how the NBI treated the statement. So I think now we have put in open court the legal implications, or how the NBI assessed the same,” Gutierrez said.

According to him, the prosecution’s confidence was reinforced during the cross-examination of its witnesses and by its decision to withdraw several witnesses after concluding that the essential facts had already been established.

Article continues after this 

Evidence put in proper context

For his part, Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V said Matibag’s testimony completed the prosecution’s presentation by placing the evidence in its proper context and showing that authorities continue to treat the alleged threat as active.

“The arrival of NBI Director Matibag provided a big piece of the puzzle, because he was able to complete the story,” Ortega said in Filipino.

Article continues after this 

“He painted the bigger picture and was able to show the evidence completely, and he was able to affirm the prosecution’s stand on the evidence — that it really happened and it’s still an active threat,” he added.

Ortega pointed out that Matibag also testified that the NBI investigation remained active, with its agents continuing to pursue leads and persons of interest involved in the alleged plot.

READ: NBI chief: Sara Duterte influenced individuals to threaten Marcos

Complete ‘chain of evidence’

Lawyer Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr., legal spokesperson and counsel for the House prosecutors, said Matibag’s testimony completed the NBI’s “chain of evidence” by explaining the bureau’s institutional assessment of Duterte’s statements.

According to Tolosa, the NBI did not rely solely on Duterte’s viral remarks but examined the totality of the circumstances before concluding that the alleged threats had become a national security concern.

“They were not relying on just one viral video or just one statement. They used a totality-of-the-circumstances approach in reaching the conclusion that these remarks had transcended into the level of a national security concern since they affect no less than the head of state, our commander-in-chief,” he said.

Tolosa also cited Matibag’s testimony that investigators were “100 percent sure” Duterte had spoken with someone regarding the alleged plot and are now working to identify that person.

“His answer was: 100 percent sure, there is [still a threat]. So again, they’re pursuing leads. This is now for the purpose of identifying that person. But there’s no question anymore if there was really a person she talked to,” he said.

It would still be up to the senator-judges to appreciate the evidence presented by the prosecution, he pointed out. But for him, the evidence was enough to answer the critical question of whether or not the vice president should remain in office.

World.title: Portion of SLEx TR4 to be operational by year-end — DOTr
World.content:
DOTr logo, INQUIRER FILES

MANILA, Philippines — A portion of the Toll Road 4 (TR4) of the South Luzon Expressway (SLEx) will be operational before 2026 ends, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) said on Wednesday.

According to the DOTr, the travel time from Sto. Tomas, Batangas to Tiaong, Quezon and vice versa will be reduced from two hours to just 30 minutes once the Package A to C becomes open to motorists by then.

“By the end of this year, we can start using the TR4, we can inaugurate it… Our target for the phase three operations of TR4 is by November, December,” Transport Secretary Giovanni Lopez said in an interview with ANC Headstart.

Article continues after this 

READ: DOTr receives unmodified opinion from COA for fiscal year 2025

Lopez then noted that the usual travel time of four hours for the whole TR4 will be lessened to one hour once the whole toll road opens.

“It’s a big ticket project in coordination and in partnership also with the DPWH [Department of Public Works and Highways]. So that’s what we expect to be operating in the road sector within a year,” Lopez added.

The agency shared that around 17,000 motorists will benefit from the SLEx TR4 daily.

The construction of the 66.74-kilometer SLEx TR4 began in March 2019. According to the DPWH, the toll road costs 58.42 billion (excluding Package F) as of December 2023.

The project is composed of six packages: 11.32-km Package A (Santo Tomas, Batangas to Makban, Laguna); 12.75-km Package B (Makban, Laguna to San Pablo, Laguna); 7.5-km Package C (San Pablo, Laguna to Tiaong, Quezon); 15-km Package D (Tiaong, Quezon to Candelaria, Quezon); 10.21-km Package E (Candelaria, Quezon to Tayabas, Quezon); and 9.96-km Package F (Tayabas, Quezon to Brgy. Mayao, Lucena, Quezon). /mr

World.title: WATCH: Lacson denies filing perjury case vs Lascañas

MANILA, Philippines – Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson denies filing a perjury case against self-confessed Davao Death Squad member and former police officer Arturo Lascañas during Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Wednesday.

World.title: Matibag: What if Robredo threatened Duterte? She would’ve been arrested
World.content:
NBI Director Melvin Matibag. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — If it were former Vice President Leni Robredo who threatened former President Rodrigo Duterte — the sitting chief executive during her time — she would have been arrested immediately like others who made threats, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag said.

At Wednesday’s impeachment trial of Duterte’s daughter, Vice President Sara Duterte, Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo tried to draw comparisons between the threats made by the Vice President against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and the threats received by former president Duterte.

READ: With or without contract to kill, VP made impeachable offense – lawmaker

Article continues after this 

Tulfo noted that several individuals who threatened former president Duterte, including public school teacher Ronnel Mas who placed a bounty on his head, were all arrested — prompting him to ask whether Robredo would have been arrested too.

“I’ll give you an example. For example, what happened now where our President was threatened, it also happened during the time of former president Duterte and Leni Robredo made threats — this is just an example, of course Leni Robredo would not do that because I know, it is not in her character,” Tulfo said in Filipino.

“[For example] Leni Robredo threatened former president Duterte, and her outbursts and threats were intense, and the same thing happened; her daughter made a follow-up threat. What would have happened, do you think it is possible that there will be an arrest ordered by PRRD like what happened to the teacher, construction worker, and unemployed college graduate?” he asked, also speaking Filipino.

In response, Matibag said that while it is a question that entails his opinion, he believes that Robredo would have been arrested also if the law is applied equally.

“Well respectfully it’s calling for an opinion, but maybe I have a basis for this, based on what you said that a construction worker, teacher, were arrested because they made threats, it is possible, there is a possibility that the Vice President during that time may be arrested immediately,” Matibag said in Filipino.

Article continues after this 

Prior to this question, Tulfo also asked Matibag why there was allegedly a difference in law enforcement agencies’ treatment of people who made threats, saying that Mas, a construction worker, and a college graduate who threatened the former president were immediately arrested, but Vice President Duterte who threatened Marcos and his relatives remains free.

“Like Ronnel Mas, a teacher, and these three ordinary citizens, we will compare that with what VP Sara and [Davao City] Mayor Baste [Duterte] did to our President, threats, almost the same thing happened- but an iron fist was used when law enforcement agencies dealt with ordinary citizens,” Tulfo said.

Article continues after this 

“Pero kapag makapangyarihang mga tao (But if it involves ordinary citizens), you treat them with kid’s gloves; why is that?” he asked.

Matibag said he cannot comment on the behavior of law enforcement agencies during the past administration, but he agrees with Tulfo that all individuals, regardless of status, must be treated fairly when they are involved in alleged felonies or criminal offenses.

The NBI chief also said that the reason why Vice President Duterte has not been arrested is that the case is still pending before the Department of Justice.

“Respectfully your Honor, first of all, I cannot speak to the behavior of the law enforcement during that time, but I agree with you that the arrest of the individuals were made without warrants, that’s the reason why the cases were dismissed,” Matibag said.

“With the case today, with what has happened, we go to the case build-up and file a case like what has happened to the Vice President, and if this will be filed before the court, that is the time that the court will issue a warrant of arrest. So we follow a process,” he added.

Matibag was presented by the prosecution as a witness for Article IV of the Articles of Impeachment, which concerns Vice President Duterte’s threats against Marcos, his wife, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and his cousin, former House of Representatives Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez.

Vice President Duterte’s threats came during an online press briefing on November 23, 2024. In that video, Duterte was asked by a vlogger to take care as she may be in danger.

The Vice President then responded by urging people not to worry about her as she has already talked to a person about killing the Marcos couple and Romualdez if she herself gets killed.

The defense panel has maintained even before the impeachment trial that Vice President Duterte’s statements were part of free speech. However, several government officials and prosecutors believe it was a grave threat — regardless of whether or not the Vice President executed a contract with an assassin to kill the three.

Regarding the threats against former president Rodrigo Duterte, this is not the first time in recent weeks that Mas’ name was mentioned. Just this July 13, members of the prosecution team believe the correct comparison to the grave threats allegations against the Vice President is Mas’ case, as he was swiftly arrested for placing a bounty on former president Duterte.

World.title: Ye’s Almaty Concert Sells Half of Available Tickets During Presales
World.content:
����������: 2297

ALMATY – Around half of all tickets for American rapper Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, sold out on the first day of presales for his Aug. 14 concert in Almaty, organizers announced on July 22.

The performance at Almaty’s Central Stadium is expected to become the largest music show ever staged in Central Asia and forms part of Ye’s world tour promoting his latest album Bully.

Presales, available exclusively through the Freedom SuperApp, attracted thousands of users within minutes of opening at noon. Organizers said the lowest-priced ticket categories sold out almost immediately, with ticket prices ranging from 120,000 tenge (US$222) to 350,000 tenge (US$648). To discourage ticket scalping, purchases during presales were limited to four tickets per customer.

Virtual queue introduced to manage demand

Organizers said the online waiting room used during the launch was not a technical failure but a standard queue management system widely used by major global ticketing platforms, including Ticketmaster, AXS, See Tickets and Eventim.

The system processes customers on a first-come, first-served basis while preventing platform overload during periods of exceptionally high demand. Buyers who completed their purchase received electronic vouchers, while tickets with unique QR codes will be emailed 24 hours before the concert on Aug. 13.

In response to strong public interest, organizers also launched Fan2Fan, an official resale platform operated through Ticketon.kz. The service allows ticket holders unable to attend the concert to resell their tickets securely. Once a ticket is resold, the seller’s voucher is automatically canceled, and a new voucher is issued to the buyer, who will receive the valid QR code before the event.

Organizers warned that tickets transferred outside the official platform cannot be guaranteed, as the final QR code will be sent only to the original purchaser.

Organizers describe the concert as the largest international music event ever staged in Central Asia and expect it to attract visitors from many countries, providing a boost to event tourism and reinforcing Almaty’s position as an emerging cultural destination in the region.

First Media Group is organizing the performance as part of its efforts to bring major international music productions to Kazakhstan. According to the organizers, the show will feature a full-scale stadium production combining music, visual art, stage design and advanced technology. The setlist is expected to include songs from Ye’s latest work alongside some of his best-known hits spanning more than two decades of his career.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s Dairy Output Rises as Cheese and Ice Cream Lead Growth
World.content:
����������: 755

ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s dairy manufacturing output rose 11.9% in the first half of 2026. The growth is concentrated in cheese, butter and ice cream while production of processed liquid milk remained nearly unchanged, according to the latest release from the Bureau of National Statistics.

The value of manufactured dairy products reached 414.9 billion tenge (US$887.4 million). Cheese and curd output reached 30,661 tons, up 26.2% year on year. Particularly noticeable growth is recorded in hard cheese output at 56.7%.

Butter and milk-spread production rose 27% to 24,376 tons, whereas ice cream output surged 64.7% to 55,199 tons in January-June. By contrast, production of processed liquid milk and cream remained almost unchanged, up just 0.4% to 331,342 tons. Yogurt and other fermented milk and cream products grew modestly at 3.2% to 134,168 tons.

Traditional fermented dairy products showed different dynamics. Kymyz (made from mare milk) production reached 774 tons, up 36.9%, while shubat (made from camel milk) production fell 42% to 509 tons.

The latest figures continue an expansion recorded in 2025, when cheese and curd production increased 18.3%, ice cream output rose 22% and processed liquid milk and cream grew 6.2%.

Last year, Kazakhstan produced dairy products worth 705.7 billion tenge (US$1.5 billion), up from 606.4 billion tenge (US$1.3 billion) a year earlier.

Dairy manufacturing remained geographically concentrated. The Almaty, North Kazakhstan and Kostanai regions together accounted for around 45.6% of Kazakhstan’s dairy manufacturing output by value in 2025.

Trade data show that rising domestic production has not eliminated Kazakhstan’s dependence on imported dairy goods. In the first five months of this year, Kazakhstan exported 859.7 tons of cheese and curd worth $3.2 million, mainly to Russia, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia. Smaller shipments also reached Azerbaijan and South Korea. Imports were far larger at 16,578.9 tons worth $81.7 million, primarily from Russia and Belarus.

Demand within Kazakhstan also increased. Domestic sales of cheese and curd reached 41,400 tons, up 11.2% from the same period a year earlier.

The figures may suggest that local producers are gaining ground around cheese production. However, imports still remain substantial, reflecting continued demand for foreign varieties and the scale advantage of producers in neighboring Russia and Belarus.

With ice cream, there is a different picture. In January-May, Kazakhstan exported $32.4 million worth of ice cream and other edible ice, exceeding imports of $19.4 million.

Kazakhstan became a net exporter of ice cream for the first time in 2025, as domestic production and exports reached record levels. The ice cream industry is highly concentrated, with Almaty Region producing roughly two-thirds of the national total. Cream-based ice cream and plombir dominate the product mix, accounting for more than 80% of output.

The government is also seeking foreign investment in higher-value dairy processing. On July 16, Agriculture Minister Aidarbek Saparov met executives from Greek company Desserta Hellas to discuss a potential project to localize cheese and dairy production in Kazakhstan, reported the ministry’s press service.

According to the ministry, Kazakhstan has 64 cheese producers and 182 dairy-processing enterprises with a combined annual capacity of around 2.7 million tons of milk. Saparov noted state support includes reimbursement of up to 25% of investment costs, interest-rate subsidies and working-capital financing at 5% annually.

World.title: Kazakhstan Steps Up Aral Restoration, Water Infrastructure and Conservation Reforms
World.content:
����������: 1305

ASTANA – Kazakhstan is accelerating restoration of the North Aral Sea while advancing large-scale water management reforms, including new reservoirs, irrigation modernization, water-saving technologies and industrial water reuse.

North Aral restoration

During a working visit to the Kyzylorda Region, Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation Nurzhan Nurzhigitov met with fishermen in the Aral district to discuss measures to preserve the North Aral Sea. He said the government, together with the World Bank, has prepared the second phase of the North Aral restoration project, which includes reconstructing the Kokaral Dam to raise the sea level and increase water storage, reported the ministry’s press service on July 17.

Since Oct. 1, 2025, Kazakhstan has directed 1.4 billion cubic meters of water into the North Aral Sea through the Syr Darya River. During the current irrigation season, water is being released into the sea at a rate of 40 cubic meters per second.

The sea’s volume has reached 23.5 billion cubic meters, while salinity has declined by 10% compared to last year to 7.9 per mille. Fishermen harvested 4,200 tons of fish during the first half of the year.

Local fishermen called for stricter enforcement of agricultural water-use limits and proposed constructing the Amanotkel hydraulic structure to increase water releases into the Syr Darya River. Nurzhigitov instructed the Water Management Committee to prepare project documentation.

Balkhash preservation

Nurzhigitov said Kazakhstan is continuing efforts to preserve Lake Balkhash. Over the past two years, around 30 billion cubic meters of water have been directed to the lake, helping stabilize its water level. A master plan for preserving the Balkhash ecosystem through 2040 is being developed with support from the French Development Agency (AFD).

Water sector modernization

The government’s water management strategy through 2030 includes construction of 42 new reservoirs, reconstruction of 37 existing reservoirs, modernization of 14,500 kilometers of irrigation canals, wider adoption of water-saving technologies, digitalization of water management, and improved flood and drought forecasting, reported Kazinform on July 20.

Agriculture accounts for around 60% of Kazakhstan’s total water withdrawals, making irrigation efficiency a key priority. By the end of 2025, water-saving technologies covered 543,500 hectares, conserving approximately 874 million cubic meters of irrigation water. The government aims to expand their use to 1.3 million hectares by 2030, saving around 2.2 billion cubic meters of water annually.

Industry, which accounts for 30% of national water consumption, is also undergoing reform. Under the new Water Code, enterprises will gradually transition to recycled and reused water systems over the next seven years, with the goal of increasing the share of reused water to 28% by 2030.

Developing human capital

The ministry has expanded water conservation education programs, reaching more than 3.3 million students this year. It has also launched nationwide campaigns to restore springs and water bodies and is carrying out digital registration of 2,772 natural springs.

Kazakhstan has expanded training for water specialists by increasing the number of universities and colleges offering water-related programs, while government-funded scholarships have risen to 1,000. Salaries at the state-owned Kazvodkhoz enterprise have more than doubled since 2024, reaching an average of 326,000 tenge.

World.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Astana Bus Brand, Begin Electric Bus Production in 2027

ASTANA – Kazakhstan will begin serial production of domestically branded buses under the Astana name in November, marking a major step in expanding the country’s automotive manufacturing, Astana Motors Chairman Nurlan Smagulov announced at a government meeting on July 21.

The project is one of the company’s flagship initiatives aimed at broadening Kazakhstan’s lineup of locally produced vehicles. The buses were developed with Chinese technology partners and incorporate components from leading global manufacturers, while Kazakh engineers contributed to their design. Production will take place in Kazakhstan.

Serial production of diesel and compressed natural gas (CNG) buses is scheduled to start in November, according to the Prime Minister’s press service.

Smagulov also announced that the company is developing a line of electric vehicles with Chinese automaker BYD using new-generation battery technology. Production of Astana-branded electric buses is expected to begin in March 2027.

ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Tourism and Sports has released the competition schedule for the international Phygital Games of the Future 2026, scheduled for July 29-Aug. 9, bringing together athletes and gamers in competitions that combine physical and digital disciplines.

The tournament will open with the 3on3 Freestyle phygital basketball event on July 29, followed by the PUBG competition from July 31 to Aug. 2. DOTA 2 (MOBA PC) matches are scheduled for Aug. 2-5, while the Counter-Strike phygital shooter tournament will run from Aug. 4-8. The UFL phygital football competition will take place on Aug. 4-9.

The Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MOBA Mobile) tournament is set for Aug. 6-9, alongside the Just Dance phygital dancing competition on Aug. 6-7. The tournament will conclude with the Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves phygital fighting event on Aug. 8.

The tournament is expected to welcome more than 800 participants representing over 50 nationalities, united in international clubs. It will also bring together technology brands and thousands of spectators for 12 days of competitions combining digital and physical sports.

World.title: Shanghai and Technology Turn in Kazakhstan-China Relations
World.content:
����������: 524

Kazakhstan’s largest Chinese business round in years put data, computing and digital logistics at the center. The measure of it will be deployment.

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s working visit to Shanghai on July 16-17 produced a familiar number and a new emphasis. Kazakhstan and China signed more than 70 commercial documents worth over $15 billion, covering artificial intelligence, transport, finance, agriculture and machinery. What set this round apart was where the weight fell. The center of gravity sat in data, computing and digital logistics, the fields that will define the next decade of the relationship, rather than in the oil, metals and transit flows that built it.

Tokayev opened the roundtable with the figures that anchor the partnership and a phrase to frame them. The two countries, he said, have entered a new “golden thirty years.” Bilateral trade reached $49 billion in 2025, a record, and Chinese firms have put more than $30 billion into the Kazakh economy, with over 8,500 enterprises carrying Chinese capital now active in the country. He named CNPC, CITIC and Huawei among the anchors, then pointed to a newer industrial layer: a gas chemical complex with Sinopec, a corn processing plant with Fufeng and a textile cluster with Lihua, alongside multi-brand vehicle assembly for Changan, Great Wall Motor and Chery. The value of Chinese participation, in his telling, sits increasingly in jobs, technology and industrial depth, with raw trade volume the older part of the story.

The pivot to data and computing

The signing list showed the shift in plain terms. Huawei took the largest share, concluding a strategic partnership with the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development and a separate equipment supply agreement with Samruk-Kazyna. Kazakhtelecom signed a framework with Hengtong Group on Data Center Valley, the gigawatt-scale computing complex rising near Ekibastuz. Almaty gained an artificial intelligence and robotics agreement involving UBTECH, and Kazakh universities tied up with Shanghai and Suzhou institutions. The timing was deliberate. The visit opened alongside the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, where Astana joined 29 governments in the Shanghai-based World AI Cooperation Organization.

Data Center Valley is where Kazakhstan’s positioning becomes legible. The same Ekibastuz site that now draws Chinese fibre and construction capital also anchors a $10 billion arrangement with Nvidia and a US-linked cloud partner, reported earlier this summer. Astana is not committing to one technology ecosystem. It is inviting both and pricing the same underlying assets into each: land, spare grid capacity and electricity near $0.025 per kilowatt-hour. Power that is scarce and expensive in the United States and Europe is abundant and cheap in northern Kazakhstan, and the government is monetizing that gap across the very rivalry that constrains hyperscale expansion elsewhere.

Mobility and ports rounded out the industrial side. Allur signed to build Li Auto vehicles in Kazakhstan, Astana Motors licensed Omoda and Jaecoo assembly with Chery, and Samruk-Kazyna, Freedom Holding and Astana’s city administration agreed a framework with Geely on electric-vehicle charging and automotive AI. On the Caspian, Guoyou committed to a multifunctional terminal at Kuryk, the port that feeds Kazakh cargo onto the Trans-Caspian route. In parallel talks, Tokayev discussed a first Central Asian battery plant with CATL. Each of these keeps more of the manufacturing chain inside the country.

Corridors, minerals and the deployment question

The logistics agenda followed the same logic. About 85% of China-Europe rail traffic already crosses Kazakhstan, and freight with China rose roughly 9% in the first half of 2026 to 18.7 million tons, while container trains dispatched from China through the country climbed more than a third year on year. In Shanghai, Tokayev sold the next layer, a digital one: Smart Cargo, a single window pooling customs, logistics and commercial data, built so that goods clear borders at something closer to the speed at which data moves. The framing matters because the Middle Corridor’s physical ceiling is fixed. Two changes of rail gauge and a Caspian crossing keep it structurally more expensive than the all-water route to Europe. Additional value has to come from speed, transparency and digital integration, since the geography will not yield maritime-scale tonnage.

Critical minerals formed the other pillar. Tokayev restated the demand Kazakhstan now makes of every partner it courts, which is processing and manufacturing capacity on Kazakh soil, with extraction rights as the opening term rather than the prize. That message runs alongside Astana’s parallel engagement with Washington and Brussels on rare earth separation and refining. It is also the message the Shanghai deals encode. The stated goal across them is technology transfer, research centres and production chains, with capital treated as the entry ticket.

The authors are Alexander Dergay, a column writer for Berliner Zeitung and the Ostdeutsche Allgemeine, and Eldaniz Gusseinov, a co-founder and head of research at Nightingale Int.

World.title: Kazakhstan, Austria Deepen Strategic Ties with New Connectivity Platform
World.content:
����������: 294

ASTANA – Kazakhstan and Austria officially launched the Austrian-Kazakh Connectivity Platform at the Austrian Parliament on July 15 to strengthen bilateral cooperation in transport, logistics, infrastructure, energy and investment, reported the Austrian Press Agency.

The platform aims to bring together government agencies, businesses and financial institutions from both countries to develop joint projects and improve transport connectivity between Europe and Central Asia.

The launch reflects the growing economic and political partnership between Kazakhstan and Austria, which have expanded cooperation in recent years through closer political dialogue and increasing trade and investment ties.

“Austria is home to highly competitive companies, advanced industrial expertise and a strong culture of innovation. Kazakhstan, in turn, offers considerable economic potential and is emerging as one of Central Asia’s key economic partners. Our role is to bring companies together and help turn business opportunities into lasting partnerships. The strong response to our inaugural event shows there is clear demand for a platform that can do exactly that,” said Karl Jurka, president of the Austrian-Kazakh Connectivity Platform.

President of the Austrian National Council Walter Rosenkranz welcomed the initiative, describing it as an effective mechanism for advancing cooperation in transport, logistics, sustainable infrastructure, digitalization and energy. He also highlighted the potential for further expanding bilateral relations.

The Kazakh Ambassador to Austria Mukhtar Tileuberdi said strengthening transport connectivity remains one of Kazakhstan’s strategic priorities. He presented the country’s efforts to further develop the Middle Corridor, a key trade route linking Europe and Asia.

Tileuberdi also briefed participants on Kazakhstan’s domestic reforms, noting that the country’s new Constitution entered into force on July 1 following its approval in a nationwide referendum. According to him, the updated Constitution expands Parliament’s powers, strengthens protections for citizens’ rights and freedoms, increases government accountability and further improves the investment climate.

He said the reforms initiated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev are aimed at building a Just Kazakhstan based on the rule of law, openness and sustainable development.

Alexander Schierhuber, Kazakhstan’s honorary consul in Lower Austria and vice president of the Austrian-Kazakh Connectivity Platform, noted that the initiative is intended to serve as a bridge between the two economies by providing businesses with a trusted platform for networking, dialogue and long-term cooperation.

“At a time of geopolitical change and evolving trade routes, reliable frameworks that allow companies to engage directly with one another are becoming increasingly important,” he said.

The launch marks a new step in Kazakh-Austrian relations, reinforcing both countries’ commitment to expanding strategic cooperation and promoting sustainable transport links between Europe and Central Asia.

World.title: Kazakhstan to Produce Li Auto, Omoda, Jaecoo Vehicles, Autonomous Trucks by 2028
World.content:
����������: 82

ASTANA – Kazakhstan plans to launch production of Li Auto, Omoda, and Jaecoo vehicles by 2028 as part of a broader effort to expand its automotive industry, strengthen domestic manufacturing, and introduce advanced technologies, Minister of Industry and Construction Yersayin Nagaspayev said at a July 21 government meeting.

The initiative follows agreements reached during President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s recent state visit to China. In addition to passenger vehicle production, Kazakhstan will manufacture autonomous SITRAK semi-trailer tractors and cooperate with BYD to develop a nationwide network of high-speed charging stations for electric vehicles.

The country is also expanding commercial vehicle manufacturing. Hyundai Trans Auto is scheduled to begin producing 500 Volvo semi-trailer tractors annually starting in the fourth quarter of this year, while Barys Truck Manufactory, in partnership with China’s XCMG, will launch production of electric heavy-duty trucks, reported Kazinform.

Nagaspayev said automotive manufacturers are integrating artificial intelligence and digital technologies in line with the President’s instructions. An AI-powered situational center has already been commissioned to improve operational safety by analyzing data from surveillance cameras, sensors, and other information systems to detect risks and emergencies in real time.

Kazakhstan currently has 11 enterprises producing passenger cars, buses, trucks, and specialized vehicles. Last year, the country commissioned the KIA Qazaqstan and Astana Motors Manufacturing Kazakhstan plants, with combined investment exceeding 346 billion tenge (US$735 million).

World.title: Georgia jails opposition TV host for 14 days over Facebook posts
World.content:
Arrests over social media posts in Georgia

On 22 July 2026, the Tbilisi City Court sentenced journalist and Formula TV host Vakho Sanaia to 14 days of administrative detention over posts he published on Facebook. The ruling was handed down by Judge Zviad Tsekvava.

The case against Sanaia was launched over Facebook posts about Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili and MP Vladimer Bozhadze. Bozhadze has represented the European Socialists party since 2025, although he entered parliament on the ruling Georgian Dream party list following the 2024 parliamentary elections.

The Hate Speech Department, established within the Ministry of Internal Affairs, referred the case to Tbilisi City Court for legal review.

Following an investigation by the department, Sanaia was fined 6,000 lari on 10 July.

In the post that led to the fine, Sanaia wrote: “I hope no one called [Vladimer Bozhadze] d**k, because the law prohibits calling Lado d**k. I would also like to urge everyone not to call Lado a d**k.”

After being fined, Sanaia published another post of a similar nature on social media: “I wrote a post saying, ‘Don’t call Papuashvili and Bozhadze d**k,’ and I was fined 6,000 lari. Am I missing something? Give them a call.”

On 18 July, Sanaia said the court had contacted him over the post and informed him that a hearing had been scheduled in his case.

Sanaia did not attend the court hearing.

“I’m laughing,” he wrote on social media after news emerged that he had been sentenced to administrative detention.

Brief overview of the department

Administrative cases over opinions expressed in the public sphere are initiated on the basis of reports compiled by the Hate Speech Department, which was established within the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

The new department has been operating since 1 June.

Its mandate is to monitor and identify public statements that violate human dignity, contain insults or elements of hate speech, where they may constitute an administrative offence.

According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, between the department’s launch and 2 July, it identified 170 alleged offences, 150 of which were referred to court.

Of those 150 cases, rulings had been issued in 33 by that date. Thirty-one people were fined, while two received verbal warnings. Most of those fined were activists. Vakho Sanaia became the first journalist to be fined on the basis of a report compiled by the department.

World.title: Russia destroyed 40,000 Armenian roses shipped via Belarus
World.content:
Russia destroys Armenian roses

Officials from Russia‘s agricultural watchdog Rosselkhoznadzor in Smolensk Region discovered a shipment of freshly cut roses from Armenia that was being transported via Belarus.

According to the Belarusian outlet Euroradio, the shipment was deemed illegal because Russia has banned the import of nearly all Armenian goods since the spring.

Armenian roses imported via Belarus / 32.fsvps.gov.ru

Moscow says the import ban was imposed in response to what it described as violations of phytosanitary requirements. However, the restrictions were introduced after Armenia declared EU integration as a foreign policy goal, leading officials in Yerevan and the EU to view the move as politically motivated.

Russia has previously imposed similar trade restrictions on Georgia and Moldova to exert economic pressure amid political disagreements.

According to the accompanying documents, the lorry travelling from Belarus’s Minsk Region to Moscow was carrying non-alcoholic carbonated energy drinks. However, an inspection found 39,200 roses instead.

The flowers were being transported without the required phytosanitary certificates or shipping documents.

Rosselkhoznadzor said some of the boxes still bore labels identifying Armenia as the country of origin.

The roses were destroyed, while the carrier was held administratively liable.

Russia suspends flower imports from Iran over suspected re-exports from Armenia

Shortly after the reports emerged that Armenian roses transported via Belarus had been destroyed, Russia’s agricultural watchdog Rosselkhoznadzor suspended the certification of flowers for export to Russia from Iran, also over suspicions that they had been re-exported from Armenia.

The agency said flower shipments from Iran in 2026 had significantly exceeded the volume recorded during the same period last year.

Rosselkhoznadzor also said that although Iran was listed as the exporting country, the appearance of the flowers and their packaging were identical to products previously supplied from Armenia.

Background

Since early spring 2026, Russia has gradually introduced restrictions on Armenian products.

Initially, the measures targeted Jermuk mineral water, followed by a range of alcoholic beverages.

On 30 May, Russia banned imports from Armenia of tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, herbs and strawberries.

This was followed by a temporary ban imposed by the Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance (Rosselkhoznadzor) on the import of flowers and ornamental plants from Armenia.

Rosselkhoznadzor has also reported problems with imports of certain livestock products, as well as fish and fish products.

Armenia also received a letter from Russia warning of the possible termination of an agreement on supplies of natural gas, petroleum products and rough diamonds.

The restrictions imposed by Russia are significant for Armenia, as the Russian market has been the main destination for Armenian agricultural exports for decades.

The Armenian authorities are currently working, with active support from the European Union, to rapidly open alternative export markets for Armenian products.

World.title: Armenia begins recruiting and training border guards for Azerbaijan border
World.content:
Armenia launches border guard recruitment

The Armenian government plans to gradually transfer responsibility for guarding the entire Armenia-Azerbaijan border from the Defense Ministry to the Border Guard Troops of the National Security Service (NSS).

To make that possible, the agency needs additional personnel. The government therefore plans to expand the NSS by introducing the “I Have the Honor“ programme, which the Defense Ministry already runs successfully.

Under the programme, university students sign a contract to undergo military training while completing their studies. After graduation, they perform their military service at the location and under the conditions specified in the contract.

Under the new proposal, participants will first serve as conscripts in the rank of private in Defense Ministry units. They will then transfer to the NSS as commissioned officers.

“The new mechanism will help strengthen the National Security Service, particularly the Border Guard Troops, by recruiting personnel with higher education,” the explanatory note to the draft says.

Under an intergovernmental agreement signed in 1992, the Russian Federal Security Service’s Border Guard Service has been responsible for guarding Armenia’s borders with Turkey and Iran. In recent years, however, Armenia has steadily moved to place the protection of its borders entirely under its own control. In 2024, Russian border guards withdrew from Zvartnots International Airport and from border areas along the frontier with Azerbaijan. On January 1, 2025, Russian border guards also left the border crossing on the Armenia-Iran frontier. Then, on March 1, Armenia’s National Security Service assumed sole responsibility for guarding the Margara border crossing with Turkey. Since the beginning of 2026, only Armenian border guards have been serving at the Akhurik border crossing on the Armenia-Turkey border.

Deferring military service during university in exchange for serving as an officer

The “I Have the Honor” programme allows students to defer compulsory military service while at university. In return, they commit to serving later as commissioned officers.

“Students attend university free of charge, with the state covering tuition fees in full at the rate set by the university for the relevant programme.”

After graduating from university and completing the required military training, participants receive the rank of lieutenant and begin contract service.

Officers receive their assignments through a lottery system.

Those trained as platoon commanders serve for two years and three months.

Those trained for military medical service serve for four years after graduation, followed by one year of clinical residency.

What other changes does the draft propose?

The legislative package also includes amendments to several laws governing military service, the National Security Service’s Border Guard Troops, and the country’s national security agencies.

In particular, the draft would clearly define the circumstances in which NSS officers may use firearms, special equipment and physical force.

Before using force, officers would have to issue a warning and allow enough time for a person to comply with a lawful order, unless any delay posed an immediate danger. The draft also requires officers to use force proportionately to the level of resistance or threat. They would also have to provide first aid to anyone injured.

If parliament passes the legislative package, border guards will also be able to use video and audio recording devices while carrying out their duties.

The draft would also raise the retirement age for senior NSS officers from 52 to 55.

Armenia launches border guard recruitment

World.title: Georgia’s Asian pivot: What does Tbilisi seek in Central Asia?
World.content:
Georgia’s Asian pivot

A section of Georgia’s Baku–Tbilisi–Kars highway. Photo: Reuters

Since the start of summer 2026, Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze has met the leaders of all five Central Asian states.

Tbilisi has signed strategic partnership agreements with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The Georgian prime minister has also made his first official visits to Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. In July, Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov paid his first official visit to Tbilisi.

The Georgian government says the renewed engagement is aimed at strengthening the country’s role as a regional transit hub. For the Central Asian states, new trade routes are becoming increasingly important alongside those through Russia and China.

Georgia is offering them access from the Caspian Sea to the Black Sea and onwards to Europe.

The growing ties with Central Asia come against the backdrop of an almost complete freeze in relations between Tbilisi and the West. The European Union has significantly scaled back political contacts with the Georgian government and suspended part of its direct assistance.

According to official EU statements, the measures are a response to what Brussels describes as democratic backsliding in Georgia.

Georgia’s EU accession process has effectively been put on hold until the government changes its political course. The EU’s 2026 report states that no political dialogue took place between the EU and Georgia during the reporting period.

Against this backdrop, the Georgian government describes its foreign policy as multi-vector.

Central Asia has become one of the main pillars of that policy. The key question, however, is what lies behind this shift: an effort to expand Georgia’s economic opportunities, or a political response to deteriorating relations with the West?

Economic data present a mixed picture. Exports to Central Asia have increased, but most of the growth is not driven by goods produced in Georgia. Re-exported vehicles account for the bulk of exports to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan.

Moreover, Central Asia’s interest in Georgia is largely based on access to Western markets. If Tbilisi moves away from the European political and economic space, its value as a transit hub could also diminish.
